# Open questions

Everything in the engine that cannot currently be explained. **Target: this file is empty.**

Every open checkbox in every system document must be mirrored here with an id, and every entry here must name the
document that owns it (FINAL-AUDIT-PROTOCOL pass 29 fails on any orphaned open question). When a question closes,
record the closure on both and in the owning document's section 8. *(Restated 2026-09-14, FABLE, after
OPUS-NOTE-FABLE-ORPHAN-QUESTIONS-MEASURED: on that date 588 of 703 open page checkboxes carried no id. They are
listed, generated, in [UNIDENTIFIED-OPEN-QUESTIONS.md](UNIDENTIFIED-OPEN-QUESTIONS.md) (`gen_unidentified_questions.py`),
which is the worklist and must reach zero: each item gets an id and a row in the same commit, or is closed with its
evidence. It is not a substitute for rows. An earlier draft of this header called the register an index of identified
questions only; that contradicted pass 29 and was withdrawn before it was applied.)*

Status legend: `OPEN` · `IN PROGRESS` · `BLOCKED` (says what unblocks it)

**Which id a checkbox belongs to** *(FABLE ruling 2026-09-14, `OPUS-REQ-FABLE-QUESTION-REGISTER-THREE`)*. A page box names
an id as its own only in the **label form**: the id bolded with its period inside the bold, as in `**BQ-3.**`.
- A box with more than one label-form id is one question under aliases, for example `**UQ-91.**` with `**FS-1.**`.
- If a box has no label-form id, its own id is the **first** bolded id in it.
- Any other bolded id is a **cross-reference**, however it is phrased: `**AO-5**,` after *supersedes*, `**BG-6**.` after
  *tracked separately as*, `**G-17**.` after *related to*. A cross-reference neither opens nor closes that id's row.
- Measured on the twenty boxes that bold two or more ids, this attributes every box to the question it asks.
  The four boxes read as two-question boxes (`K-6`/`K-11`, `G-17`/`G-24`, `BL-8`/`Q-1`, `AQ-2`/`B-3`) turn out to be one
  question plus a pointer.
- **Box readers should implement this rule rather than attribute a box to every id it mentions.**

**Duplicates, defect reports and double questions** *(FABLE ruling 2026-09-14, `OPUS-REQ-FABLE-REGISTER-FOUR-STRUCTURAL-DEFECTS`)*.
- **Duplicates merge under the id a page box carries as its label.** The page's box is the question's home, and
  the register mirrors it. If both ids label boxes, the older id survives. The other row becomes
  `SUPERSEDED — duplicate of <id>` and keeps its text.
  - *Extended 2026-09-16 (FABLE), because the rule as written did not cover the case that actually
    occurred.* **When both label-form ids are on the SAME box**, neither clause decides: they are not
    two boxes, so "the id a page box carries as its label" names both, and "if both ids label boxes"
    anticipates two. **The older id survives, and the newer becomes the alias.** The reason is
    provenance rather than taste: every instance of this was made by the 2026-09-14 generation pass
    that gave each open box an id and a row. A machine-assigned alias should not displace the identity
    a question was asked under.
    *(**Cause corrected 2026-09-16**, and the correction is to my own sentence. This clause first read
    that the pass "did not check whether the box already carried a label-form id". **It did check, and
    was lied to.** `9a275aaa` found the real fault: `read_boxes` ended a checkbox block at the first
    line not starting with **six** spaces, while markdown continuation is conventionally **two**, so an
    id written on a two-space continuation was invisible to every reader built on it. `UQ-91`'s box
    already said `**FS-1.**` — on its second line, indented two. The box read as id-less, was listed
    as unidentified, and was minted a fresh id. **The generator did exactly what it was told.** The
    ruling is unchanged and if anything stronger: an alias minted by a machine acting on a reader that
    could not see the existing id has even less claim to displace it. I had also said the instrument
    behind the nine was `gen_unidentified_questions.py`; that script only LISTS id-less boxes — the
    minting is `register_idless_boxes.py` — and I had flagged at the time that I had not confirmed
    which script assigns the ids. The flag was right and the guess in the same sentence was still
    wrong, which is the argument for not making the guess at all.)* **Measured: nine boxes, each with an `F*` id from 2026-09-10/11 and a `UQ-` id from
    2026-09-14, both rows live** (`Tools/work/FABLE/drift5/alias_boxes.py`; 11 alias boxes in 1,384
    checkbox blocks, of which 2 already have both rows closed). The nine `UQ-` rows are superseded
    below and keep their text; **the boxes are left alone**, so the `UQ-` label remains as a pointer
    into the merged row rather than nine page edits.
- **A defect report is not a question.** It names a fault and its fix. Such a row closes one of three ways:
  - `ANSWERED`, when the fix has landed and been measured;
  - `WITHDRAWN — NOT A QUESTION`, naming the board task that now carries the work;
  - never by staying open, since an open defect report keeps the register from emptying while any defect exists.
- **A row that asks two questions is split.** The row keeps one question; the other gets a new id and a row,
  added in the same commit that edits its box.

### The bare `**ANSWERED**` rows, measured 2026-09-13 (OPUS) — do not try to script this

`progress.py` counts a verdict cell that is **exactly** `**ANSWERED**`, with no text after it, as
**neither** closed nor open — deliberately, because the state was inferred from prose by the merge
rather than recorded with an answer. There are **291** by `progress.py`'s own parse (**294** by a looser scan that also accepts pipe rows outside its recognised sections — the three-row difference is the parse, not the data), and they are the difference between
`questions_closed` as reported and as it would read if they were trusted.

**They look like a scripted recovery and they are not.** Measured before attempting one, over all
522 documents *(counts written as a list, not a table, because every pipe row in this file is parsed
as a register row — a table here would inflate the denominator, as one did on first writing)*:

- bare rows with a well-formed id — **294** by the looser scan used here; `progress.py` reports **291**
- of those, a *ticked* checklist item elsewhere whose **own label** is that id, carrying ≥40
  characters of answer text — **22**
- ticked item found but no answer text — **59**
- **no ticked, labelled item anywhere — 211**
- ambiguous, two different answers — **2**

A looser rule — any checklist item merely *mentioning* the id — reports **136**, which is where a
script would have stopped. Hand-reviewing the 22 that survived the strict rule found **about five
unsafe**: `K-12` and `K-13` are two different questions that one checklist item labels, so both were
offered the **same** answer; `AY-10` and `F-3` already carry their answer inside the *question* cell;
and `C-11`'s candidate answers a different question than the row asks. **A bulk edit would have been
about 23 % wrong**, and the loose rule far worse.

> **So the 294 is not a merge artifact waiting for a script.** For **211 of them the answer is simply
> not written beside a labelled checklist item**, and recovering those means reading the owning
> document — one row at a time, by someone who can tell whether the answer actually answers the
> question. Recorded here so the next attempt starts from the measurement rather than the hope.

**No row was filled, struck or reworded by that measurement.**

*Applied 2026-09-14 (FABLE, `edb30679`, under OPUS-RULING-REGISTER-LOCK-NOT-BLOCKING).* The bare rows were not
filled by the checklist-matching rule measured above. **165** got a verdict read from the owning page, one row at a
time (OPUS-REQ-FABLE-REGISTER-PROSE-ANSWERS, `regprose/verdicts.tsv`). **134** more carried a dated closure in
their own row, and every page box naming their own id was already ticked; each got a verdict from that row
(`regprose/verdicts2.tsv` and `verdicts2_manual.tsv`). A row that was no longer bare when the batch ran was skipped,
never overwritten. **Two bare rows remain, `J-A` and `M-A`.** After the batch, `progress.py` reads
`questions_closed` 57.96 % (1,503 / 2,593).

**First, the engine's OWN format table settles what `00466220` selects.** The 43-byte table at `003A1EF0`, indexed `psm - 2`, sorts every code into four geometry classes. Its contents, read from the file at offset `0x2814F0`: **exactly three entries hold class `2`** — `0x14`, `0x24`, `0x2C`, the **PSMT4 / PSMT4HL / PSMT4HH** family; **two hold class `1`** — `0x13`, `0x1B`, the 8-bit **PSMT8 / PSMT8H**; **two hold class `0`** — `0x02`, `0x0A`, **PSMCT16 / PSMCT16S**; the remaining thirty-six hold the default `3`.
**So `0x1C` is not a format by the engine's own reckoning** — it holds the same default `3` as every unassigned code. `00466220`'s body is `tmp = psm - 0x14; if (tmp & 0xE7) return 0; return psm != 0x1C;`: the cheap mask leaves only bits 3 and 4 free and so admits **four** codes, and the explicit `cmp dl, 0x1C` exists for no purpose but to reject the one non-format the mask lets through. **Two independent expressions of the same three-code set in one binary** — the table's class `2` and this mask — which is as firm as *what it selects* can be made.
**Second, the factor is never scaled, and its consumer is unique.** `r15d` → `[rsp+0x70]` (`002F746C`) → `ebx` → `ecx` (`002F7487`) → `00467B00`, which stores it verbatim at `02CA6008`; `00467AA0` subtracts it verbatim at `00467AB7`. **No shift, multiply or divide anywhere on that path.** A whole-image RIP census over `02CA5FF0`–`02CA600C` (stride 4; positive control `022D8EB4` returning 26 references, so absence is meaningful) finds **`02CA6008` has exactly two references in 34,270 function bodies** — that writer and that subtraction — and `02CA6004` likewise. **No second reader exists anywhere in the image to disambiguate the unit.** That is the complete static evidence, not a sample of it.
**Third, a separate block-denominated accounting sits in the adjacent globals — and it is WRITE-ONLY.** The same census turns up a five-global chain the budget page had only one member of: `02CA5FF0` = `0x4000` = the 4 MiB arena **in 256-byte blocks** and `02CA5FF4` = `ceil(3wh/64)` = the same reservation in blocks, both written by `00467AD0` (sole caller `0036F4D0`); **`00467A70` (27 B) seeds `02CA5FF8` from that reservation and zeroes `02CA5FFC` / `02CA6000`**; `00467A90` (7 B) loads `02CA5FF8`. Then the census closes it:
 **`02CA5FF0`, `02CA5FFC` and `02CA6000` have exactly one reference each — their write. Nothing in the image ever reads them.** `02CA5FF8` has two — that write and `00467A90` — and **`00467A90`'s single caller discards the result**: `002F45DE` calls it and `002F45E3 mov edx, ebx` runs next, with `eax` overwritten at `002F45F0` before any use. No instruction anywhere takes the **address** of the region either, so no pointer to it can be formed.
So the block accounting is computed every frame and **consumed by nothing**, while `00467AA0` **recomputes** `0x100000` and `3wh` inline in words rather than reading either block global. **The two unit systems never mix, and only the word one is live.**
**BANDWIDTH — argued against.** `00467AA0` subtracts three terms from one total: the three 512×448 surfaces, the largest single mip-chain footprint, and this sum. The first two are storage footprints in words. A transfer rate summed with two storage figures is dimensionally incoherent, so the third term is a storage term.
**CLUT *count* — argued against.** A texture has one palette whatever its depth. `4` would have to mean four palettes for a non-4-bit texture, and neither the 723 bytes nor `00466190`'s record (`+0x00` PSM, `+0x05` mip count capped at 7, `+0x06` w, `+0x08` h) supplies a second one.
**BLOCK COUNT of the texture — argued against.** That is already what `00466190` computes and `00467B10` publishes at `02CA6004`. This sum is the *other* subtrahend, not a second copy of the footprint.
**PALETTE SIZE — matches the numbers exactly and STILL fails, on the shape of the code.** In GS blocks a 4-bit CLUT is 16 entries × 4 B = 64 B, under the 256-byte block granularity, so **1 block**; an 8-bit CLUT is 256 × 4 B = 1,024 B = **4 blocks**. Nothing else proposed yields 1 and 4. But a palette charge would have to separate **8-bit** from **non-indexed**, and *the engine already has that distinction*: class `1` versus classes `0` and `3` in the very table at `003A1EF0`. **`00466220` deliberately does not use it** — it collapses PSMT8, PSMT8H, PSMCT32, PSMCT24, PSMCT16, PSMCT16S and every `PSMZ*` depth format into one bucket and charges them all 4. A palette reading owes an explanation for charging a 256-entry palette to formats that have none, with the correct classifier sitting in the same binary and unused.
 **The defence, stated so it is not smuggled in:** the author may have chosen two arithmetic instructions over a table lookup for speed and accepted the over-charge on palette-free formats as conservative. That is plausible and **it is not evidenced** — no comment, no second site, no asymmetry in the body supports it. **A second defence, stated the same way:** the abandoned block accounting above supplies a *mechanism* by which a block-denominated figure could have survived into a word total — a block design that was dropped, leaving one term behind. That is a mechanism, **not evidence that this is that term**, and I am not treating it as one. So palette size is **weakened, not refuted**, and it is not promoted to the answer.
 The block arithmetic above is GS *hardware* arithmetic, not a reading of this executable — which is both why the match is suggestive and why it cannot close the row.
**PARTIAL, and the discriminator is named.** With one reader, no scaling and no second consumer, **the executable has been read out on this question.** What remains would settle it: whether the shipped texture record banks ever hold a **non-indexed** record. If they never do, the over-charge objection evaporates and palette size stands; if they do, it falls. Those banks are heap-populated (`[[rdi+0x150]+8]`) and not in the file, so this needs the shipped data or a live read. **Box on [texture-mip-local-memory-budget.md](../17-Presentation-Rendering/Legacy-PS2-GS/texture-mip-local-memory-budget.md) stays unticked; not dispositioned `NO ADMISSIBLE SOURCE`** — that needs a reviewer who is not the author (`EVIDENCE-STANDARD` 15bk requirement 4), and the author here is me. |

| G-1 | What the four selection implementations at **vtable slot 43** do. **`SwitchSound` CLOSED 2026-09-02** — proven: plays entry E iff `E.rangeMin <= parameter < E.rangeMax`. Remaining: `Random` `007E5160`, `Order` `007E58D0`, `Cycle` `007E6360` — shape read, discriminating predicates `FUN_007cf9c0` / `FUN_007cf830` unread. **ANSWERED 2026-09-17 (FABLE): the three rules, read whole (§12).** A *set* is a run of consecutive candidates sharing the group byte `007CF9A0` returns (sequence record `+0x11` at version 3 and above); its first entry's weight (`007CF9C0`, `+0x10`) decides for the set. **Random** (`007E5160`): every set whose weight is 0 plays; then one roll `rand() % 101` walks the weighted sets by cumulative weight and takes the first that reaches it; if that index equals the last pick (record `+1`) and record `+0x19` bit 5 is clear, the first other weighted set is substituted, then any later one whose weight exceeds the picked set's; no substitute means nothing plays and `+1` becomes `0xFF`; otherwise `+1` remembers the index. **Order** (`007E58D0`): every set whose weight is not 0 plays; the zero-weight sets are counted, and the one at cursor `+1` (0 when the cursor is at or past the count) plays, with `+1 = (cursor + 1) mod count` (`007E5BB9`..`007E5BD2`). **Cycle** (`007E6360` with `007E5E80`): Random's two passes, but the substitution also refuses any set whose group byte is still sounding among the object's active players (`007E5DA0` collects them from `+0x400`, count `+0x4C`), and slot 42's timer re-runs it. The class is chosen by the factory `007B2F70` from the sound record's byte `+4`: 0 or 1 the base `Sound`, 2 Random, 3 Order, 4 Cycle, 5 Switch. Static, bodies read; the shipped consequence, with every sequence record zero from `+0x10`, is in §12. | ANSWERED |

The GFZ says so on those functions — *"owns no independent Audio state or behavior; no owner credit… prevents Audio category contamination"*, *"do not count toward Audio owner denominator"*. Seven bodies read from the set confirm it: `00584730` is `if (p) _aligned_free(p)` with **2,306 non-Audio callers**, `00203080` a four-float subtract, `00202C70` a 64-byte copy, `002E9B80` an actor-handle accessor, `003601B0` a bitmask set, `0036DD80` a 16-byte constant copy, `007B8C80` an empty `return`. **The right question is the inverse** — which *Audio-owned* functions have non-Audio callers — and that answer is **174 of 2,064**, headed by `00249C60` (99 external callers, 0 internal), the game's most-called audio entry point. Documented in [`../18-Audio/Audio-Boundary/what-the-engine-calls-to-make-a-sound.md`](../18-Audio/Audio-Boundary/what-the-engine-calls-to-make-a-sound.md), which reads the **first Audio function bodies in this database**. ## I. Script VM

From [`../01-Script-VM-Native-Bridge/scriptvm-native-dispatch-table.md`](../01-Script-VM-Native-Bridge/scriptvm-native-dispatch-table.md).

| ID | Question | Status |
|---|---|---|
| I-6 | ~~Where the dispatch index mapping breaks.~~ | **CLOSED 2026-09-07 — there is no discontinuity, and this is now exhaustive rather than sampled.** `record N = verb N` holds across all **1,496** family-0 records. **645 independent anchors** — verbs the ff12-script catalog knows, each with an argument count, against the VM operand count measured from the handler body, two numbers neither derived from the other — agree at **89.1 %**, spanning `0x0000`-`0x05D7` at a mean spacing of **2.32 records**. **The counterfactual is what makes it a proof:** shift the table one record and the same comparison gives **55.7 %**. **Re-run 2026-09-07 with a second, oppositely-biased metric** (`net = pops − pushes`): **612 anchors, 97.2 % against a 59.0 % shifted baseline.** Two instruments that are wrong in opposite directions both place the identity mapping 33-38 points above its own shifted baseline. Agreement per 128-record bucket ranges 77.6-100 % with **no step anywhere**, and a slip at record K would give ~56 % above K. The disagreements are a **catalog gap, not a mapping gap** — and under `net` there are only **17**. ⚠ **The explanation first published for them is RETRACTED:** it read the `+1` cluster as *"popping the handle of the thing being waited on"*. **The bodies say otherwise** — the shared `begin` `0x0034C290` pushes a literal `0` and pops it straight back, so the handler supplies its own operand and the catalog's zero was correct. The over-generalisation *"every one durative"* is also wrong: seven of those fifteen verbs are instantaneous. **Residual, stated rather than rounded away:** a compensating pair of shifts falling entirely inside one anchor-free window is not excluded; **the largest such window is 25 records.** No single shift of any size survives. **The 2026-09-02 withdrawal got the right answer by a circular route** and is corrected in `COVERAGE.md`. |
| I-7 | ~~Why record `0x048C` carries three handlers.~~ | **ANSWERED 2026-09-07 — it does not.** `0x048D` **`openfullscreenmenu_48d` is the only durative command in that neighbourhood** and all three handlers are its own: begin `003462D0`, poll `00352E00`, result `00346DA0`. `getmapgroundtype_48c` (`0x048C`) is instantaneous; its handler is `003476B0`, its own `result`. **And it is what the verb means** — opening a fullscreen menu is not instantaneous, so the script must wait: `begin` opens it, `poll` asks each frame whether the player is still in it, `result` delivers what they chose. Its neighbours (`getmapid`, `getmapgroundtype`, `npc_to_gimmick`) are one-shot queries needing only a `result`. **This document's oldest puzzle was one durative command among instantaneous ones, read through a frame shifted by one field.** |
| I-2-done | What fields `+8`/`+16`/`+24` of the ScriptVM dispatch table mean. | **ANSWERED** - the table is the **`result` column** of a three-callback command table at `0x01EED700` (begin `tbl+8+32N`, poll `tbl+16+32N`, result `tbl+32+32N`). The documented frame sits 24 bytes above the record boundary, so `+0`=`result(N)`, `+8`=`begin(N+1)`, `+16`=`poll(N+1)`. This also dissolves the old GFZ "contradiction": `003462D0` is `begin(0x048D)`, `00346DA0` is `result(0x048D)` - both correct. |
| I-2 | What record fields `+8`, `+16`, `+24` mean (277/230/1 records use them). Lifecycle phases is a guess. | **ANSWERED** - they are the **next** command's callbacks. The document's frame sits 24 bytes above the true record boundary, so `+0` = `result(N)`, `+8` = `begin(N+1)`, `+16` = `poll(N+1)`. "Lifecycle phases" was the right instinct, but they belong to the neighbouring command. |
| I-3 | Where the `0x2000+` debug verbs dispatch from — 468 catalog entries outside this table. | **ANSWERED** - they are **family 2** (`0x2000 >> 12 == 2`), which uses the shared default command table. The family-0 table this document describes cannot see them. |
| I-4 | ~~What the rest of each 32-byte record holds.~~ | **ANSWERED 2026-09-07.** The record is **four** pointer slots; `begin` (`+0x00`), `poll` (`+0x08`) and `result` (`+0x18`) are three of them. The fourth, at record `+0x10`, is **zero in all 1,496 records** and is read by no accessor. The earlier *"1 record uses `+24`"* was the read past the end of the table that section 13 of the owning document identified — bounded by the table's own record count, it is zero. |
| I-5 | ~~Why 262 in-range verbs have a null handler slot.~~ | **ANSWERED 2026-09-07 — the premise was wrong, and the correction is the finding.** 262 records lack a **result** callback; only **3** lack a callback of any kind, and none of those 3 is a named catalog verb. The other **259 implement `begin` and `poll`** — they are **durative** commands, and a durative command has nothing to return. *"Null handler"* was an artefact of reading one column of a three-column table. |

## K. Movement

From [`../06-Movement-And-Navigation/heading-speed-to-position-delta.md`](../06-Movement-And-Navigation/heading-speed-to-position-delta.md).

> **Falsification pass 130 (`repos-46`, 2026-09-02) overturned this document's headline formula.**
> It read `X = sin(heading)·speed, Z = cos(heading)·speed` with `Y` from an unidentified angle. The
> byte-level trace of `002E4419`–`002E45A1` gives a **spherical** decomposition:
> ```
> X = sin(yaw)·cos(pitch)·speed     yaw   = wrap(movementState[0xA4])
> Y = sin(pitch)·speed              pitch = wrap(movementState[0xA0])
> Z = cos(yaw)·cos(pitch)·speed     W     = 1.0 on all four exits
> ```
> The two sin/cos pairs are **not independent** — `cos(pitch)` is a common factor on both horizontal
> components, so **an actor on a slope covers less ground per frame at the same requested speed.**
> A planar branch (`FUN_00267260 != 0 && FUN_00264460 == 0`) drops the pitch terms and recovers the
> old formula, which is why the wrong reading looked right. The GFZ annotation makes the identical
> omission — **two sources agreeing is not two pieces of evidence when one came from the other's
> neighbourhood.**

| ID | Question | Status |
|---|---|---|
| K-1 | Source of the **second angle** driving `delta.y` — a separate sin/cos pair, not the heading. | **ANSWERED** — it is `movementState + 0xA0`, consumed as a **pitch**: `Y = sin(pitch)·speed`, and the same `cos(pitch)` foreshortens `X` and `Z`. One spherical decomposition, not two independent pairs. |
| K-2 | What actor class `(flags & 0xE0) == 0x60` denotes, and which classes movement excludes. **ANSWERED 2026-09-12 (FABLE), reconciled with `BV-4`:** class 3 is the steerable actor class (sequences 5–7: party, NPCs, monsters, treasure, warps); movement's setters exclude class 0 (script-only controllers, no `+0xB8`), class 1 (placed objects — `+0x38` heading readable, never steered) and class 2 (trigger lines). | **ANSWERED 2026-09-12 (FABLE), reconciled with `BV-4`** — class 3 is the steerable actor class (sequences 5–7: party, NPCs, monsters, treasure, warps); movement's setters exclude class 0 (script-only controllers, no `+0xB8`), class 1 (placed objects — `+0x38` heading readable, never steered) and class 2 (trigger lines). |
| K-3 | What `003A1D30` computes — assumed vector length, unverified. | **ANSWERED** — it is `sqrtf(fabs(x))`: 23 bytes, `cvtss2sd` → `andps` with the 128-bit sign mask at `01CEBD80` → `cvtpd2ps` → `jmp sqrtf`. **Scalar, not a vector routine** — the caller supplies the sum of squares. 12 direct callers, 17 sites. |
| K-4 | The world-context integration path (`002E5380` / `002E54A0`) and what `world_ctx+0x90` bit 4 selects. | **ANSWERED 2026-09-14 (FABLE): the "world context" is the movement body; bit 4 = the field-cell solver moved the body this step.** Path: `Movement_UpdateActorFrame` → `002E5610` → `002E5380` → `002E54A0` → `003DB140` → `00380C40(placement, move)`, which zeroes the displacement and clears bit 4. The cell solver `002327D0` (and `0022F9B0`) accumulates sub-steps into it and sets bit 4, and `00380800` then normalises it. `00329B00` copies that unit vector to battle unit `+0x1C0` with `+0x1F0` bit 9, and `BattleLocomotion_FinalizeHeadingState` `0033BFB0` turns the unit toward it. The no-context branch adds **all three** components; the `X` line is written `*candidate_or_delta` while the others use `[1]`/`[2]`, so an excerpt matching the indexed form dropped it. **"The X term is missing" was promoted to an open question instead of being re-read.** |

one writes a qword and cannot be this float field, leaving **one**: `FUN_002E5E10` (374 B, Movement), which stores `((angle + bias) − (int)((angle + bias)/2pi) × 2pi) − bias` with `bias = angle >= 0 ? +pi : −pi` — **a single sign-biased wrap aimed at `[-pi, pi]`.** So the field is **a heading in radians, re-wrapped on every write by the only writer.** ~~open-coded `Angle_NormalizeRadiansPi`; no path can leave it out of range; three or four `FUN_003DA850` invalidations; the wrapper sets nothing new~~ **Corrected 2026-09-11 (ASTRA-CONTRA-FABLE-FACING-WRITER, EXP-072 + re-reading):** the signature is `(actor, float angle XMM1, float aux XMM2, int commit R9D)`; a null controller skips both stores and every callback; the wrap is not a range guarantee (exact `±pi` flips sign, `+1.0` → `3F800002`, `±inf` and NaN pass through; ~~`≥ 2^31 × 2pi` passes through~~ **corrected 2026-09-12, EXP-074:** past the signed conversion limit the pass stores `f32(a ± π + T) ∓ π` with `T = 2^31 × 2π`, unchanged only for `\|a\| ≥ 2^58`) and differs from the looping `0033CB70`; the thirteenth, `MT-2`, produced `PClassDescriptorForType<...>` reflection objects rather than the container instantiations it asks about. **The reason is structural: these rows ask about POD structs, list element types and `std`/EASTL containers, for which the compiler emits no RTTI at all**, so a non-polymorphic type's silence in the RTTI map is evidence of nothing whatever. *The finding lived only in `_index/_inbox/FABLE.md` and had reached no row until now.* |
| K-7 | What `FUN_00267260` and `FUN_00264460` test. Together they select the planar branch. | **ANSWERED 2026-09-02** — [`../06-Movement-And-Navigation/Movement-Mode-Selection/how-the-engine-chooses-3d-or-flat-movement.md`](../06-Movement-And-Navigation/Movement-Mode-Selection/how-the-engine-chooses-3d-or-flat-movement.md). `00264460` (37 B) is **"does this actor move in three dimensions?"** — `(b >> 1 \| b) & 1` over controller `+0x151`, i.e. **bit 0 OR bit 1**, an *either* and not a two-bit field. `00267260` (78 B) is the flat-motion test and needs **four** conditions: the actor system up, the controller valid (`+0x14F` bit 0 clear and `+0x138` non-null), actor `+0x09` bit 0, and actor `+0x08` bit 1. **Both read the same controller object at `actor+0xC0`, at neighbouring bytes.** Note the asymmetry: **3-D is the default** — flat needs four conditions, 3-D needs one bit. |

Never written during play — but **not always 1.0**: the 60 fps setting runs the whole game at 2.0 / 0.5. **EXTENDED 2026-09-07 — the branch is now read, from the Rewards side.** `FUN_001EDDC0` (165 B) gates the whole block on its own parameter: `test ecx,ecx / je 0x1EDE1F` — **non-zero writes `(2, 2.0, 0.5)`; zero skips it entirely and the `.data` defaults `(1, 1.0, 1.0)` stand.** So the triple is a **frame-rate compensation set**: an integer sub-step count, a scale-up and its reciprocal. Independent re-census here gives **211 / 45 / 182** reads against this row's 211 / 46 / 182 — **a one-count difference on `01DFE0B8`, method difference, not adjudicated.** *Downstream:* this closes `CM-1` and `CM-2` in the loot-pickup document — the field clock counts **frames**, and a pickup's 1800-frame life at 30 fps is 3600 at 60 fps, **sixty seconds either way.** |

## L. Spawn / Encounter lifecycle

From [`../05-Spawn-Encounter-Lifecycle/spawn-placement-and-retirement.md`](../05-Spawn-Encounter-Lifecycle/spawn-placement-and-retirement.md).

> **Falsification pass 131 (`repos-46`, 2026-09-02) overturned this document in five places and
> moved it `PARTIAL` → `DOCUMENTED`.** The whole tunable ring is now recovered with defaults and
> owners: arc **180°** (the *forward* half-plane, ±90° of leader facing), min/max spawn **39.0/42.0**,
> retire range **43.0** (one unit of hysteresis past the ring), attempt limit **1**, return window
> **300 seconds**, automatic active cap **28** of a 32-slot pool, and a shared "max considered
> distance" that ships **+INF**.
>
> **The document's claim that "monsters do not materialise in your face… that is a distance rule, not
> luck" is wrong twice.** `Spawn_TrySelectCandidatePosition` has two exclusive modes on the first byte
> of an authored field-class-0 record; in **AREA mode it draws the position from the shared gameplay
> LCG** (radius quantised to 1/100, heading inside the arc, around the leader) and **never calls the
> distance validator at all**. And the minimum distance is applied **only** when the unit carries flag
> ~~bit 49 or 53~~ **bit 45 or 49** *(corrected in the ledger 2026-09-12; L-9)* — every other spawn-backed unit gets `minR = 0.0` **and may be placed on top of the
> player**. Every distance in this system is **squared and XZ-planar**; height never counts.
>
> Also corrected: `0031B810` is **not** a table. The document listed it as a "party/player slot table
> (up to 4)". It is `BattleUnit_FindMappedDefinitionSelectorByIndex`, a 70-byte function with 27
> callers; the table it consults is at `DAT_02EBF190 + 0x5A5A`.

Rejection is universal (first violation returns 0); acceptance is existential (`accepted` starts at 0 and is set only inside the eligible branch), so **"nobody to measure against" is a REJECTION, not a vacuous pass.** The spawn path passes `include_all_party_slots = 0`, so "eligible" narrows to the **party focus alone** — the one character you are steering. |

| Q-2 | What `DAT_02CF8260` counts and what the `+0x1D` comparison decides. | **ANSWERED 2026-09-14 (FABLE): the class-descriptor id allocator.** `+0x1D` is a qword index (byte `+0xE8`). Thirteen functions stamp the counter into `+0xE8` and increment it; the base destructor `00633390` decrements it only when `+0xE8 + 1` equals it, so an id is reclaimed only from the most recently numbered descriptor. `00638AE0` sizes a `counter + 1` table by id, links each descriptor to its base (`+0x78`), and writes pre-order hierarchy indices into `+0xEC` (descendants follow their class — the interval numbering of an isKindOf range test). |

It serves the cluster loader's acceptance of big-endian `PHYR` files; which order serves load vs save is not established. |

The 384 non-deleting thunks are in no vtable, have no data reference and **no direct caller** — **no ordinary edge reaches them at all**; what transfers control to each is a tail jump from a compiler-generated unwind funclet, and it is those funclets' **instructions** that say when: **315** reload the object from the parent frame (`mov rcx, [rdx + 0x60]`), **69** name a static (`lea rcx, [static]`). *Restated 2026-09-15 under FINAL-AUDIT pass 6, propagated from the page: the earlier wording “are each reached once, by a tail jump from an exception-unwind funclet” put the reachability claim on the unwind edge, which is the banned inference — and `COVERAGE-DIMENSIONS` excludes all 3,834 EH-funclet edges from the call graph, so that edge is not a caller. The finding is unchanged; the 315/69 instruction split is what carried it all along.* Normal-exit teardown is the inlined 26 B static-teardown family — [class descriptors §15](../22-Middleware-PhyreEngine/Reflection-And-Class-Metadata/class-descriptor-and-metadata-system.md). | ANSWERED |

The question's own `2,134` is superseded by 2,248; see [the class descriptor system](../22-Middleware-PhyreEngine/Reflection-And-Class-Metadata/class-descriptor-and-metadata-system.md) §12 and §14. |
| DK-1 | **`0063BC00` has exactly 369 distinct callers, and the RTTI names exactly 369 instantiable descriptor classes** (331 `Concrete<T>` + 38 `WithoutDefaultConstructor<T>`). Is that a mechanism or a coincidence? | **ANSWERED 2026-09-14 (OPUS) — a MECHANISM, and the RTTI test was the wrong instrument.** Disassembling every caller and reducing each body to its **mnemonic sequence** (registers kept, numeric literals ignored): **369 callers collapse to 23 distinct sequences, 345 of them to four** — 162 bodies of 55 instructions in one sequence, 104 of 64, 70 of 65, 9 of 62. Within each of those sizes the sequence is unique. The raw bytes all differ, and that is the tell: consecutive stubs differ in a single `rel32` to consecutive targets and in their immediates. **A template instantiated once per class.** This EXPLAINS the failed RTTI test rather than contradicting it — only `WithoutDefaultConstructor<T>` instantiations carry their own RTTI record, so 15 of 369 is what an RTTI probe should return. Control: the shape test blanks only literals, so a match means the compiler emitted the same code; and 369 distinct callers across 373 call sites, so the count is not an artefact of per-site counting. NOT CLAIMED: which class each stub belongs to. [class-descriptor-and-metadata-system.md](../22-Middleware-PhyreEngine/Reflection-And-Class-Metadata/class-descriptor-and-metadata-system.md) §DK-1 **WHAT THIS REPLACES, preserved:** OPEN — recorded as unproven. The confirming test failed: only **15 of the 369** callers carry an RTTI identity, all slot 10 of `WithoutDefaultConstructor<T>` — 15 of 38, not 38 of 38. A coincidence in two counts is a lead, not a mechanism. [the class descriptor system](../22-Middleware-PhyreEngine/Reflection-And-Class-Metadata/class-descriptor-and-metadata-system.md) §10. |

Proof by siblings that install the class's own vtable in the out buffer: `005D6E00` writes `PDynamicMeshInstance`'s `00D498B0`; `005CE850` writes it and then `PModifierNetworkDynamicMeshInstance`'s `00D498D0` (an inlined base-then-derived chain). The triple is the attach point's fields: the `PWorldMatrix` object, the `PMeshInstance` object (`02CB6E80` = `WithoutDefaultConstructor<PMeshInstance>`), 0. Field names and the slot-10 call site are not established. |

All nine language copies (`ch`, `cn`, `de`, `es`, `fr`, `in`, `it`, `kr`, `us`) are byte-identical. **`eventmemorylist.bin`** - magic `EVMEMLST`, count 8, `10 + 2 * 8 = 26` bytes: `0x0`, `0x31`, `0x29C`, `0x29E`, `0x30E`, `0x367`, `0x368`, `0x390`, one copy under `common`; [the event-memory page](../14-Story-Event-Quest-Hunt/event-memory-at-actor-bind.md) had already recorded these eight. Both lists open with a zero entry, so the zero is the format's habit rather than an authored id. *Not established:* what the 52 flags gate - the file's name says map-jump groups, which is a name, not a reading of their consumers. Authored data. *Earlier status, kept:* OPEN - **a retrieval, not a research problem.** Both files are inside the 31 GB `SRYK` archive, and [the field-record document](../03-World-Area-Field/Field-Record-Table/field-record-table-navimapdata.md) already carries an extracted file's MD5 and `vbf_path`, so the route exists. Until then *53* and *8* are **capacities, not counts** - the `u16` at `+8` is what the loops trust. [§8f](../14-Story-Event-Quest-Hunt/persistent-flag-banks.md). |

Their only references are `lea r9` into reflection-registrar calls by `00681D80`, `006827C0`, `006CD000` and `006CE190`, so they are registered members of a reflected class — which makes the script identity **authored runtime data**, and that is a reading of the vocabulary rather than of the executor. **Why *when* cannot be answered here:** both executors have **zero callers** by graph and by byte-level decode. **This does not overturn `DA-1`**, which already holds that static evidence cannot settle whether a Lua chunk ever runs, and the Lua page's own conclusion stands unchanged: *“a runtime question, and a breakpoint on `00684D10` remains the way to settle it.”* **Not read:** `00686280` (1,448 B), the second executor.  |

| R-5 | What schedules script execution — per-frame hook or load-time only. | **ANSWERED 2026-09-22 (FABLE): neither - the question has a third answer, because the scheduler is NEVER CONSTRUCTED.** The 2026-09-18 note closed the DATA route; the CODE route is now closed too, and together they leave none. **`PScripting::PScheduler`s vtable is `00D6FD68`** (slot 0 is `00685140`, the chunk executor). **Exactly two bodies in the image reference that vtable:** `00681560`, which stamps it into `this` (`0068157D` / `00681584 mov [rcx], rax`) - the constructor - and `00681880`, which stamps and frees - the destructor. **The constructor has exactly ONE caller, `00680D80`**, 44 bytes of placement construction: `test rdx,rdx` / `mov rcx,rdx` / `call 00681560` / `mov al,1` (`00680D97`-`00680DA5`) - construct in place at the address given, report success. **`00680D80` has ZERO code references and exactly one stored pointer**: `.rdata` `00D6F418`, which is **slot 10 of `PClassDescriptorWithoutDefaultConstructor<PScheduler>`** (vtable base `00D6F3C8`). What would escape it is a call through a computed address, and there is **no code reference to `00680D80` at all** for such a computation to start from. *Consistent with `DA-1` and `UQ-312`: the Lua path is linked, registered and reflected end to end, and nothing in the shipped game enters it.* **NATIVE/STATIC - image and shipped assets, nothing executed.** [the Lua bindings page](../22-Middleware-PhyreEngine/Embedded-Lua-And-Object-Bindings/embedded-lua-and-phyre-object-bindings.md) *Bound corrected and enumerated 2026-09-22 (FABLE), same day as the answer above.* **The answer stands; the stated escape route did not.** A caller needs no reference to `00680D80` - it needs the DESCRIPTOR, and can reach slot 10 virtually, which is exactly the bound `DA-1` records. **So who holds the descriptor is now enumerated.** It is a static object at **`02E41370`**, built at boot by CRT initializer `00166140` (zero callers; its single stored pointer is `.rdata` `008C41E0`, inside the initializer table) and destroyed at exit by `008B2300` (26 B - vptr swap to `00D6F120`, then `jmp 00633390`; zero callers, `atexit`-registered). **`02E41370` has NINETEEN referencing sites and not one belongs to the game:** two are that initializer, two are that teardown, and the remaining fifteen are all inside the scripting module itself - `00680950` x2, `00681F30` x6, `006836B0`, `00683DC0`, `00683F70`, `00685810`, `006858C0`, `006859E0`, `00685FB0`. *The two that look like exceptions to `DA-1`s "all inside the scripting module" are the CRTs own teardown, not a consumer.* **So no code outside the scripting module and the CRTs init/teardown ever holds the descriptor, and the scripting modules own entries are the ones nothing reaches.** |

The linker scattered that table's strings across `.rdata`; **the adjacency means nothing.** **Code references: `PhyreObject` 13, `__index` 2 (both inside Lua — `00826500` is tagged `ThirdParty.Scripting.Lua`), `__newindex` 0, `__eq` 0.** Phyre's binding layer names none of them. **The metatable is an identity token compared with `lua_rawequal`, not a dispatch table**, exactly as the owning document's §4 describes. *Honest limit:* an absent name-string reference does not prove no metamethod is installed, since Lua sets metafields by indexing the event table rather than by naming the string. **Bonus:** the two `lua_pcall` sites with zero callers (`00684D10`, `00686280`) are **vtable slots of `PScripting::PClassCallableMethodScript::PCallerScript`**, two further slots of which are the folded `ret 0` stub `005C5230`; their callers are slots of `PScripting::PScheduler`. **Lua is reached entirely by virtual dispatch, and no `.lua` file ships in the archive.** |

A single witness cannot prove a correlation holds, but it is enough to **refute** one, and refutation is what this row asks for. *What is genuinely left is a different question and should be asked as one:* **what measure does track startup cost** — bytes constructed, objects built, or wall time, the last of which is the only live-only one of the three. **The row as written is answered and should not be waiting on anything.** See `00-Engine-Core-Runtime/Startup-Data-Construction/`. |

Note also *why* no scan has seen inside it — an array reached as `base + index × 0xD0` emits no literal displacement for any element past the first, so every displacement-keyed instrument in the kit is blind to 42 of the 44 by construction, exactly the failure `AU-5` records. What survives is **only** the store's own two byte-identical 208-byte records and the exact boundary — **there is no code-side witness at all**, which is precisely why the span stays undeclared. The question stands and needs a witness found some way other than by stride. **WEAKENED FURTHER 2026-09-19 (OPUS), by evidence already in the store.** `count5A42`'s row records that *"a repeat at stride `0xD0` is VISIBLE BUT NOT ESTABLISHED: the flag-to-sub-object distances differ (`0xC` then `0xE`)"*, and it is exact: record A's guard `+0xC4` sits `0xC` below its object `+0xD0`, record B's guard `+0x192` sits `0xE` below its object `+0x1A0`, so **the pointers step `0xD0` while the guards step `0xCE`** — the records are not congruent. FOR the array: the pointer stride, a shared count slot at record-relative `+0xC2`, and the span closing to the byte on the 44th boundary. AGAINST it: that two-byte mismatch, and no code-side witness of any kind. **`check_repeated_records.py` cannot see the mismatch** — it compares declared field sizes, so records whose guards sit at different relative offsets look identical to it, which means a sweep that compares tilings is not comparing structures. | AC-10 | ~~Whether digit columns are in fact even on screen. The mechanism believed to cause them does not exist, and **the observation itself was never measured**.~~ **ANSWERED 2026-09-17 (FABLE) — from the bodies, and no screen is needed.** The row asked about an observation; the property it wanted is a fact of the code. **Within one formatting call the digit step is one register loaded once.** `002AE610` decodes ONE reference character before its digit loop — the 16-bit code at `+0x20` of the map table, which this page already identifies as the entry for `'0'` (`002AE7B7`, `002AE7D7 call 002AC2F0`) — and `002AC2F0` writes the whole 16-byte spacing block from that glyph (`movaps [0209CC60]` at `002AC56A`/`002AC59F`, then `[0209CC68]` from the signed advance byte `[rdi+0xA9]` at `002AC5C3`). The formatter then loads `xmm8 = [0209CC68] + [0209CC6C]` at `002AE7DC`/`002AE7EA` and advances its pen by `xmm8` per digit at `002AEA4C`; `xmm8` is written nowhere else between the load and the epilogue restore at `002AEAF7`, and the digit loop `002AE920`–`002AEA96` contains no reload. So every digit of one number advances by the `'0'` glyph's pitch — **monospaced by construction**, whatever the drawn digit is. **Across calls the same holds whenever the font and scale are the same**, because the step is derived from `'0'` each time, not carried over: on exit the formatter overwrites the block (`002AEABB`/`002AEAC2` zero it, `002AEAC9` stores the number's total advance into `0209CC68`) and the next call re-derives it. Two numbers drawn with the same font and scale therefore share their pitch; column alignment then depends only on the caller's starting pen, which is authored layout, not a mechanism. **The row's premise is withdrawn:** *the mechanism believed to cause them does not exist* was true of the per-glyph-metric belief `AC-9` refuted, and `AC-9`'s own answer names the mechanism that does exist. **What this does not settle, and is not this row:** whether the general glyph loop `002A9F00` keeps one pitch per line or lets the control-code interpreter `002AC5F0` re-set `0209CC68` per character (it writes it at 14 sites) — that is the 2026-09-14 note on this page, about text, not digits. Static, body read; the `xmm8` liveness is re-checkable in one listing. | ANSWERED |

## AM. Battle locomotion

|---|---|---|
| AM-1 | Which angular band selects which turning behaviour. | **ANSWERED** - the three angles are one **hysteresis loop**: **45 deg** is a deadband (below it no turn starts and the heading is returned unchanged), **120 deg** gates latching the **fast** turn rate `st[0xF0]` (also requiring `st[0x170] & 0x1C == 0x1C`), **20 deg** releases the latch so the turn finishes at the slow rate `st[0xEC]`. The turn ends when the heading matches. |

A final `x0.99` guard means a unit never steps past its target - it lands 1 % short each frame. Distance is **XZ only** (`Vector3_ComputeXZDistance`), so height does not count. |

| AM-5 | ~~What `DecodeOrderGoal` (965 B) decodes, and the order format it reads.~~ | **ANSWERED 2026-09-26 (FABLE, Claude Opus 5.5): status restated; the last unread order case was read on 2026-09-18, and every opcode has one.** *Previous status, kept as history:* **ADVANCED 2026-09-08 — format and dispatch established, semantics not.** Order record: **`+0x00` u16 opcode, `+0x02` s16 parameter**; two floats fetched separately via `00265090` with the larger kept. Opcode space is **`0x4000`-based**, dispatched by three range tests and an MSVC two-level table (indices `00312B10`, targets `00312AF8`): **`4000–401F` — 32 opcodes, one shared case, index = opcode − 0x3FFF**; `4020`, `4022`, `4023`, `4024` — four specials; **`4021` and `4025` — two holes inside the band that route to the reject path**; **`4026–4035` — 16 opcodes, one shared handler `002367A0`, index = opcode − 0x4026**; a separate compare chain from `0x4124`. **`0x4022` is thereby placed** — the literal in this document's fixed-speed-escape item is an order opcode, not a magic number. **What any case *does* is unread — `DE-1`.** **ANSWERED 2026-09-18 (FABLE) — the last unread case is read, and every opcode now has one.** The low-band dispatch is two image-relative tables (index bytes at `00312B10`, case RVAs at `00312AF8`, `003127AA`–`003127C5`) and they send `0x4020` alone to `003127D7`: the arm requires the battle-state record at unit `+0x698` to carry kind byte **1** at `+5` (`003127E7`; the page's `0x4022` reading tests the same byte for 0, the party kind), takes the **SpawnRecord** at unit `+0x6A0` and points at its `+0x50` — the *live persisted world position* on [the spawn page](../05-Spawn-Encounter-Lifecycle/spawn-placement-and-retirement.md) — keeps the `s16` parameter in `r8d`, and jumps to the shared sampler tail `00312A5D`, which calls `00312DF0(reference, −1, parameter, unit, out)` and, on success, copies the sampled point into the goal and stores the radius (`00312A5D`–`00312A8F`). So **`0x4020` is “wander within ±N of your own spawn position”**, the non-party sibling of the `0x4000`–`0x401F` family (which samples around a POSENT reference by index) and of `0x4125` (which samples around reference 20). With that, every opcode's case is read: `0x4000`–`0x401F` and `0x4026`–`0x4035` under `DE-1`, the index under `DE-4`, `0x4021` under `DE-2` (the engine's default order), `0x4022` / `0x4023` / `0x4024` and the `0x4124`+ band under `DE-3` above, `0x4025` the one true hole, and `0x4020` here. Static: the two tables and the arm. |
| AM-6 | ~~Which RNG stream the randomised recovery draws from.~~ | **ANSWERED 2026-09-08 — the process-global CRT `rand`.** All three randomised functions (`003343D0`, `00334E00`, `0033E1F0`) call **IAT slot `008C3098`**, resolved *in the import table* to `api-ms-win-crt-utility-l1-1-0.dll!rand`. `ResetAvoidanceStateRandomized` (278 B) **calls nothing else at all**. **Not the shared gameplay LCG (`00328370`) and not either Mersenne Twister.** The CRT stream is shared with 48 sites across 30 functions, so its state depends on whatever else the frame did: **a blocked unit's detour is not reproducible across machines, and no synchronisation of the game's own RNG changes that.** Engine evidence that foe avoidance is a purely local decision. |

| AO-3 | What the phase byte at `commandState[0x15]` enumerates. | **ANSWERED** - `0` not started (run begin then poll), `1` running (poll only), **`2` finished returning an integer**, **`3+` finished returning a float**. Six records do nothing observable (fs_setclanrank, fsroll_setcounternow/setdouble into the ret-0 stub; the two counters read constant 0; getdouble constant 1; fs_reloadmrp finishes at once). | ID | Question | Status |

| AP-1 | What distinguishes control-code bands **1-3**, **11-27** and **28-283**. The middle band is polled across *any* device, the upper band **per bank**. | **ANSWERED 2026-09-02, with a correction to the band bound.** `00197160` dispatches with three unsigned subtract-and-compare tests: `(code-0x0B) < 0x11` → `IsControlCode11To27ActiveAnyDevice`; `(code-0x1C) < 0x7D` → `IsControlCode28To283ActiveForBank(…, bank 0)`; `(code-1) < 3` → `IsPrimaryControlCode1To3Active`. The any-device / per-bank split reproduces exactly. **But the upper band at this call site is 28–152, not 28–283** — `0x7D` is 125. The callee's GFZ name may reflect what it accepts; the caller routes only 28–152. Cross-check: the largest reserved control id is **152**. Codes `0` and `4`–`10` are polled by no band (**BG-5**). |
| AP-2 | ~~Whether `0x80` is the analog neutral.~~ | **ANSWERED 2026-09-08 — yes, and a constant proves it rather than the midpoint argument.** `InputManager_TranslateBindingProfileToControlState` (`00197160`) computes `out = (v + 1.0) * 128.0 + (currentByte - 128.0)`, clamped to `[0, 255]`. **`128.0` is a literal at `008F3A2C`**, used both as the centre of the `-1..+1` → `0..256` axis map and as the reference the digital contribution is measured from. **Also settled on the way: axes 2 and 3 are multiplied by `-1.0` (`01CEBC9C`) unconditionally and again when the per-axis flag at `DAT_01F7FFE0+8`/`+9` is set — so the engine inverts those axes by default and the "invert" option restores them.** |
| AP-3 | What `InputControl_AdvanceChannelTimingState`'s constants **16384, 1760, 1790, 180, 546** are - which are thresholds and which are rates. | **ANSWERED 2026-09-02.** **Thresholds:** `1790` (ceiling on the hold timer at `+0x12`), `1760` (the trigger to set the rate negative), `180` (phase length, clamping both `+0x14` and `+0x10`), `16384` (ceiling on the accumulator at `+0x16`). **Rate:** `±546`, stored at `+0x18` and added to the accumulator once per tick — `0xFDDE` is `−546` read as a **signed** short, `0x222` is `+546`. `16384/546 ≈ 30` ticks to traverse the range, so the accumulator is a triangle ramp. Full per-branch arithmetic in the binding-profiles document §4. **What the ramp drives is still unknown (BG-4).** |

Frame = 4 B header + 8 x u16 masks + 16 analog axis bytes; `4+16+16 = 36` and `0x44 + 16*36 + 16 = 660` exactly. What the masks *contain* remains open. **ANSWERED 2026-09-18 (FABLE) — the eight masks, both sets, read from the three builders and the poll.** Frame-relative, from the slot base `+0x44`: `+0x04` / `+0x06` **held**, `+0x08` / `+0x0A` **auto-repeat**, `+0x0C` / `+0x0E` **newly pressed**, `+0x10` / `+0x12` **released** — the first of each pair is **set 0**, the second **set 1**. *The poll* `0035F420` writes the device-slot dword `022CB640` to −1 (`00862660` is `mov dword [rdx], -1`, so its name is right and the value is an all-ones eligibility mask), polls the control state into `022CB680` (`00862670`), and copies sixteen per-button bytes into the slot at `+0x58` .. `+0x67` through the index table `01EF9238` (`00 01 02 03 06 04 07 05 0E 0F 0C 0D 08 09 0A 0B`: button bit *i* takes control-state byte `2 + table[i]`), with `0x80` for bits 0–3 when not down (`0035F4D0`–`0035F508`). *The transitions builder* `0035FAC0` runs **first** (`0035F517`): held = the `022CB640` word AND NOT the control-state word (`0035FB50`–`0035FB64`, the buttons are **active-low**), with the D-pad opposites cancelled (`0x50` = up+down, `0xA0` = right+left, `0035FB6D`–`0035FB82`; the bits are the SCE order, up `0x10`, right `0x20`, down `0x40`, left `0x80`); when record `+0x09` bit 1 is **clear** it writes set 0 — `+0x04` held, `+0x0C` pressed = `(prev ^ held) & held`, `+0x10` released = `(prev ^ held) & prev` — and calls `0035FBD0` for `+0x08`; it always writes `+0x06` (`0035FBBD`). *The analog builder* `0035F760` runs **second** (`0035F529`), so its stores are the ones that survive: it snaps the two stick pairs (slot `+0x5A` / `+0x5B` and `+0x58` / `+0x59`, centre `0x80`) to centre inside the dead zone `[record+0x0D]` (`0035F7BD`–`0035F876`), zeroes the four D-pad bytes `+0x5C` .. `+0x5F` whose bit is not held, and derives direction bits from stick A beyond the threshold `[record+0x03]` (`0035F8D5`–`0035F901`: down `0x40`, right `0x20`, up `0x10`, left `0x80`, each clearing its opposite). **`r12` is the physical D-pad nibble**: when record `+0x09` bit 1 is **set**, bits 4–7 of the held word are set aside in `r12` and the stick's directions replace them (`0035F8C0`–`0035F8CA`), set 0 is written from that stick-as-D-pad word (`0035FA3D`–`0035FA6B`) and the stick and D-pad bytes are rewritten as scaled magnitudes with `[record+0x0C]` and `[record+0x0B]` (`0035F90D`–`0035FA33`); otherwise `r12` is 0. Then `ebx = ebx OR r12` restores the nibble and **set 1 is the union** of digital buttons, stick directions and the physical D-pad: `+0x06` held, `+0x0E` pressed, `+0x12` released (`0035FA79`–`0035FA9F`), and `0035FBD0(record, frame, prev, 1)` fills `+0x0A`. *The repeat builder* `0035FBD0` keeps eight countdown bytes at record `+0x24 + set + 2i`, one per button-group word at record `+0x34 + 2i`, reloaded from record `+0x04` (initial delay) or `+0x05` (repeat rate), and emits the group's held bits into `frame + 8 + 2·set` when its counter runs out (`0035FBF9`–`0035FC87`). ~~The record initialiser `0035F260` sets the thresholds `+0x0A` / `+0x0B` = `0x0090`, `+0x0C` = `0x20` (`0035F31D`–`0035F323`) and never writes `+0x0D`, so the dead-zone radius is 0 unless a caller sets it.~~ *(Corrected 2026-09-30, SWE2-DATA: those are the initialiser's own displacements from `rdi` = record+1 (`022CAE91`), the one site that addresses the channel record one byte in. The 24-byte record is the **message struct itself**, so `0x8001`/`0x8002` are not an id space but the **payload of message id `0x0C`**: UI notification codes in a dense enum based at `0x8000`, decoded by `sub rax,0x8000`. `0x8000` = selection changed, `0x8001` = confirm/activate, `0x8002` = cancel/back - **independently reconfirming A0 = confirm, A4 = cancel**. | AY-1 | Whether the `st2e` string tables' indices align with action ids, and the heap encoding. | **ANSWERED - no, and the format was misread.** Records are **string IDs**, not offsets; header `+0x14` is the heap offset; the heap carries `{one, base=12, size, count, offsets[count+1]}` - **`count+1` and `base=12` are forced by the data**, and a wrong reading still yields plausible text (every string truncated to its last ~10 chars), which is the trap. Encoding is a **custom charset**: `A`-`Z` = byte+0x21 from `0x20`, `a`-`z` = byte+0x27, space `0x04`, punctuation above `0xA0`. Description ids are **`40000 + category*100 + slot`** on a hundreds grid - only 82 of 322 fall below 543. Validated three ways: block 10 has **13** entries (13 Espers), block 9 has **18** (6 characters x 3 ranks), and blocks 1-5 match `word.bin` block 3's magick order. |

| EW-7 | ~~**Why attaching ANY debugger permanently disables the game's input.**~~ | **ANSWERED 2026-09-08 — and the premise was wrong.** Attaching does **not** disable input: with a full debug event loop and **no debug registers programmed**, input is **3 of 3** before, during and after. **It is the HIT RATE.** A cold breakpoint (`003EAA70` at the front-end, 0 hits) leaves input at **3 of 3**; a hot one (`0020E600`, **255,944 hits in 12 s**) takes it to **0 of 3**. **And a hot breakpoint changes which code runs at all** — armed beside two hot ones, `003EAA70` recorded 0 hits in-world; armed **alone** in the same state it recorded **1,130,002 in 75 s**. Rule: **arm the target alone; take the control in its own run.** [`RUNTIME-RESEARCH.md`](RUNTIME-RESEARCH.md) §8d. |
| EW-2 | **Why attaching a dbgeng debugger freezes `FFXII_TZA`.** | **ANSWERED 2026-09-08 by replacing the instrument.** The dbgeng server's resume path never actually resumes this target; rather than debug someone else's engine, the Win32 debug API was driven directly — `hwbp.py`, hardware breakpoints in the DR registers of every thread, so **no code byte is modified**. **The game keeps running: 5.062 CPU seconds over 6.0 s wall, 105 threads armed, 133,679 control hits with arguments captured.** Breakpoints, argument capture and controlled negatives all work. **The remaining limitation is `EW-7`, not the freeze.** [the runtime-research page](RUNTIME-RESEARCH.md) §8d. |
| EW-5 | **The real registration order of the input name registries — and whether 143 and 97 are complete.** | **ANSWERED 2026-09-08 — one live walk settled both.** The chains are **exactly 143 and 97 nodes**, every one with a readable name, and against the 240 recovered statically there are **0 live-only and 0 static-only** — so **nothing is registered at runtime** in the observed state. The order (the chain reversed, because the list is push-front) is **`Empty = 0` first, then strictly descending by value** in both registries — and in the channel registry **the only places consecutive registrations share a value are 11..26, exactly the 16 alias groups**, reproducing the static grouping independently. [the input name registry contract](../15-Input/Input-Name-Registry/CONTRACT-input-name-registry.md) §13. |
| EW-4 | **What the other four paired functions in each name registry do.** | **ANSWERED 2026-09-08.** A **scalar deleting destructor** (unlink, then `operator delete(this, 0x20)`), **two lookup forms** — one writing an out-parameter and returning **`0x13` NOT_FOUND**, one returning the pointer — and an **enumerator** that flattens the list into an array of `count * 8` bytes, reallocating only when the count differs. **Two things reading the insert alone could never have shown:** the return-code family has a **fourth member, `0x13` NOT_FOUND**, which the insert can never return; and the enumerator frees the previous array **only when bit 31 of the stored count is clear**, so that bit is an **ownership flag**. Each key-side twin verified to reference its own head `02EB83B8` and vtable `01CD89D8`. **5 of 5 identified, 1 of 5 reconstructed.** [the input name registry contract](../15-Input/Input-Name-Registry/CONTRACT-input-name-registry.md) §6. |

Bit 7 wins over bit 3. That the byte is a flags word rather than a value is independent: `FUN_00434cd0` tests bits 3, 4, 5 and 6 of it separately, and `FUN_00435050` — called immediately before this ladder and gating it — tests bit 3. **What distinguishes the three paths is elaboration, not kind.** Their callee sets nest: all three share **33** callees; `00437130` has **exactly** those 33 and nothing else; `00438860` adds **12** more; the inline path's own extras are the ladder's own call targets. So the same drawing operation is reached at three levels, cheapest inline, and `00438860` (20,603 B against 5,930 B) is the elaborate one. **Not claimed:** what the twelve extra helpers do, or which visual feature each bit names — that needs the 20 KB body read, and the selection rule was the question. **Added 2026-09-15 (OPUS) — the builder decodes, so the authored bit behind each path is now named.** The page's own wording says `+0x1F1` is *“built in the walk from record bytes `+0x4A` and `+0x590` (`00449B93`–`00449C6D`)”*, and that range had not been read. It is seven MSVC bitfield inserts of the form `dst ^= ((src ^ dst) & mask)`, which is itself independent confirmation that `+0x1F1` is a flags byte: a compiler does not emit seven single-bit inserts into an enum. Writing `v` for `rec[+0x590]`: `00449B93` puts `rec[+0x4A]` bits 2–4 into `+0x1F1` bits 0–2 (mask `7`, source `rec[+0x4A] >> 2`); then mask `0x10` ← `v` bit 1, mask `0x20` ← `v` bit 2, mask `0x40` ← `v` bit 3 (each source `v << 3`); mask `0x80` ← `v` bit 5 (source `v << 2`, written as `and cl, 0x7F` / `xor` against the unmasked value); and `+0x1F2` bits 0 and 1 ← `v` bits 6 and 7 (source `v >> 6`). **The mask-`8` insert at `00449BA9` is the one that is NOT a single-bit copy, and it is the interesting one.** Its source is built as `(v >> 2) OR (v << 3)` (`shr dl, 2` / `shl al, 3` / `or dl, al`), whose bit 3 is `v` bit 5 **OR** `v` bit 0 — so `v` bit 5 is written into **both** `+0x1F1` bit 3 and `+0x1F1` bit 7. Read against the ladder's priority (bit 7 beats bit 3), the three paths have one authored bit each: **`rec[+0x590]` bit 0 alone sets bit 3 only → `00437130`; `rec[+0x590]` bit 5 sets bit 3 and bit 7, and bit 7 wins → `00438860` (VU0); neither set → the inline path at `00435699`.** `v` bit 4 is not inserted anywhere in this range. **CONCEDED 2026-09-15 (OPUS) — FABLE refused to tick this box and was right, and I reproduced their measurement before conceding.** What they confirm and what stands: the ladder at `0043566F`/`00435677`/`00435688` exactly as written, the callee counts (33 shared, `00437130` exactly those 33, `00438860` plus 12), and the `00449B93` builder decode. **What is withdrawn is the sentence that made this row ANSWERED.** *“The same drawing operation is reached at three levels, cheapest inline”* is refuted by size: `004355D0` is **5,936 B / 1,279 instructions** against `00437130`'s **5,930 B / 1,271** — the inline path is **six bytes larger**, not cheaper, and nothing measured supports a cost ordering. **And one detail was simply wrong:** I wrote that the inline path's extras are *“the ladder's own call targets”*. They are **seven**, and only four are — `00435050`, `00434CD0`, `00437130`, `00438860`. Handles are **`(generation << 8) \| index`** with a 24-bit generation wrapping to 1 (never 0); `[entry+0x30] == 0` marks a free slot. **The byte-wide index against 128 entries is safe by construction** - the allocator never assigns >= 128. | BN-2 | The field split inside `phyreBody[0xC0]` and `child->material[0x04]`. Inside, `edx = ebx AND 7` and `eax = ebx >> 3` (with the signed-correction branch `lea eax, [rbx + 7]` / `sub edx, 8` that a compiler emits for a signed divide by 8), then `movzx eax, byte ptr [rcx + r14]`, **`btr eax, edx`**, and the byte is stored back. **That is exactly `mask[i >> 3] &= ~(1 << (i AND 7))` for `i = 0..15`, with no special cases** — the pseudocode this page already carries, now confirmed against the instructions. **So the mapping is produced by a uniform loop over the slot index**, and bit 10 corresponds to slot 10 for the same reason bits 13 and 14 correspond to slots 13 and 14. **The 13/14 evidence was never the general case; it was two instances of it.** **One site sits outside the loop and uses the same arithmetic**: `00197322`–`00197342` applies `AND 7` / `>> 3` / `btr` to the computed index `rsi + 4` rather than to a loop counter. Same rule, one special-cased slot. *The bound, and it matters.* **The loop stops at `0x10`, so this establishes the correspondence for slots 0–15 only** — not for all 28 binding slots the format defines. **Bit 10 is inside that range, so the row's lead is now a finding**; anything about slots 16 and above is not covered by this loop and I did not look for where those are built. |

## BQ. ScriptVM verb dispatch

> **Mechanism 1 — a script verb can call another verb's native handler, with the operand stack as the
> calling convention (7 rows).** `setentrypos` (`0x0405`, `00354FB0`) pops one index, looks the entry
> up, **pushes four floats onto the operand stack**, and calls `00350510` — which is the result
> callback of `0x0019 setpos_19`, declared with four arguments. The verb is literally *"look up that
> entry's position, then do `setpos_19` with it"*, and the four values travel over the same stack a
> script would have used. `ucsetpos` (`0x0168`) does it by **tail jump** into `0034EBC0`, the handler
> of `0x0001 setpos` (three arguments), or drains three floats when its target does not resolve.
> **This is a call-chain class the database did not have** — not a wrapper and not a shared helper:
> the callee is a full verb in the same table.
>
> **Mechanism 2 — the fullscreen menu bails without reading its operands (34 rows).** Thirty-two share
> one 20-byte predicate, `FUN_00280120`: `return *(u64*)(*(void**)0x0209AC30 + 0xC0) == 0` — *is the
> menu object absent*. Every guarded handler opens `call 0x280120 / test eax,eax / jne <return>`,
> bailing without reading anything. It is family 7's standard prologue, on **65 of its 131
> callbacks**. Family 7's records come in exactly four shapes — `(—,—,guarded)`×20,
> `(guarded,guarded,—)`×22, `(—,—,plain)`×54, `(plain,plain,—)`×5 — so **a guarded durative verb
> guards both `begin` and `poll` and has no `result` at all.**
>
> **The decisive check: `min(sums) == 0` on all 34, and `max(sums)` equals the declared count on all
> 25 that declare one — 25 of 25, zero mismatches.** So the arity is **not path-dependent**: the verb
> takes N arguments and there is a path on which it takes none of them. **A guard, not an
> optional-argument convention.** The 34th row (`unkCall_3092`, family 3) is the same shape with its
> own predicate, so the pattern is not unique to the menu.

| BQ-25 | ~~The **88 teardown functions**, confirmed only **negatively** (0/88 on both construction instruments, which is correct but is not a positive identification).~~ **ANSWERED 2026-09-19 (OPUS) — identified by WHAT REACHES THEM, and they are two unrelated things.** Both groups are byte-uniform (28 × 44 B and 60 × 72 B, **one** instruction-mnemonic sequence each) and **all 88 have zero direct callers** — which is exactly why a call-graph instrument could only ever answer negatively. **THE 60 ARE `atexit`-REGISTERED.** Each is the target of exactly one rip-relative `lea`, from **60 distinct hosts** of 228–240 B in the `0015Cxxx` family, one apiece, each ending `lea rcx, <thunk>` then `jmp 00808B90` (`atexit`) — `0015C62B` in `0015C560` is the instance read. The thunk loads a global begin/end pointer pair and, if the count exceeds one and begin is non-null, calls **`qword ptr [rax + 0x18]`**, the allocator's virtual deallocate — **60 of 60, with no other call in any body**. A static container freed through its allocator at exit, which is a positive identification of *teardown* in the only sense the word has. **THE 28 ARE A VIRTUAL METHOD, NOT A CRT TEARDOWN.** They appear **only as 8-byte VAs in `.rdata`** — 28 sites for 28 thunks, never `lea`'d, never called — in runs of contiguous function pointers. Across **all 28** (the population, not a sample) the neighbours at `−2` (`0062EFD0`), `−1` (`0062F080`) and `+3` (`00660570`) are identical **28/28**, while `−4`, `−3` and `+2` differ in every one: a shared base-class layout with per-class overrides, making the thunk **one slot of a common interface implemented 28 times**. Each null-checks its object argument, calls **exactly one** callee (**28 distinct callees, one per class**) and returns `al = 1`. **NOT CLAIMED:** which interface the 28 implement — the three constant slots name it and none has been read — what the 28 callees destroy, *(both answered 2026-09-29: the class-descriptor interface, slot 10; the callees are the classes' constructors - see the object-construction page)* or which containers the 60 hosts own. The `mov qword ptr [rsp+0x20], -2` both groups open with is an MSVC EH-state slot and distinguishes nothing; read as evidence the 28 were unwind funclets it is misleading, and the `.rdata` vtable runs refute that reading. [object construction, destruction and static lifetime](../24-Compiler-And-CRT-Runtime/Cxx-Runtime-Families/object-construction-destruction-and-static-lifetime.md) | **ANSWERED 2026-09-19 (OPUS)** — the 60 are `atexit`-registered static-container teardowns freeing through allocator vtable slot `+0x18` (60/60); the 28 are one slot of a shared vtable layout (three neighbours identical 28/28), slot 10 (+0x50) of a Phyre class-descriptor vtable (27 PClassDescriptorConcrete<T>, 1 PClassDescriptorWithoutDefaultConstructor<PScheduler>), the class's placement default constructor - they construct, they do not destroy (corrected 2026-09-29, SWE2-EC7 under FABLE family ruling R4; object-construction page, section "The 28 construct"). |

## BJ. Lazy statics and the one-time init lock

Owner document:
[`../24-Compiler-And-CRT-Runtime/Lazy-Static-Initialization/lazy-statics-and-the-one-time-init-lock.md`](../24-Compiler-And-CRT-Runtime/Lazy-Static-Initialization/lazy-statics-and-the-one-time-init-lock.md)

Filed by peer session `repos-94`, 2026-09-02. Population: **1,681 distinct objects, 1,732 sites,
707 holder functions**, 1,545 with an abort funclet, 136 without.

| ID | Question | Status |
|---|---|---|
| BJ-1 | Which of the 1,681 are reached on a **normal boot** versus only in specific areas or menus. Needs runtime evidence; static reading cannot answer it. **TESTED AND THE ROW IS RIGHT — 2026-09-16 (FABLE), now with a number instead of an assertion.** *Static reading cannot answer it* is the kind of claim I am supposed to attack, so I attacked it. It holds, and the measurement is worth more than the verdict. **The attempt.** A lazy static whose holder is not reachable from the process entry cannot be initialised on a normal boot — that *is* a static statement, and it would partition the population for free. Seeds: the PE `AddressOfEntryPoint` **`00808EE4`** plus **all 1,172 listed functions in the CRT static-initializer table `008C31D8`–`008C5678`**. **Why it fails.** Forward direct-call closure over those 1,173 roots reaches **2,397 of the 38,161 listed bodies — 6.3%**. The engine is driven overwhelmingly through **indirect** calls, so *unreachable in the direct graph* is the normal condition for **94% of the image** and carries almost no information. The partition it produces — **94 holders reachable, 613 not** — is therefore **dominated by the blind spot, and I am not publishing it as a finding.** **One thing the attempt does establish.** The population reproduces independently: the callers of `_Init_thread_header` `008092FC` number **exactly 707**, matching the figure filed by `repos-94`, so the holder set is confirmed by a second route. **And it names the instrument that would actually work.** The obstacle is indirect-call resolution — vtable and function-table binding — which is **the same blind spot `AR-5` ran into** (477 `call reg` sites, 11 indexed calls). **One instrument answers both questions.** Until it exists, boot reachability is not statically decidable here, and the row's *requires runtime evidence* stands. **Recorded as a dead route on purpose**, so the next reader does not spend the same day on it. | **ANSWERED 2026-09-28 (FRONTIER, carried residue).** The row's question - which of the 1,681 a normal boot reaches - is live-only by measurement (FABLE's direct-call route dead at 6.3% reach; OPUS's NATIVE-REPLAY built the 19-guard executed lower bound, 3/3 identical, md5 f60666a1), and the residue (the 1,662 guards outside the replay world) is bounded and carried by a live board obligation, `OPUS-REQ-ASTRA-BJ1-GUARD-SNAPSHOT` (HM-1 shape: live residue carried by a named real carrier). The flag is analysis state the image does not record.* **NARROWED 2026-09-17 (FABLE), and a closure proposed for review:** every five-byte `E9 rel32` function in the list, 835 of them, jumps to an address that is itself a function-list entry; none jumps into the interior of a function or outside the list (a pass over `functions.tsv` resolving each displacement). With the earlier findings, that the 16 are byte-identical in form to the 819 flagged ones and that their one shared feature (a leaf target without unwind data) also holds for 260 flagged forwarders, no property of the bytes, of the targets or of the references separates the two sets. What separates them is the state of the Ghidra project when each forwarder was first analysed (a function created before its target existed is not re-thunked, and four of the 16 carry the older owner tags of an early manual pass), which the executable cannot answer. **CLOSED 2026-09-18 (proposed FABLE, reviewed and signed OPUS) as `NO ADMISSIBLE SOURCE`, and TWO THINGS WERE CORRECTED IN THE SIGNING.** **(1) The kind was wrong and it was the one kind the addendum refuses.** The proposal cited kind (c), which addendum 2026-09-15bk names as what this status is NOT for - the placeholder rows whose answer is a live run - so the closure had been filed under the clause that denies it. BU-1 is a fourth shape the enumeration never had: a fact about the ANALYSIS TOOL's project state. The addendum now carries it as **kind (d)**, with bar 3 spelled out for that kind as a separating-property sweep run by someone other than the author. **(2) The stated mechanism is refused and the row no longer carries it.** The proposal explained the flag as *'a function created before its target existed is not re-thunked'*. That predicts the unflagged set skews FORWARD; measured, **3 of 16 unflagged jump forward (18.8%) against 458 of 819 flagged (55.9%)** - it skews backward, three to one against the prediction. The finding that survives is that the flag is project state the image does not record; WHICH project state is precisely the part no admissible source can supply, so the row states it no longer. **THE REVIEWER'S SWEEP, because a signature without one is a shrug:** population rebuilt from the BYTES rather than the size column - every listed function whose five-byte body decodes as exactly one `E9 rel32` - giving **835 forwarders, 819 flagged, 16 unflagged**, reproducing the proposal exactly; then eleven categorical and three numeric properties tested for one all 16 share and no flagged forwarder does (target is a list entry, target is itself a five-byte forwarder, target owner, target size, own owner, own and target name shape, own and target caller counts, own and target section, jump direction, `final_no_owner`, tags). **None separates them.** The proposal's 260 reproduces to the unit: 559 of the 819 flagged have a target with a `.pdata` record, leaving exactly 260 without, and 0 of the 16 have one. Recorded because it came close and failed: **all 16 unflagged are 16-byte aligned, against 743 of 819 flagged** - 90.7% of the flagged set shares it, so it separates nothing. | BT-5 | Whether the 160-slot pool ever actually **exhausts** in normal play, and what happens when it does. The budget is proven; the behaviour at the limit is not. **ANSWERED 2026-09-18 (FABLE) — it cannot exhaust under the lifecycle, and if it did the character would simply draw without its shadow objects.** *Why it cannot:* the record array holds exactly 160 records (`0x48800 / 0x740`, the count this page derives) and the pool has exactly 160 slots (`0xA0`, the allocator's loop bound at `003B56FF`); the only allocation site is the promotion `00428710`, which takes one slot per record (`003B56D0(record.id)` at `00428785`) and only when `003E68E0` says the record carries an FCP payload whose first byte is non-zero (`003E68E4`..`003E68F7`); retirement frees the slot through `003B6000`. One slot per promoted record and as many slots as records means the scan can never find all 160 taken unless a record were promoted twice without retiring, which the lifecycle contract's step order excludes. *What would happen:* `003B56D0` walks the `0xE0`-byte entries testing bit 0 of `+0x40` (`003B56F0`..`003B5705`) and, finding none free, returns 0 (`003B5707`); the promotion stores that 0 into `+0x114` without a test (`0042878A`); and every consumer of `+0x114` guards on a non-zero handle before touching the entry (the shadow verbs above, `003B6900(handle, 6)` / `(handle, 4)`), so nothing dereferences a missing entry and the character renders without the shadow objects the entry would carry. A valid handle is never 0 by construction: it is the generation shifted left by 8 with the slot in the low byte, and the generation counter `02B40520` wrapping from `0xFFFFFF` to 1 (`003B5724`..`003B574D`). Static: the allocator, the promotion, the predicate, the record count. | ANSWERED |

## Proposed questions raised 2026-09-02/03 — staged, not yet triaged

**92 questions were raised by seven parallel sessions during the audit run and none had
reached this ledger.** They were staged correctly in `_inbox/` — sessions do not edit
`_index/*.md` — and the coordinator merged answers as they arrived and **not proposals.**

> **A question nobody can see is a question that gets re-derived.** And the ledger's own
> denominator was wrong by 92 the whole time, so `questions_closed` was reported against a
> population that excluded everything the run had opened. **Merging them lowers that
> figure, which is correct: the work was done and the count was not.**

**These keep their originating session ids rather than being assigned lettered ones.**
Assigning a letter is triage — it asserts a question is new, distinct from every existing
row, and worth a permanent id. **None of that has been done**, and doing it silently during
a merge would be the same defect as a status field asserting a check that never ran.


### On the `state` column, and what it does not mean

**It is derived from the text, not from a check.** The merge took the longest line mentioning each id
in staging, and **that line is sometimes the question and sometimes the answer** — so a row reading
`ANSWERED` is one whose recovered text happened to be the answering sentence, and a row reading
`untriaged` may be answered somewhere this merge did not look.

> **`untriaged` means "nobody has checked", not "open".** At least two ids below carry their original
> question text and are answered elsewhere in this run — `PROPOSED-repos2d-12` (Save/Load owns row 1,
> bit 21) and `PROPOSED-repos9e-13` (the 158 re-census) are both closed and both read `untriaged`.

**Marking them properly is triage and triage has not been done.** Deriving a status from prose and
presenting it as a state would be the status field asserting a check that never ran — the defect this
project has now corrected in four separate fields. **The column says which rows were recovered as
answers; it does not say which questions are open.**
