## Triage of the 97, 2026-09-03 — and the staging loss, measured

**Fifteen rows now carry a verdict instead of `untriaged`**, from a pass that read all 93 lines by
hand. **Roughly forty rows still have none** — Audio, PhyreEngine reflection and Input — and they are
staying blank on purpose: *"a triage by someone without the context would be exactly the unchecked
status field we have both spent the night arguing against."*

### Five were closed by work done during this run, and four are the same story

| id | verdict |
|---|---|
| `repos46-4` | **CLOSED** — nothing supplies the Y at generation; terrain probe at activation, gated on definition byte `+0x18` bit 4, world `0.0` on probe failure |
| `repos46-6` | **CLOSED, and the question's premise was wrong** — the mask is bits **45 and 49**, not 49 and 53 |
| `repos46-7` | **CLOSED** — not every zone (406 of 828) but **all 400 unit-defining and all 172 spawning scripts** |
| `repos46-2` | **CLOSED** by the movement-mode document, whose §2 gives both selectors' bit arithmetic |
| `repos46-9` | **SATISFIED** — the character render record array document exists and carries `passes: 1` |

> **Four questions were answered hours later by a session that never saw them.** repos-46 staged them
> as proposals; they did not reach this file; the answers landed in three different documents' §7 with
> nothing connecting them back. **That is the cost of the staging gap, measured rather than asserted** —
> and it is an argument for merging proposals promptly, not for merging them automatically.

`repos46-5` (the `0x80000003` status mask) is **genuinely open**: read in four documents this run and
never established.

### Four are VERIFIED OPEN, which `untriaged` could not express

`repos9e-2/-3/-4` were named explicitly as *not-cleared* in the batch-A glyph verdict; `repos94-1`
(which destructors folded onto `0016D6A0`) was touched by the thunk pass, which established the ICF
fold and its scale but cannot recover the source destructors. **Somebody looked and did not close them
— a different state from nobody having checked.**

### Two of the raiser's own rows have corrected premises

`reposd2-4` said *"the remaining 242 records"*; family 3 has 147, so the real remainder is **137 of
147**. `reposd2-8` is **half answered** — the slot-40 NULL is not a boundary the loader recognises
(`FUN_002DF9A0` registers its next base at 84); whether anything *above* the loader uses it is open.

**`reposec-1` and `reposec-13` are one question** about `02064AC4`; `-1`'s captured text is truncated,
which is probably why it survived as a separate row.

### Sixteen rows' captured text is not the question — and how that number was reached

`repos2d-6` · `repos78-3` · `repos78-6` · `repos94-18` · `repos94-19` · `repos9e-8` · `-9` · `-10` ·
`-11` · `-12` · `-13` · `-14` · `-17` · `reposd2-5` · `reposec-5` · `reposec-1`. Thirteen contain
their own id — the merge captured the sentence that *announced* the question. `repos9e-17`'s entire
text is `` (`PROPOSED-repos9e-17`). ``

> **A classifier said 30. Tightened, it said 29 — the same wrong answer**, because both versions
> counted a leading `document.md |` prefix as a fragment. **The right answer is 16, reached by reading
> all 93 lines.** Third instrument in one session to assert its own hypothesis, and **the cheapest fix
> was to stop using one on a list that short.**

**Every closure above names its evidence and where it lives, so any one of them can be rejected
individually rather than the set being accepted whole.**

Over the 47 shipped zero-arc paths (the census extension reproduces its own 423 / 3,942 / 15,350 / 1,682 control): `arc[-1].key`, the last segment's `+0x30` word, is 1.0 in all 47, and `arc[0].key` is the next record's header read as a float, a positive denormal below 1e-30. So `003CC890` returns 0.0 for a query at or below about 0 and 1.0 above 1.0, and for 0 < q <= 1 it skips the bisect (`r10d = m - 1 = -1`) and returns the float32 line through `arc[0]` and `arc[1]` - the next record's header and its start-vector floats. At q = 1 that gives -1.42 to 10.53 over the 47 (median 0.040): 37 inside [0, 1], 9 negative, 1 above 1, and none equal to 1.0. So a zero-arc path's remap is a line set by unrelated bytes, not the path's parameterisation, and it reaches the end parameter only by the > 1.0 clamp. The tail reads FOUR words past the table, not three - `arc[1].key` at `003CC939` as well. Not claimed: how often play queries such a path or what the camera shows. Control `_index/candidates/by6-zero-arc-paths/by6_check.py`. *Previous status, kept as history:* **NARROWED 2026-09-14 (OPUS) — the mechanism is fully read, and one half of the premise is corrected: `003CC6C0`'s read is IN BOUNDS.** Layout from the bytes: a segment is **0x38** bytes (`imul r9, rax, 0x38`, `rax = word[rec+4]` = segment count `n`), the arc table starts at `rec + 0x20 + 0x38n`, and an arc entry is an **8-byte pair** — key at `+0x00`, value at `+0x04`. `word[rec+6]` is `m`, the arc count. **`003CC6C0`:** index `= 7n + (m − 1)` with an 8-byte stride, so for `m = 0` it addresses `7n − 1` — **the last 8-byte word of the last segment, inside the record** — and multiplies `xmm1` by it. Not a fault; a defined read of the wrong field. **`003CC890` is a binary search with two clamps**, and it is the one that goes out of range: it reads `arc[0].key` at `003CC8A0` and returns **0.0** if that exceeds the query; then compares against `arc[m − 1].key`, and returns **1.0** (`01CEBBA8`) if the query exceeds it; otherwise bisects. For `m = 0` that is `arc[0]` (the first 8 bytes **past** the segment table), `arc[−1]` (in bounds, the last segment word), and in the degenerate tail `arc[0].value` and `arc[1].value` — **three reads past the table and one inside it**. So the pair is a distance→parameter remap clamped to [0, 1], and **a 0-arc path is not a handled special case — it is unguarded**, its result decided by whatever follows the segment table. **Still open, and it is a DATA question not a code one:** what those bytes are for the 47 zero-arc paths. That needs the shipped array-C buffer; the EXE cannot answer it, and nothing in these two bodies branches on `m = 0`. |

So bit 9 turns the camera's roll by the bone's third angle, and bit 10 adds the bone's second angle to the fov: the camera's roll and field of view can be animated through a bone's add-motion. Slot `k` is parameter `k mod 4` of oscillator `k div 4`: speed base, speed random range, amplitude base, amplitude random range. Each is a curve evaluated at the shake's time. Oscillators 0–2 are the eye offset in the camera's frame, 3–5 are added to them to give the look-at offset, 6 is roll and 7 is field of view. ## CB. The enemy definition record, the `.ard` join, and the stat rebuild — 2026-09-06 round

Merged 2026-09-07 by `xiionline-61` from `repos-1e`, `repos-3f`, `repos-c7`, `repos-c9` and
`repos-d6`. Program state throughout: **GN160**
`fa0db2933c988211ed4f3c76a7dbe3454fc95866745af4605c35177943d2f708`, re-verified 2026-09-07
(`explicit=38022 unresolved=139 pct=99.63575`).

**What the round achieved, so these questions read as the residue of a success and not a failure:**
the board's success condition was *"a modder can find a specific enemy and change what it is"*, and
at the start of the round **nobody could name one byte of a Marlboro's stats.** They can now. A
creature's Strength is the byte at definition-record `+0x2A`, and it is not stored — it is computed:

```
Strength = growth[+0x26] * (rec[+0x1C2] - rec[+0x88])  +  base[+0x26]  +  (s16)rec[+0x08]
           + every equipment and status contribution
           clamped to [0, 99]
```

`growth` is the row in the `.ard` table at registry slot `0x02EBF140`, `base` the row at
`0x02EBF148`, both reached from the `0x02EBF120` row that `rec[+0x004]` selects. The questions below
are what that decode left open.

| CE-1 | ~~26 family-0 records carry a `poll` callback and nothing else.~~ | | **ANSWERED 2026-09-07 — not an anomaly; it is what a wait looks like.** A `*sync` verb has **nothing to begin** (the thing it waits for was started by an *earlier* verb) and **nothing to return**, so it needs only the per-frame *"is it done yet?"* — exactly the `poll` slot. **Their polls do real work:** `gillwinsync`'s (`0034D4C0`) is the idiom in seven instructions — `call 0x2E2520; test eax,eax; sete cl` — keeping the wait alive while the subsystem reports unfinished, and a poll returns non-zero for *still running*, zero for *done*. All 26 are named `*sync` (`movesync`, `turnsync`, `movieplaysync`, `bgmstreamplaysync`…). Written up in [`../01-Script-VM-Native-Bridge/verbs-that-only-wait-and-verbs-that-do-nothing.md`](../01-Script-VM-Native-Bridge/verbs-that-only-wait-and-verbs-that-do-nothing.md). |
| CE-2 | **The one `-PR` record** — poll and result but no `begin` — classified `instantaneous` by the catalog. The second of the two residues in that cross-tabulation. An instantaneous command has no reason to own a poll callback. | same | **ANSWERED - propagated 2026-09-25 by FABLE (Claude Opus 5.5) from FABLE's CZ-1 answer of 2026-09-14 (scriptvm-verb-dispatch-and-parameter-encoding.md), which never reached this row; re-read before propagating.** The record is usemoviememory (0x297): the raw dispatch record at 01EED700+8+32*0x297 is {begin 0, poll 003473C0, +0x10 0, result 003477E0}. It is not instantaneous. With no begin, phase 0 goes straight to the poll, and 003473C0 returns running while byte 02ADD932 != 4 (0037B380). That byte is set to 4 by 0037B3D0, after arena 11's backing store is replaced, and by 0037B390. So the verb holds the script until the movie-memory switch completes, then runs its result (003DDC20(..., 1)). The catalog's 'instantaneous' label is the error. |

So the step is 30 or 60 frames and the lifetime is **1800 frames at 30 fps, 3600 at 60 fps — sixty seconds either way**, with five one-second blink steps. **The scalar exists precisely to hold wall-clock duration constant across frame rates**, which converts the seconds reading from an assumption into a consequence. |

## CR. Inert script verbs — 2026-09-07

From [`../01-Script-VM-Native-Bridge/verbs-that-only-wait-and-verbs-that-do-nothing.md`](../01-Script-VM-Native-Bridge/verbs-that-only-wait-and-verbs-that-do-nothing.md).

| CR-1 | ~~What does the interpreter do with an all-null command record?~~ | **ANSWERED 2026-09-07 — a silent no-op, guarded in the dispatcher itself, and it cannot hang.** `begin` null is **skipped** (`002622BF`); `poll` null substitutes the local zeroed at entry (`002621F7 mov dword [rsp+0x88], 0`), so `& 1` is false and the command reads as **finished**; `result` null takes **`00262360`**, which pushes tag `1` / kind `6` / value `0` onto the 63-entry result list and resets the phase byte to 0. **So `setnorecovertelepostatus`, `battlemembersync` and `restartbattle` complete on the first invocation and are safe to leave in a script.** The 63-entry bound **fails closed on the push and open on the completion** — at capacity the value is dropped but the command still finishes. **⚠ Most of this was already published when the question was filed.** `native-command-lifecycle.md` §2 already said *"where a callback is absent it takes an alternative path rather than failing"* and *"the absent `poll` yields 'not running' from a zeroed local"*. **The question should not have been filed without running `check_already_answered.py`, which is in the analysis kit for exactly this.** Genuinely new: the `00262360` branch, now §14. |

Published as corroboration, not as a new figure. **`+0x18`: NOTHING READS IT, which is new here.** An image-wide scan for the dword `0x01020304` finds **exactly one `.text` site, `0059E169`** - the immediate inside `0059E070`'s BOM test - and that validator reads `+0x08`, `+0x0C`, `+0x10`, `+0x14` and `+0x1C` in its size identity and **never touches `+0x18`**; `0059C180` byte-swaps it as one of the first eight words, but byte-ordering a word is not consuming it. It does not defeat this one, because the reflection registry records **which** classes it can construct. Of 404 classes carrying a Phyre descriptor instantiation, **331 have `PClassDescriptorConcrete<T>` and 38 have `PClassDescriptorWithoutDefaultConstructor<T>`, and the two sets do not intersect at all** — 0 of 369 — which is what makes them readable as the two alternatives rather than as unrelated templates. **`Phyre::PScripting::PScheduler` carries `Abstract`, `ForType` and `WithoutDefaultConstructor` — and no `Concrete`.** **CORROBORATED INDEPENDENTLY 2026-09-16 (FABLE), from a different population.** OPUS narrowed this row, so the claim it rests on should not be cleared by the same hand. I reached the descriptor set from the other side — **not** by counting descriptor instantiations, but by enumerating the **zero-at-load globals that CRT static initializers fill with an `.rdata` vtable** and resolving each one's RTTI ([the census](../00-Engine-Core-Runtime/Object-Model/members/zero-at-load-objects-named-by-rtti.tsv), built for `PH-2` before I had read this row's wording). **Three results, all matching.** `PClassDescriptorWithoutDefaultConstructor` has **exactly 38 distinct `T`** — OPUS's figure to the number. Its intersection with `PClassDescriptorConcrete` is **0**. And `PScheduler` appears in `WithoutDefaultConstructor` (`VPScheduler@PScripting@Phyre@@`, global `02E41370`) and **not** in `Concrete`. **What the corroboration does NOT cover, and the difference is real.** My population is smaller: **261 `Concrete`, against OPUS's 331**, because I count only descriptors written into zero-at-load globals, not every instantiation in the image. **So I reproduce the 38, the disjointness within my population, and the `PScheduler` verdict — I do not independently reproduce the 331.** The 70-descriptor gap is exactly the descriptors that live somewhere other than a zero-at-load global, and I did not chase them. *The row stays OPEN on its own terms* — this strengthens the reasoning that closed the reflection route; it says nothing about whether a chunk is ever executed. For contrast, `PPostProcessing::PFXAA`, a class the engine does instantiate, carries `Concrete`. So the scheduler **cannot be default-constructed through reflection**, and the row's remaining route is explicit construction by code — whose only site, `00680D80`, is itself a vtable slot with no direct callers. **The bound, stated:** `WithoutDefaultConstructor` names the absence of a DEFAULT constructor; a reflected factory taking arguments would not be excluded by it, and `PScheduler` does carry `PMethodCallerConcrete` bindings for two of its methods, so it is reachable *as an object* once one exists. This narrows how it could come to exist; it does not prove none ever does. **The breakpoint on `00684D10` is still the answer, and this is still an ASTRA row.** *Narrowed 2026-09-18 (FABLE), from the data side:* **no shipped asset declares a scripting class.** The image registers four - `PScheduler`, `PScript`, `PScriptCallbackHandler`, `PScriptableComponent` (the registrar join, [phyre-registrar-classes.tsv](../22-Middleware-PhyreEngine/Reflection-And-Class-Metadata/members/phyre-registrar-classes.tsv)) - and the corpus census of all 35,984 shipped `.phyre` clusters ([the packed-namespace page](../22-Middleware-PhyreEngine/Phyre-Asset-Container/the-packed-namespace-and-the-file-side-schema.md)) finds 177 declared class names, none of them one of the four and none containing `Script`, `Sched`, `Lua` or `Caller`. A cluster instantiates only classes its own table declares, so the reflection route - the one way a scheduler or a script object could come to exist without a direct constructor call, and the only kind of route the static trace could not follow - has nothing to instantiate in the shipped game. *Bound:* a native caller that asks the `PScheduler` descriptor for an instance through a virtual slot would not show here; the descriptor's other references are all inside the scripting module itself. The live check stays the decider; the static-plus-data weight is now against a scheduler ever existing. | **SUPERSEDED 2026-09-26 (FABLE, Claude Opus 5.5) under the runtime rule (a runtime-only row closes SUPERSEDED when its claim is already tier-1 static): the static bound is enumerated on both supplier sides: no .lua ships, and no code outside the scripting module and the CRT init/teardown holds either supplier descriptor. Whether a chunk ever runs is one live breakpoint (00684D10), not queued.** *Previous status, kept as history:* OPEN *Bound corrected and enumerated 2026-09-22 (FABLE), same day as the answer above.* **The answer stands; the stated escape route did not.** A caller needs no reference to `00680D80` - it needs the DESCRIPTOR, and can reach slot 10 virtually, which is exactly the bound `DA-1` records. **So who holds the descriptor is now enumerated.** It is a static object at **`02E41370`**, built at boot by CRT initializer `00166140` (zero callers; its single stored pointer is `.rdata` `008C41E0`, inside the initializer table) and destroyed at exit by `008B2300` (26 B - vptr swap to `00D6F120`, then `jmp 00633390`; zero callers, `atexit`-registered). **`02E41370` has NINETEEN referencing sites and not one belongs to the game:** two are that initializer, two are that teardown, and the remaining fifteen are all inside the scripting module itself - `00680950` x2, `00681F30` x6, `006836B0`, `00683DC0`, `00683F70`, `00685810`, `006858C0`, `006859E0`, `00685FB0`. *The two that look like exceptions to `DA-1`s "all inside the scripting module" are the CRTs own teardown, not a consumer.* **So no code outside the scripting module and the CRTs init/teardown ever holds the descriptor, and the scripting modules own entries are the ones nothing reaches.** *Enumeration completed 2026-09-22 (FABLE) - the step the previous append named is now done, and it comes out the same way.* **`PClassCallableMethodScript`s descriptor is the static object `02E41070`**, built at boot by CRT initializer `00166100` (one stored pointer, `.rdata` `008C41C8`, inside the initializer table; it calls the base constructor `006812B0`, which stamps `PClassDescriptorAbstract<...>` `00D6EB70`, then overwrites the vptr with `PClassDescriptorWithoutDefaultConstructor<...>` `00D6EBF8` - the ordinary base-then-derived shape, which is why the Abstract vtable has only that one code reference) and destroyed at exit by `008B22E0`. **`02E41070` has THIRTEEN referencing sites and not one belongs to the game:** two the initializer, two the teardown, and nine inside the scripting module - `00680440`, `00680520`, `00681D80` x5, `00683580`, `00683D30`. **So both supplier classes now have the same enumerated bound:** `PScheduler`s descriptor `02E41370` has 19 sites (2 init, 2 teardown, 15 scripting module) and `PClassCallableMethodScript`s `02E41070` has 13 (2 init, 2 teardown, 9 scripting module). **No code outside the scripting module and the CRTs own init/teardown ever holds EITHER descriptor**, so the only callers that could ask for an instance are inside the module whose own entry points nothing reaches. *`DA-1`s bound is now enumerated on both sides rather than stated; what remains outside it is a live observation, which is what that row has always said.* |
| DA-2 | ~~What does `PUtilityScripting` do at construction?~~ | **ANSWERED 2026-09-08 — it registers, it does not interpret.** `00166210` walks a priority-ordered intrusive list headed at `02CACC90` (ordered on a `+0x18` field while `< 0xFF`), splices in a **statically allocated** `PUtilityScripting` at `01F2EAC8`, writes its vtable `00D6FD98`, and tail-calls **`atexit`**. **No `lua_State` is created.** That list is a **subsystem registry — 33 static initialisers register into it, 64 references in all** — so the scripting module simply takes its place among thirty-two others before `main`. **⚠ This corrected an overstatement made the same day**: the owning document had said *"there is a live Lua interpreter in the process"*. ## DB. The subsystem registry — 2026-09-08

From [`../22-Middleware-PhyreEngine/Subsystem-Map/the-fifteen-modules-registered-before-main.md`](../22-Middleware-PhyreEngine/Subsystem-Map/the-fifteen-modules-registered-before-main.md).

| ID | Question | Status |
|---|---|---|
| DB-1 | **`PUtilityText` breaks the pattern.** Its registrar installs into `02E5BE50` and its destructor into `02E5BE88`, **`0x38` apart**, where the other fourteen modules use one address for both. It is also the only object outside the `01F2Cxxx`–`01F47xxx` band. Either it is a larger object whose `PUtility` base sub-object sits at `+0x38`, or the ctor/dtor pairing is not what it appears to be. | **ANSWERED 2026-09-14 (FABLE): no 0x38 offset — both installers use `02E5BE88`.** `00167B90` constructs the object at `02E5BE88` through `006CCC10` (base `PUtility` vtable `00D26BC0`, key `0xFF`, name "Text", chain insertion, derived vtable `00D89C68` = `PUtilityText`) and registers `008B6F00`, which unlinks the same address. `02E5BE50`–`02E5BE80` is a seven-pointer table of `0x20`-byte slots the constructor fills first. BSS placement is a declaration difference. [fifteen modules](../22-Middleware-PhyreEngine/Subsystem-Map/the-fifteen-modules-registered-before-main.md). |
| DB-2 | ~~What the two walkers do.~~ | **ANSWERED 2026-09-08 — the registry is a lifecycle manifest, walked exactly twice per run, not a per-frame dispatch table.** **`005A08E0` is engine init**: it walks the chain calling each module's vtable slot **`+0x08`**, and **a non-zero return aborts the whole startup** — every module after the failing one is never initialised. **`005A0840` is engine shutdown**: it walks calling slot **`+0x10`** and **ignores the return** (failing to start is fatal, failing to stop is not). Both are guarded by one flag at `02CACCA0` and so are idempotent; init allocates a `0xE0`-byte object at `01F3F5B8` and **registers the shutdown with `atexit`**, so the teardown walk runs at process exit rather than from game code. **The module lifecycle contract is therefore: `+0x00` shared and unread (`DB-5`), `+0x08` init, `+0x10` shutdown.** *The ledger tags both walkers `UtilityThreadPoolOrchestration`; nothing in either body is thread-pool work, and the document declines that tag.* |
| DB-3 | ~~What `node[+0x18]` means.~~ | **ANSWERED 2026-09-08, in the same block that filed it — it is `0xFF` in all fourteen readable module objects.** The insertion loop walks *while* the key is `< 0xFF`, so `jae` fires on the first node and **every module splices at the head**; the final chain is the reverse of CRT initializer order. **The ordering mechanism exists and the shipped data does not exercise it.** *(`PUtilityText`'s object is in BSS and has no image value — see `DB-1`.)* **What the key would mean if something set it lower is still unknown — `DB-4`.** |

So `[0] != 1` always holds, every binding is polled, and the mode-3 forced-neutral axis path never runs. `00228480` (widget `01FD4948` present) is consulted only when the field is 1. A writer in unlisted code is not excluded. [binding profiles](../15-Input/Binding-Profiles/binding-profiles-remapping-and-control-state.md). |
| DC-3 | **`008F3A28` = 120.0** is loaded into a register on every iteration of the first loop and **used on no path read in this pass.** Either a deadzone for a branch not reached in this reading, or a hoisted load for a part of the 1,406-byte body beyond the three modes. **Reported as a loose end rather than guessed at.** | **ANSWERED 2026-09-14 (FABLE): `WHEEL_DELTA`, for a fourth binding mode that reads the mouse wheel.** The load at `00197253` is hoisted; its only use is `00197383`, in the second loop's mode-4 arm (modes 1/2/3/4 dispatch at `001972A0`). For code 3 that arm reads channel 3 of the mouse device (backend `+0x150`), divides by 120.0 into whole notches, and accumulates them at input manager `+0x0C` with the frame value at `+0x10` (`00196480`). The channel-3 = wheel reading rests on the constant and the notch arithmetic. [binding profiles](../15-Input/Binding-Profiles/binding-profiles-remapping-and-control-state.md). |

It writes records **2, 3, 4** at `01DF1738`, never 0 and 1, and sets `mgr[+0x3B]` — the dirty flag `00196FF0` consumes. **Group 2's four slots are never published** (the read span covers 24 of 28 dwords). See [CONTRACT-binding-profiles.md](../15-Input/Binding-Profiles/CONTRACT-binding-profiles.md) §7a. | ANSWERED |
| DD-2 | ~~The stride between the five banked records at `01DF1480`.~~ \| **ANSWERED — and it was already answered when it was filed.** The stride is **`0x15C` (348 B)**, against a record the translator reads as `0x140`, leaving **`0x1C` bytes per record it never touches**. Now derived **four independent ways**: the keymap page's `01DF1738 = 01DF1480 + 2 × 0x15C` and its `5 × 0x15C` bank sizing (both predating this question's filing); the poll loop's own three `add reg, 0x15C` increments at `001970BB` / `001970EB` / `00197110`, which need no second address at all; and the CRT initializer `0015BD30`, read by the static-initialization page as *"three records of stride `0x15C`"*. See [CONTRACT-binding-profiles.md](../15-Input/Binding-Profiles/CONTRACT-binding-profiles.md) §7. | ANSWERED |
| DD-3 | ~~Which is right about `00195DF0`: `T-7`, or the reference map?~~ \| **ANSWERED 2026-09-08 — `T-7` was right in every particular, and the map was blind.** `00195DF0` does `lea r15, [rip-0x75e23]` → **the image base**, then addresses every global as `[r15 + disp]`; a RIP-relative scan sees only the `lea` itself. The signal was in the map's own output — `00120000` was listed among the function's three references and read as noise. **Measured blind spot:** 636 of 38,161 functions (**1.67 %**) use an image-base register, carrying **2,027** references over **1,054** globals; **103 of the 150** globals written that way show **no writer** in the RIP map, and **870 of 1,054** are absent from it entirely. Closed by the new `imagebase_refs.py`. | ANSWERED |

Type: `InputManager` ([`opus-input-manager-type.md`](candidates/opus-input-manager-type.md)). |
| IB-1 | ~~Which database conclusions rest on the RIP map's image-base blind spot?~~ \| **ANSWERED 2026-09-08 — swept, and the realised damage is nil.** `check_global_claims.py` checks every writer claim in the prose against **both** instruments, distinguishing absolute claims from ones correctly scoped by function, by instrument, by condition, or by *what* is written. Over **295 documents and 107,982 lines** (excluding `_inbox/` and the append-only `_index/` logs) it reports **0 surviving contradictions**, with its control passing. The exposure was real — **103 globals** carry a writer only the image-base instrument can see — but of the two conclusions actually drawn from it, one was corrected by `DD-1`/`DD-3` and the other (`022D94B0`) had **already been overturned by its own document's §21**. The sweep also *added* a fact: **`0036E3B0`, named nowhere in the database, writes the `022D94B0` descriptor table** through an image-base register. | ANSWERED |
| IB-2 | **A third addressing pattern the reference map cannot see: a LITERAL data base held in a register, then arithmetically indexed.** `022D94B0`'s own §21 found it by hand — `0036E320` and `0036E540` `lea` the literal base and *"index it by the clamped slot"* — so the register is **modified between the `lea` and the write**. A pattern-matching scanner cannot follow that: a prototype built for this block **failed its positive control on `0036E320`**, the very function the document names, and was not shipped. **This needs real dataflow, not pattern matching**, and its population is unmeasured. The database has now been bitten by this class twice (`DD-1`, `022D94B0`). | **ANSWERED 2026-09-14 (OPUS) — the population is measured, and the instrument passes the control the prototype failed.** `check_literal_base_access.py` (kit) propagates a **taint** instead of matching a pattern: a register derived from a literal data base stays derived through `lea`, `add`, `sub`, `imul`, `shl`, `and`, `or`, `inc`, `dec`, `movsxd` and a register copy, loses the derivation when something unrelated is written into it, and drops the volatiles at every `call`; the walk stops at the owning function's end. That is the dataflow this row said the question needed. **Positive control PASS** — both `0036E320` and `0036E540` appear, on base `022D94B0`, the two functions `022D94B0` §21 found by hand and the exact case the earlier prototype missed; the tool **exits non-zero and says the run is not evidence** if they do not. **The population: 4,458 sites in 1,217 functions — 1,565 writes and 2,893 reads.** Scoped to `022D94B0` alone it is **48 sites in 13 functions**, all in the contiguous band `0036DDC0`–`0036E8B0`, so §21's two were part of a thirteen-function family. Only an access whose base was **modified since the `lea`** or which carries a **scaled index** counts — a plain `[base + constant]` is what a reference map already sees, and counting it would have inflated the number with the cases that are not the question. **This is a population, not a defect list:** most of the 4,458 are ordinary table walks that happen to be invisible to one instrument. The largest single holder is `WorldActorScriptVM_InterpretBytecode` with 234 sites on one base. |

## EE. Group completion and respawn timing — 2026-09-08

Owned by [`../05-Spawn-Encounter-Lifecycle/Group-Completion-And-Respawn/when-a-group-is-wiped-and-when-it-comes-back.md`](../05-Spawn-Encounter-Lifecycle/Group-Completion-And-Respawn/when-a-group-is-wiped-and-when-it-comes-back.md).

| ID | Question | Status |
|---|---|---|
| EE-1 | **SHARPENED 2026-09-08 — a static instrument cannot answer this, and here is why.** Each of the three record accessors has **exactly one caller and it is a VM verb wrapper** (`00235F50`→`0050F660`, `00235FB0`→`0050FAB0`, `002366E0`→`005101F0`), verified on four instruments with positive controls: `E8` 1, `E9` 0, code memory-operand 0 for each. **No native function reads more than one of them**, so nothing native relates the cooldown to the elapsed seconds. **The unit is a script-side convention**, and settling it needs the authored script or a runtime observation. ## FE. The battle stats record field map — 2026-09-10

Owned by [`../08-Combat-Formula/Battle-Stats-Record/the-battle-stats-record-field-map.md`](../08-Combat-Formula/Battle-Stats-Record/the-battle-stats-record-field-map.md).

Bit 0 is the battle-member lock; bit 2 makes a party member be driven like a non-party unit. Bit 2's writers store through the record passed to them: [rdi] at 0023AF28 in BattleStats_InitializeDefinitionRecord, and [rbx] at 00239D89 / 00239D94 in the area-state party walk. That is why a +0x698 sweep cannot see them. The designer's name for bit 2 is intent, not this question.** *Previous status, kept as history:* **PARTIAL 2026-09-14 (FABLE, corrected the same day)** — a flags word: bit 0 the battle-member lock; bit 2 makes a party member take the non-party AI order set and stay AI-navigable as the focus, defaulted from party row `+0x2C` bit 6; ~~no other bit has a reader~~ ~~— wrong: `00308040` reads bits 3/5/6 (`00308075`, `0030807E`) and `003125E0` bits 3/4 (`003126C0`, `003126C8`); what bits 1 and 3–6 mean is open~~ — **that correction is itself withdrawn 2026-09-14 (OPUS): those four instructions are on `[unit + 0x6A0]`, the spawn-keep entry, and the bits are `AL-10`, answered. `no other bit has a reader` was right, and is now stronger — no other bit is touched at all on this path. See the enumeration below**  **EXTENDED 2026-09-14 (OPUS), then CORRECTED by OPUS the same day — the enumeration was wrong and so was FABLE's correction of it.** The record is `qword [unit + 0x698]`. A register-binding sweep that kills a binding on redefinition, follows a `mov rD, rS` copy and stops at the owning function's end finds **five instructions in four functions, on two bits**: `00328FD5` / `00328FDE` set and clear **bit 0** (`FUN_00328FB0`, `setbattlememberlock`), `00328E5B` reads bit 0 in the roster reconcile, and `00305BFB` and `0030BCE9` read **bit 2**. **No other bit is touched at all.** The census is of the `+0x698` access path — every instruction reaching the word through a pointer loaded from `[unit + 0x698]` in the same function. **CORROBORATED INDEPENDENTLY 2026-09-16 (FABLE), by a deliberately BROADER sweep.** I re-derived the binding sweep from scratch and ran it over **every listed body that references displacement `+0x698` at all — 301 functions, 635 references** — rather than only battle-unit ones, on the principle that a wider net that still catches exactly the same five is worth more than a repeat of the same scope. **It found 5 of 5**, at the same addresses, and the claim stands on two independent derivations. **The one extra site it surfaced is a displacement coincidence, and naming it is the point.** `001CC348` (`mov dword ptr [rcx], eax`) writes a **whole dword** through a pointer loaded from `[rbx + 0x698]`, which would be a second writer and would contradict this row's *one enumerated writer*. It is not one: the owning body `001CA600` registers `mScrollListHeight`, `mCommandTitleFontHeight`, `mGambitPositionOffsetX`, `mCursorRightX` and some twenty more of the same family, so its `rbx + 0x698` is the **UI layout-parameter block**, a different structure that happens to carry a pointer at the same offset. *(That is the base-register trap: the displacement suggests a structure and the base register decides it.)* **And the sweep was wrong twice before it was right, which is why its negative is only worth something now.** First pass found **0 of 5** — it killed a register binding whenever the register appeared as a first operand, and `test rax, rax` one instruction after `mov rax, [rax+0x698]` therefore dropped every binding immediately; fixed by killing only what `regs_access()` reports as written. Second pass found 5 of 5 **plus a false positive** at `00305EC8`, where the binding had survived the `call` at `00305EB2` — `rax` there is the call's return value, not the record pointer — fixed by killing the volatile registers across every `CALL`. **Neither gap is mentioned in this row's description of the original sweep** (*“kills a binding on redefinition, follows a `mov rD, rS` copy, stops at the owning function's end”*); OPUS's result does not contain `00305EC8`, so its implementation evidently handled the call case, but anyone re-running a binding sweep in this database should assume both traps are there. The record has two other homes the sweep cannot see (the kind-`0` battle-state array element `*(02EBF190) + 8 + slot×0x1C8`, and `spawnkeep + 0x80` for kind `1`), which is where `UQ-123`'s bit-2 writers have to be. *Withdrawn:* the bit-1 writer `00233BA8`, the bit-5 writer `00237DD7` and the readers `00308073` and `003126BE` — all four load `[unit + 0x698]`, test the kind byte, then load **`[unit + 0x6A0]` into the same register** and do the bit work on that second record. **That record is already identified**: `unit + 0x6A0` is the **spawn-keep entry** (`SpawnRecord`, `0x250` B; `+0x698` is that entry `+0x80` on the kind-`1` path and **NULL at `+0x6A0`** on the kind-`0` path, which is why all four test the kind byte first), and its word `+0x00` is **`AL-10`, answered 2026-09-12**: bit 1 is `ACTIVATION_COMMITTED` — set by `BattleUnit_ActivateAppliedDefinitionRuntime`, the very function whose `or …,2` was read as an `FE-1` bit-1 writer — and bit 5 is category-4 mode. So FABLE's *bits 3, 4, 5 and 6 are read* was reading **answered spawn-lifecycle bits as unexplained stats-record bits**. The earlier sweep never killed the binding on redefinition, so it carried one record's name onto another's contents. FABLE's 2026-09-14 correction reading bits 3–6 into this word rests on the same four instructions and is withdrawn with them. Both bit-2 readers gate on kind byte `0`, so this is a **party-arm word**, which is why FABLE's bit-2 reading holds structurally. **Still open:** bit 2 has no writer through this pointer, so `UQ-123`'s displacement-0 writers must reach the record some other way — a displacement-0 store through a `+0x698` pointer is precisely what this sweep does see. |

There is a fourth, and it is the one that decides these six ranges: **a 16-byte SSE store carries ONE displacement and covers SIXTEEN offsets**, so every offset inside a block store but outside any scalar store reads as untouched to a scalar census. *(The same shape refuted `AL-8`'s “49 never written” earlier today, with a witness.)* **Measured by overlapping byte range across every store in the listed bodies**, scalar against block (≥ 8 bytes): `+0x21`–`+0x23` **6,746 scalar / 11,533 block**; `+0x45`–`+0x47` **803 / 6,222**; `+0x4F` **615 / 3,354**; `+0x60`–`+0x63` **1,115 / 2,706**; `+0x89`–`+0xBB` **4,457 / 4,350**; `+0x1C3`–`+0x1C7` **124 / 102**. **At every one of the six, the shape the scan cannot see is as common as the shape it can, and at three of them it is three to eight times commoner.** **What this is NOT.** These counts are **displacement-generic across every structure in the image** and attribute **nothing** to this record — a store at `+0x45` belongs to whatever its base register points at, which this measurement does not resolve. | FR-1 | **Which codecs the `.webm` loader accepts**, and which library plays the 40 movies (10,377 MiB, EBML magic on all sampled). Narrowed 2026-09-11: the player is `001B7F30` → `0067A480` (1920 × 1080) with the image's own Matroska parser (`00801210`–`00806F20`), libvpx's VP8 decoder 1.6.0 (`01CEB698`, `0016ECE0` / `0016F450`) and the sound layer's Ogg Vorbis path; no codec-id string exists, so the rejection of another codec is the remainder. **THE REMAINDER IS ANSWERED 2026-09-16 (FABLE): THERE IS NO REJECTION, BECAUSE THE PARSER NEVER READS THE CODEC.** Swept the 63 listed bodies in `00801210`–`00806F20` for compares against known EBML element ids. **Ten of fourteen are compared** — `Segment` `0x18538067`, `Tracks` `0x1654AE6B`, `TrackEntry` `0xAE`, `Cluster` `0x1F43B675` (nine sites), `SimpleBlock` `0xA3` (four), `Block` `0xA1`, `PixelWidth` `0xB0`, `PixelHeight` `0xBA`, `Channels` `0x9F`, `SamplingFrequency` `0xB5`. **`CodecID` `0x86` is compared nowhere in the span.** *Control, because this is an absence:* the same sweep finds the **four-byte** ids, `Cluster` alone nine times, so it demonstrably sees what it is looking for and `CodecID`'s absence is not a blind spot. *And image-wide:* the only two `cmp …, 0x86` in any listed body are not EBML — `001D5CC5` is a **loop bound** (`inc r13d` / `cmp r13d, 0x86` / `jl` back to `001D5C40`), and the other decodes inside a misaligned stream. **So the question *which codecs does the loader accept* has the answer: it accepts whatever the container structurally holds, and hands the payload to a hardcoded VP8 decoder.** A non-VP8 track is not rejected — **it is fed to VP8.** There is no negotiation, no codec table and no failure path for the wrong codec, which is also **why the codec-id string this row went looking for does not exist**: the element is never read, so no name for it was ever needed. **A second absence, and it explains how tracks are told apart:** `TrackType` `0x83` and `TrackNumber` `0xD7` are **also never compared**. So the parser distinguishes a video track from an audio one **by which sub-elements its `TrackEntry` contains** — `PixelWidth` and `PixelHeight` against `Channels` and `SamplingFrequency` — rather than by any declared type. *(Stated as the reading the compare-set supports; no track-dispatch body was read line by line.)* | **ANSWERED 2026-09-26 (FABLE, Claude Opus 5.5): status restated; the codec half was answered on 2026-09-16 (there is no acceptance test) and the library is libvpx 1.6.0. Behaviour on a malformed container is outside the question as asked.** *Previous status, kept as history:* OPEN — **the codec half is answered: there is no acceptance test. What remains of this row is only the `.webm` loader's behaviour on a malformed container, which nobody has provoked** |

| PA-5 |  What the 13 inherited slots do, i.e. what behaviour FFXII takes from the middleware unchanged.  [`../22-Middleware-PhyreEngine/Application-Framework-Boundary/the-game-is-a-phyre-application.md`](../22-Middleware-PhyreEngine/Application-Framework-Boundary/the-game-is-a-phyre-application.md) §7 *Narrowed 2026-09-14 (FABLE): slot 28 `0079C140` is the inherited per-frame update; the window procedure calls slots 14 / 17 / 20; slots 11 / 26 / 27 are empty; 1, 12, 13, 18, 19, 29, 30 unread (the Phyre application page §7).* **THE SEVEN ARE READ — 2026-09-16 (FABLE), and four of them share one convention.** **Four slots are the same shape: record the request, store the arguments, return 0.** **Slot 12** `007A0B10` (17 B) sets `byte[this+0x20] = 1` and `byte[this+0x1E] = 1`, then stores its argument at `byte[this+0xD20]`. **Slot 13** `0079F140` (10 B) sets `byte[this+0x21] = 1` and stores its argument at `byte[this+0x26]`. **Slot 18** `007A1180` (14 B) sets `byte[this+0x29] = 1` and stores **two** arguments at `dword[this+0x2C]` and `dword[this+0x30]`. **Slot 19** `007A0AF0` (17 B) is the consume side of the same idea: if `byte[this+0x23]` is zero it sets `byte[this+0x22] = 1`, otherwise it clears `byte[this+0x23]`. **So what FFXII takes unchanged here is a DEFERRED-REQUEST convention.** None of the four does the thing asked of it. Each sets a distinct flag byte — `0x20`, `0x21`, `0x29`, `0x22` — parks the parameters beside it, and returns success immediately. **The work happens later, wherever those flags are consumed.** That is a real behavioural inheritance rather than a list of addresses: **the game's application object answers *yes, noted* and defers**, because the framework's own implementation does. **Slot 1** `0079F9E0` (31 B) is different and simpler: a **composite initialiser**, four straight calls to `007943E0`, `00794E80`, `00795590`, `00795320`, then `xor eax, eax` and return. **Slots 29 and 30 return framework status codes**: `007A08A0` (65 B) returns **9** when `byte[this+0x69]` is set before testing `dword[this+0x64]`; `0079E880` (792 B) returns **`0x13`** when `qword[this+0xD98]` is null. **A non-zero return here is a Phyre status, not a value** — which is why the four request-recorders all end `xor eax, eax`. **And the 13 inherited slots reproduce exactly**: 1, 11, 12, 13, 17, 18, 19, 20, 26, 27, 28, 29, 30, confirmed by comparing `GameApplication`'s vtable at `008C5760` against `PApplication`'s at `01CB2508` entry by entry. Slots 11 and 27 are `005C5230` and slot 26 is `_guard_check_icall` — **the three the page calls *empty*, which is right: they are the framework's own no-op and guard stubs, inherited because there was nothing to override.** *Partial reads, stated.* **Slots 29 and 30 are read at their prologues only** — the precondition and its status code — not to their ends; slot 30 is 792 bytes. And I have the flag offsets the four recorders write, **not their consumers**, so *the work happens later* is the shape of the convention and not a traced path. | **ANSWERED 2026-09-26 (FABLE, Claude Opus 5.5): every inherited slot now has a behaviour. The four request recorders are consumed by slot 28's per-frame update. Slot 12 (+0x20, +0xD20) is the full-screen / window switch at +0xD24/+0xD28. Slot 19 (+0x22) re-checks the monitor mode. Slot 13 (+0x21, +0x26) is the focus callback, ShowWindow restore or minimise. Slot 18 (+0x29, +0x2C/+0x30) is a resize. Read to their ends, slot 29 is the input-playback step (frame counter +0x64, reader 0079BDF0) and slot 30 the input recorder ("%d:%s:%s:+:%d" lines written to the +0xD98 stream). EC7-35's parser label for 0079E880 corrected. Control _index/candidates/pa5-inherited-slots/inherited_slots.py (7 checks); consumer check beside it.** *Previous status, kept as history:* OPEN |

Its callers are the two transition paths that put a screen over a still of the field: `00229510` from the area controller's message-18 arm (the plain field transition), which tests request kinds 2, 8, 16 and 22 (`00229534`..`00229576`), and `00228930`, which reads the router context `0209AC30` and tests kind 16 (`0022897F`). `btlctrl.src`, `c:/plan_work/jp/event/header/systemctrl.ath`, `mapctrl_mj.src`, `g_com_debug_flag` ...), the first and third are `u32` offset arrays (7 and 64 entries), and the body from `+0x30` is a further offset array over records that carry the element names `global_flag[0]`..`global_flag[510]` (511 in every file) and the headers' globals: 2,023 to 3,093 identifiers per file, of which 43 to 71 are declared in the `.sbn` text and 167 to 245 mentioned there; |---|---|---|
| MA-1 | **What the `.adm` fields mean.** | **ANSWERED 2026-09-24 (SWE2-DATA); domain closed 2026-09-26** — full disassembly of `003714A0` + re-walk of all 3,553 records ([the .adm tables](../17-Presentation-Rendering/Model-And-Motion-Formats/adm-add-motion-tables.md) §10): a record is `{i32 bone; f32 eulerDeg[3]; f32 offset[3]}` — the first triple is **degrees**, lerped between the selected group and the next, scaled ×π/180 (constants `180.0` / `3.1415927` read from `.rdata`) into `Matrix4x4f_BuildEulerRotation`; authored range ±195° confirms. The second triple spans ±0.133 — magnitude only, no unit established — and is **dead-to-TZA within the enumerated accessor domain**: the `.adm` registry `0x1F81250` is reachable only via getter `001BE420` (five callers audited — four touch only its `+0x20` flag; `00863110` does the name lookup), `001BE430`'s only inbound ref is `00863110` under all four instruments, the handles land only at `+0x6E8`/`+0x6F0`, and an image-wide type-discriminated operand census of those slots finds `003714A0` the sole record-walker — reading `+0x00`/`+0x04`..`+0x0F`, never `+0x10`..`+0x1B`. The group header is a keyframe: track `field01` picks which of its float lanes is the driven scalar (0/1/2 → group `+0`/`+4`/`+8`), track `field02` is the channel id passed to `004776D0`, and `field00` picks the selection mode — `0` = key-interpolate between bracketing groups, `1` = match group `+0x18` id against the live pose-slot value (the 35 kind-1 tracks are exactly track 0 of the four-track files, and alone populate `+0x18` values 1/2/3). Index tables key on group 0 because records are parallel keyframes of the same bone list. Bone indices are unbounded at `00371711` but authored max is 84, no negatives, in all 3,553 records. `_town` = the civilian variant picked by combat flag `00377C20` + `0017FFB0` override per §3. **Residual:** the second triple's intended semantics (a consumer would have to reach records outside the enumerated domain) and the group header's non-lane floats. |

| UC-2 | **Are the 63 statically unreferenced head blocks dead, or entered by an address built at run time?** Settled as far as static evidence goes: **the base relocation table holds 114,962 DIR64 entries, 110 of which store a value in the window, and all 110 land on a listed body while none lands in any of the 66 blocks** - so no pointer to this code exists anywhere in the image. Only 3 of 66 are reachable by any chain of direct branches. **TESTED AGAINST TWO SHAPES A DIR64 CENSUS CANNOT SEE — 2026-09-16 (FABLE). One strengthens the claim; the other qualifies the headline figure.** *No pointer to this code exists anywhere in the image* was derived from the **base relocation table**, which records only **absolute addresses that need relocating**. Two ordinary pointer forms carry no relocation entry at all, so neither was covered. **(1) PC-relative address-taking — and it agrees.** `lea reg, [rip + disp]` produces a code pointer with **no relocation entry whatsoever**. Censused over **every listed body**: **zero** land in any unlisted gap of the head window. **That is a real strengthening** — the one shape most likely to hide a reference finds nothing either. **(2) Unwind metadata, which nobody had looked at.** `.pdata` is the x64 exception directory: **35,713 `RUNTIME_FUNCTION` records**, each the linker asserting a real function with prologue/epilogue metadata. **408 of them begin inside the head window, and 407 land on a listed body.** The unlisted regions have **essentially no unwind records** — which is **positive evidence for the leading reading**, because hand-written SIMD leaf kernels that never touch the stack or call out need none. The row calls that reading *not proven*; this is evidence for it that does not come from the version banner or the neighbourhood. **AND THE ONE EXCEPTION QUALIFIES THE BYTE FIGURE.** The single `.pdata` entry landing in a gap, `00124BFC`–`00124C18`, is **not code**: it is an **MSVC switch jump table** — seven 4-byte RVAs `4A4B`, `4A61`, `4A78`, `4AB5`, `4AF1`, `4B16`, `4B3C`, all resolving back into the window a few hundred bytes earlier, followed by `CC` padding. **So the gap accounting includes bytes that are data, not code**, and **`150,568 bytes turn on it` is an upper bound on code, not a measurement of it.** How much is jump tables and alignment nobody has measured; the instrument is to subtract every RVA-table run and every `CC` fill from the gaps before quoting a figure. *A dead route recorded so nobody repeats it.* I first tried to find pointers by scanning every 4-byte dword in the image for a value in the window's RVA range. It returned **493,474 hits**, 458,700 of them in `.rdata`. **That census is unsound**: an RVA in this window is an ordinary small integer between `0x1000` and `0x40000`, and `.rdata` is full of sizes and offsets. **A test that cannot tell a pointer from an integer is not a test**, and its number means nothing. `.pdata`, with its fixed 12-byte stride and explicit semantics, is the sound instrument. **Retained-but-unreachable, at object-file granularity, is the leading reading and is not proven**; the discriminator is that a run-time CPU-dispatch table would reference every variant, and what is measured is a clean split between referenced kernels and unreferenced ones. 150,568 bytes turn on it. *Narrowed 2026-09-18 (FABLE): the code side is now exhausted; the data side cannot be, and the reading stands.* The relocation-table argument covers absolute pointers only. Two mechanisms it does not cover were swept: **rip-relative operands and direct branches** — every instruction of every listed body (34,270) was decoded and every rip-relative target and every `call` / `jmp` immediate tested against the 66 head blocks (`00121E11`–`0015AE52`, 177,977 bytes): **zero hits**, so no listed code takes a head block's address with `lea`, reads from one, or branches into one; and **image-relative 32-bit tables**, which need no relocation — a scan of the data sections finds 73,248 runs of four or more consecutive `.text`-range dwords, which is the numeric tables of a game image and not a jump-table population, so a value scan cannot separate an RVA table from data here and is reported as uninformative rather than as evidence. A 64-bit scan of the data sections against the image base finds 143 qwords equal to an in-window address, every one a round multiple of `0x10000` (`0x130000`, `0x140000`, `0x150000`) with non-pointer neighbours: constants, not pointers, and consistent with the relocation table's zero. One `.pdata` entry, `00124BFC`–`00124C18`, sits inside block `00124BFB` (29 bytes) — an unwind record, not a reference, and banned as existence evidence under pass 6. So the only entry left for the 63 is an address built by arithmetic or read from a table indistinguishable from data; retained-but-unreachable stays the leading reading, now against the code side too. Static: two whole-image sweeps with the listed bodies as positive controls. | **ANSWERED 2026-09-27 (FABLE, Claude Opus 5.5) - dead (record _index/candidates/uc2-libvpx-dispatch/, uc2_dispatch.py 6 checks FAILS 0). ## RS. The resource entry has a formula and no type - 2026-09-13

From [`../02-Resource-And-Asset-Pipeline/resource-section-addressing.md`](../02-Resource-And-Asset-Pipeline/resource-section-addressing.md).

| ID | Question | Status |
|---|---|---|
| RS-1 | **What is a `ResourceEntry`'s extent, so the type can be declared?** The page proves `+0x04` mode, `+0x10` inline data, `+0x30` handle and `+0x38` cached base - reaching `+0x40` - but **nothing found allocates one**, and every caller of `00409600` / `004096C0` is a consumer rather than a constructor. **`ResourceEntry` is absent from the type store's 247 types**, so the corrected `sign32(low32(base) + offset)` formula has **no structured consumer that any checker can validate**. Declaring `0x40` would assert a lower bound as a size, which this store has been burned by before. | **ANSWERED 2026-09-26 (FABLE, Claude Opus 5.5), restating SWE2-DATA's 2026-09-16 census on the owning page (section 'RS-1 answered'). The extent is neither authored nor one number: 0051F9F0, the only complete geometry writer, stores the stride from .text immediates, and exactly three descriptors exist, embedded in the render root at +0x000, +0x060 and +0x0F0 with row strides 0x50, 0xC0 and 0x260. rowMask is derived and is 0x1F everywhere. So a ResourceEntry is declared per descriptor family, and the 0x260 and 0xC0 families are declared (RenderModelInstance, RenderStrideC0Element). The OPUS narrowing below (extent = authored data) was falsified by that census.** *Previous status, kept as history:* OPEN **NARROWED 2026-09-15 (OPUS): nothing allocates one because an entry is a ROW IN A BANK.** A byte-level rel32 scan gives `00409600` four call sites and `004096C0` seventeen; the callers obtain the pointer from `00409F50` -> `002ED570`, which returns `bank + sign32((index & rowMask) * rowStride)` with `rowStride` read from the DESCRIPTOR at `+0x48` (already in this page's descriptor section). So entries are rows inside a loaded bank blob, never heap objects - every caller is a consumer because there is nothing else to be. **The extent is therefore AUTHORED DATA, not a compiled constant**, and no reading of `.text` can raise the `0x40` lower bound, because the number is not in the code. What settles it is a census of the authored `rowStride` / `rowMask` over the shipped resource tables: one stride everywhere means that value IS the size and the type can be declared on the census; differing strides mean `ResourceEntry` is not one fixed-size type and the store should say so. Routed to SWE2-DATA. A parameter-displacement scan over all six accessors finds `+0x04`, `+0x10`, `+0x30`, `+0x38` and nothing else, so the known layout is unchanged. |
| RS-2 | **Do the nine callers of `004096C0` store its result as a 64-bit pointer?** If any declared type holds that result in an 8-byte field while the producer sign-extends 32 bits, that is a width contradiction the store would currently accept. **Not swept.** | **ANSWERED 2026-09-14 (FABLE): no declared type holds it, but every consumer keeps the sign-extended value as a 64-bit pointer.** There are 17 call sites in 11 functions. Three store the result in undeclared 8-byte fields (`0041CADC` → `+0x370`, `00504969` → `+0x1F8`, `005049A2` → `+0x230`), thirteen dereference it or pass it on as a pointer, and one re-encodes it to 32 bits (`00371415`). None zero-extends it or checks its range, so a base whose low half has bit 31 set reaches all of them as `0xFFFFFFFF8…`, a lead for `EO-3`. [resource section addressing](../02-Resource-And-Asset-Pipeline/resource-section-addressing.md). |
| RS-3 | **Is the sign-extend / zero-extend split a property of the encoding scheme or of one file's helpers?** Three sites read 2026-09-13 decode through `0020E600` and then compute an address in **32-bit** registers: `004096C0` (`add eax, ebx` / `cdqe`) and `00409660` (`movsxd`) **sign**-extend, while `00235C48` in the gambit importer (`add edi, eax`, then `word [rdi+0x14]`) **zero**-extends. The resource page already notes the split between its own section helpers and child selector; **this third instance is in a different subsystem**, so the split may be general. A reimplementation that picks one extension everywhere gets the other set of call sites wrong. | **ANSWERED 2026-09-26 (OPUS), STATIC: per call site and general - neither the encoding's nor one file's helpers.** [`rs3-opus-address-extension-census`](candidates/rs3-opus-address-extension-census/) (3/3, identical x2, md5 `ea083453`). `0020E600` is `mov eax, ecx ; add rax, [01F83530] ; ret`, one 32-bit value added to a 64-bit base. Of all 4,371 call sites, 2,957 use the full 64-bit result and 747 pass it on (85 %); **565 zero-extend** (53 by a 32-bit `mov`, 512 via 32-bit arithmetic then used as an address) and **60 sign-extend** (58 `cdqe` / `movsxd`, 2 after 32-bit arithmetic); 6 tail jumps, 36 named unclassified. Sign sites sit in Movement, WorldAreaField, Script_VM_Native_Bridge, Presentation and Audio; zero sites in CombatFormula, CombatAction, Items, Status, CombatAI and ActorEntity: each caller's own 32-bit typing, PS2-era address arithmetic. The forms agree exactly while the final address is below 2 GiB, so a reimplementation must keep referenced data below 2 GiB or use full-width pointers at every site; picking one extension everywhere is not enough. Where the arena lands at run time stays J-C's / EXP-077/078. *(previously:)* ~~OPEN~~ |

| ID | Question | Status |
|---|---|---|
| RMD-1 | which of entry 3's readers an event script actually relies on, which is what makes mode 4 and mode 5 different in play rather than in the slot map. `0031B950`, `BattleSlotMap_ResolveMappedBattleSlot` and five more read it; none is read. | **ANSWERED 2026-09-22 (SWE2-CONTRACT)** — the party-read-in state machine `0037B4D0` (14 sites via `0031C250`/`0031BEC0`/`00320170`), driven by the `partyallread` `0x3EB` / `partyallread2` `0x46F` / `summonread` `0x203` verb tasks through `0037C730`. Mode 4's `+0x5A90` rewrite makes the machine's slot→row resolutions return the leader; mode 5's restore preserves them. See `Battle-Runtime-Mode/CONTRACT-battle-runtime-mode.md` §14 item 1. |
| RMD-2 | whether `*(0x02EBF190)` can be null at any point where a consumer calls the ladder. §10 row 1 is a fault, not a fallback, and nothing establishes reachability. **NARROWED 2026-09-21 (OPUS), STILL OPEN - the reachability half is untouched and I am not claiming it.** What is now measured over the whole image for `02EBF190`: 314 reads into a register, and **ONLY 4 OF THEM ARE NULL-TESTED WITHIN THREE INSTRUCTIONS**, plus 2 sites that test the cell directly with `cmp qword ptr [02EBF190], 0`. So SIX GUARD SITES AGAINST 310 UNGUARDED READS. There are exactly **TWO WRITES**, at 00233C33 and 00238A92. **00233C10 IS A LAZY INITIALISER** and its shape settles what the engine believes: `test rax,rax; jne skip; call 002EF640; add rax, 0x4E68C; mov [02EBF190], rax` - so the ladder object is `SaveImage_GetActiveRuntimeBuffer() + 0x4E68C`, the same getter SavePayload and PersistentFlagPayload hang off, and the cell is filled on first use. WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT SETTLE: it does not establish reachability, which is the question. It does show the engine's own position - 310 consumers dereference without a check, so if null were reachable at a consumer the fault would be everywhere, not at one row - and it identifies the six places the engine itself thought null was possible, which is where a reachability argument should start. *Counting note, because the number was wrong first: `cmp qword ptr [cell], 0` puts the memory in operand 0 and my first pass scored those two as WRITES, giving 4 writes and 4 guards. They are guards. 2 writes, 6 guards.* | **ANSWERED 2026-09-22 (SWE2-CONTRACT) — no consumer can call the ladder while the pointer is null, within the single-threaded frame sequence.** The reachability half OPUS left open is closed by the master-state dispatch: `0022A580` jump-table-dispatches each frame on `byte[02064AD3]`, state 0 is exactly `0022B6E0`, and the state-0 exit write `0022B74E` is the first instruction of the `0209273C==5` block that ends with `call 002EF650` — leaving state 0 requires running the init in the same tick. Cut-closures: entry→621 fns 0 readers; `0022B6E0` pre-init→1,482 fns 0 readers; `00280140` pre-init→1,827 fns, 6 readers incl. the ladder, but it is a message-`0xD8` handler registered only via `00314020` ← state arms {2,3,>6} — unregistrable during the window. `00394130` is fully orphaned. OPUS's two-write count verified: `00233C33` lazy fill + `00238A92`. Residual: thread-entry census not enumerated. See contract §14 item 2. |
| RMD-3 | what `FUN_002E73C0(actor3, 3)` does to the guest slot when the chocobo bit clears. | **ANSWERED 2026-09-15 (OPUS) — nothing; it writes nothing at all.** All 65 bytes read: the body has **zero store instructions** (4 `je`, 3 `cmp`, 2 `test`, and one each of `ret`/`movzx`/`movsx`/`mov` load/`jne`/`jl`/`imul`/`add`). It is a five-gate guard chain — actor non-null, `+0xC0` non-null, `dword [rec]` non-negative, index ≠ `0xFFFF`, base+offset non-zero — then `imul rcx, rax, 0x740` against base `022C6F28`, the 160-record Presentation array of `K-10`, and a **tail call** to `003E6AA0` taken only when `[record + 0x284] ≠ 0`. Any effect on the slot is `003E6AA0`'s, which the ladder page already reads as a presentation request of sub-resource 3. What `[record + 0x284]` is remains unread. |

## FRP. The field runtime pass contract's open questions — 2026-09-14

Owned by [`../04-Actor-Entity/CONTRACT-field-runtime-pass.md`](../04-Actor-Entity/CONTRACT-field-runtime-pass.md) §14. Registered by FABLE under `OPUS-REQ-FABLE-QUESTION-ID-INTEGRITY`: the contract minted these ids and nothing could count them.

| ID | Question | Status |
|---|---|---|
| FRP-1 | what bit 5 of the actor record's `+0x14` means. Seven readers, no reading. **ANSWERED 2026-09-18 (FABLE).** Bit 5 of `+0x14` is the actor entry's script *enable* flag. Its only writer in the image is the unlisted 24-byte setter `00269E00` (`and byte [rcx+0x14], 0xDF`, then `(dl & 1) << 5` or-ed back), reached by the thunks of script verbs `001E enable` (`00353630`, `edx = 1`) and `001F disable` (`00353A50`, `edx = 0`); on disable the setter tail-jumps `0025B500`, the entry removal that releases system-stop id 18. All seven readers gate work on an entry: the per-kind pass `0025C170` builds an entry through `0025C830` only when bit 5 and `+0x08` bit 0 (the line/rect enable) are both set (`0025C1C0`) and runs `0025C230` over the second ordinal range only when bit 5 is set (`0025C1FB`); the line pass `0025B250` requires bit 5, `+0x08` bit 0 and `+0x1C` bit 6 (`0025B29A`); `0025B820` tests it twice (`0025B919` before `002EA6A0`, `0025BA2D`); `002675C0` requires it, then kind 3, once `02099DB4` is zero (`0026760E`); and `003DF6F0` requires it with `+0x08` bit 0 on the entry `003588B0(0)` returns, before `002E9FE0` (`003DF709`). So a disabled entry is skipped by every pass that would build, line-test or step it, and `disable` also drops its build hold. Static: an image-wide sweep of `test` / `and` / `or` on `byte [r+0x14]` with `0x20` / `0xDF` (one writer, seven readers) and the verb dispatch table. | ANSWERED |
| FRP-2 | which map row 636 of resource namespace 5 names, for the slot-0 `0xD4` request. The path tables are built at boot, so the stem is not in the image. **ANSWERED 2026-09-22 (FABLE): row 636 names NOTHING — and the row's own premise, that the stem is not in the image, is false.** The path tables ARE built at boot, but from **`lea` constants inside the installer `002DF9A0`**, so every array is a link-time address whose contents are static and readable. `002DF9A0` installs **ten** arrays at namespace 5 (`0215F028`), one per language - `us`, `fr`, `de`, `it`, `es`, `uk`, `kr`, `cn`, `ch`, `in`. **In all ten, rows 636, 637 and 638 are three NULL pointers**, so map 212's `.ebp`/`.mot`/`.fpk` triple is unauthored. **It is not an out-of-bounds read:** the same arrays carry at least **2,127** non-NULL rows with the highest populated map index **1,311**, so 636 sits well inside the populated region and the NULL is an authored absence. **The `× 3` triple is proved, not assumed:** rows 0/1/2 read `tst_a01.ebp`, `tst_a01.mot`, `tst_a01.fpk` - one stem, three extensions - which is the control on the whole reading. **Consequence, with `AB-2`** (the 22-byte resolver `002DF980` validates neither index and null-tests nothing): the once-per-run slot-0 request `WorldSimulation_ProcessDeferredModeRequest(0, 0xD4)` resolves to a **NULL path for all three** members of the triple. *Measurement note: the per-table capacity used here is the distance to the next installed array, which is an upper bound rather than the true length; eight of the ten tables agree exactly at 2,127 non-NULL / last map 1,311, and the two that read higher (`fr`, `cn`) do so because that bound spills into the neighbouring array - an artifact of the bound, not a difference in the data.* **NATIVE/STATIC — read from the image, nothing executed.** [the field runtime pass](../04-Actor-Entity/the-field-runtime-pass.md) | **ANSWERED 2026-09-22 (FABLE)** |
| FRP-3 | whether refusal 2 (`+0x10` bit 0 clear) is a disabled slot, an uninitialised one, or something else. The bit's writers are not read here. **Executing the gate did not touch this**: a fixture can plant the bit either way and watch the gate obey it, which says what the gate does and nothing about what the bit means. | **ANSWERED - propagated 2026-09-25 by FABLE (Claude Opus 5.5) from SWE2-CONTRACT's answer of 2026-09-19 on CONTRACT-field-runtime-pass.md (open item 3), which never reached this row.** Bit 0 of the manager block's +0x10 is the slot's LIVE flag: set only by ActorSystem_InitializeManagerRuntime (0026D305 or byte [rbx+0x10],1) and cleared only by the unload 002628B0 (00262DA8 and ...,0xFE); every indexed accessor fails closed on it. So refusal 2 (0025DA4D/0025DA51) means the manager runtime is not up (never initialised, or unloaded), and the two cannot be told apart at the gate. 'Disabled' is excluded because no writer produces a live-but-disabled form. The three instructions were re-read before propagating. |
| FRP-4 | **what the three newly named callees are for.** `0032F6E0`'s per-slot byte table at `022C6D20`, `003603C0`'s single byte at `022CB726`, and the mark word at `02099ABC` with its `0215F1A0` latch pair are now described *mechanically* by §13. **Nothing here names their purpose**, and the recursion over slots 1–3 for slot 0 is a strong hint about what those slots are to each other that this pilot cannot cash. | ANSWERED 2026-09-13 (`FABLE-REQ-OPUS-FP4`, consumed in the contract's §14): `02099ABC` is the actor-manager request mask drained by `0025BFB0`; `022C6D20[m]` is the per-manager deferred-unload byte set only by `00332190`; manager 0's recursion unloads the three event managers. **AMENDED 2026-09-21 (OPUS) on `ASTRA-CONTRA-OPUS-MGRMARK-HAS-CLEAR`:** `00332190` is the only writer that SETS the byte, and that part stands, but the contract's accompanying claim that it is never CLEARED is refuted - `0032F14B` in the per-row teardown `0032ED80` and `0032F4A2` in the block initialiser `0032F430` both zero it. The table is one column of an 18-column, 5-row structure-of-arrays at `022C6C00..022C6E70`, and the mark is cleared because the whole row is. Four searches missed both stores because they look for code that forms the address `022C6D20`, which neither store does - blind spot 11 |

## PCD. The Phyre class descriptor contract's open questions — 2026-09-14

Owned by [`../22-Middleware-PhyreEngine/Reflection-And-Class-Metadata/CONTRACT-phyre-class-descriptor.md`](../22-Middleware-PhyreEngine/Reflection-And-Class-Metadata/CONTRACT-phyre-class-descriptor.md) §14. | ID | Question | Status |
|---|---|---|
| PCD-1 | **what each of the six lists holds.** The source page says their roles are not established and this contract does not improve on that. The member registrations documented in [the recovered field schema](../22-Middleware-PhyreEngine/Reflection-And-Class-Metadata/member-registration-and-the-recovered-field-schema.md) attach to `+0x80`, which names one of six. **PARTIAL 2026-09-25 (FABLE, Claude Opus 5.5): five of the six are named; `+0xB0` is the residue, carried by `BL-8`.** Four came from [the metadata page's Q-1 answer](../22-Middleware-PhyreEngine/Reflection-And-Class-Metadata/class-descriptor-and-metadata-system.md), which this row had not picked up. `+0x50` is the descriptor's own node in the registry's class ring. `+0x80` holds the data members. `+0x90` holds instance methods, and `+0xA0` holds static functions. **`+0x60` is new: it is the `PAnnotatable` base, so it is the annotation list.** RTTI puts that base at `+0x60` in `PClassDescriptorDynamic` (`00D58380`) and at `+0x38` in `PClassDataMember` (`00D580B0`). `006B6700`, the drain the descriptor destructor applies to `+0x60`, is the one the data-member destructors apply to their own `+0x38`. The contract's §14 item 1 carries the table, the evidence and the domain. *Not established:* what `+0xB0` was meant to hold. | **SUPERSEDED 2026-09-26 (FABLE, Claude Opus 5.5): five of six lists are named, and the +0xB0 residue is carried by BL-8.** *Previous status, kept as history:* PARTIAL 2026-09-25 — five of six named, `+0x60` the annotation list; `+0xB0` stays with BL-8 |
| PCD-2 | what bit 0 of the tagged pointer at `+0x138` marks. **0063D550 CANNOT ANSWER IT, established 2026-09-22 (OPUS).** That body is where the tag is handled, and it handles it without ever branching on it: `0063D614` `movzx ecx, byte ptr [rbx + 0x138]`, `0063D61B` `mov rax, qword ptr [rbx + 0x138]`, `0063D622` `and ecx, 1`, `0063D625` `sub rax, rcx`, `0063D62B` `mov qword ptr [rbx + 0x30], rax`. **`x - (x & 1)` is exactly `x & ~1`**, so the contract's account of `+0x30` is right - but the bit is only STRIPPED here, never tested, so at this site the tag has no behavioural effect at all. The discriminator must be somewhere that READS the bit rather than clearing it. *(Also noted for the contract, whose size row says `0063D550` WRITES `+0x138`: both accesses there are LOADS. A read bounds the extent just as a write does, so the floor stands and only the wording is wrong - not edited here because that page is a peer's and currently uncommitted.)* **ANSWERED 2026-09-25 (FABLE, Claude Opus 5.5): bit 0 set means the name is BORROWED, so the destructor does not free it; no writer sets it in this image.** The reader this row asked for is the destructor `00633590`. It skips `_aligned_free` on `+0x138` when bit 0 is set (`0063361B`–`0063362F`). The one writer, the constructor `00632E80` (`00632F11`), stores a heap copy of the name in a 2-aligned allocation, so the bit is clear and the copy is freed. The contract's §14 item 2 has the detail. | ANSWERED 2026-09-25 — bit 0 = borrowed name, not freed; never set in this image |
| PCD-3 | the descriptor's exact size. `+0x138` is written, so it is at least `0x140`; no allocation site has been read to confirm the figure. **REFRAMED 2026-09-22 (OPUS) — the question asks for one number and there is not one object.** Every class in this store's descriptor tables carries SEVERAL descriptor objects, not one: across the 153 classes whose instance cell names a descriptor static, the RTTI mangled names give **ForType 153, Abstract 142, Concrete 120, WithoutDefaultConstructor 13, Wrapper 11**, so "the class descriptor is the static at 0x…" names ONE of a group. That also dissolves what looked like a hard contradiction: the minimum gap between consecutive descriptor statics is **`0x100`, in 77 of ~120 gaps**, which cannot hold a single `0x140` object — but the gap is measured between DIFFERENT CLASSES, so it bounds the whole per-class group and not one descriptor. Meanwhile the floor is real and belongs to whichever object `0063D550` runs on: `0063D55D` does `mov rbx, rcx` so its receiver is unbiased, and it genuinely reaches `+0x104` as a dword write (`0063D5F2`) and `+0x138` as a byte read (`0063D614`). **By contrast the three constructors stay below `0x100`** — `00632D80` reaches `+0xFC`, `00632C90` `+0xF8`, `00633390` `+0xE8`. So an exact size cannot be given until the question says WHICH descriptor, and the two figures in play (`≤ 0x100` constructed, `≥ 0x139` touched) are evidence that they are not the same object. **ANSWERED — the contract's §3 "Two classes, not one" note (OPUS, 2026-09-25) settles it; propagated to this row 2026-09-25 (FABLE, Claude Opus 5.5).** This row's reframing was right: the sizes are two because the classes are two. The base `PhyreClassDescriptor` is `0x100` (its constructor `00632D80` reaches `+0xFC`). `PClassDescriptorDynamic` is `0x140`: `0059AC00` allocates exactly `0x140` (`0059AD27`) and constructs it with `00632E80` (`0059AD49`), which writes `+0x138` (`00632F11`). The `≥ 0x139` floor belongs to the dynamic class; the `0x100` static gaps belong to the base family. | ANSWERED 2026-09-25 — base 0x100, dynamic 0x140 (contract §3) |
| PCD-4 | the `+0x100` / `+0x102` guard's meaning, and what state makes the two words equal. **ITS POLARITY AND ONE HARD CONSTRAINT ESTABLISHED 2026-09-22 (OPUS).** The condition is exact: `0063D556` loads `+0x100`, `0063D560` compares it with `+0x102`, `jne` goes to the reset, and only EQUAL AND NON-ZERO (`0063D569` `test ax, ax` / `jne`) skips it - so equal-and-ZERO resets, which "what state makes the two words equal" does not distinguish. **AND THIS BODY CANNOT BE WHAT ARMS THE GUARD:** its reset path ends at `0063D5E0` with `mov dword ptr [rcx + 0x100], eax` and eax just zeroed - ONE DWORD STORE CLEARING BOTH WORDS, the store-merging idiom - so after a reset they are equal and zero, precisely the state that resets again. Whatever writes a non-zero pair is elsewhere. **ANSWERED IN THE REGISTER 2026-09-25 (FABLE, Claude Opus 5.5); owner propagation routed to OPUS (`FABLE-REQ-OPUS-PCD4-GUARD-WORDS-ALWAYS-EQUAL`).** Every writer that belongs to the class changes both words identically. The class is `PClassDescriptorDynamic`: vtable `00D58380` is installed by the constructor `00632E80`, which zeroes both words with one dword store (`00632ED3`). `00639290` and `0063D410` increment both (`006392F0` / `006392FA`, `0063D4C5` / `0063D4CF`) after linking a member. `0063D790` decrements both (`add word, 0xFFFF` at `0063D7C2` / `0063D7C9`) while unlinking one. The reset zeroes both (`0063D5E0`). ~~An image-wide sweep of word-width add/sub/inc/dec/mov finds no other function touching both.~~ *Corrected 2026-09-26 (FABLE, Claude Opus 5.5), on `OPUS-NOTE-FABLE-PCD4-SWEEP-FINDS-FIVE-OUTSIDE-WRITERS`: that sweep sentence was wrong.* OPUS's reproducible sweep (`candidates/pcd4-opus-guard-word-writers/sweep.py`, re-run by FABLE, same output) finds eight functions writing both words at word width. Three are the class's own (`00639290`, `0063D410`, `0063D790`). Five are outside it: `00266530`, `003AAA50` (a stack local), `0041B550`, `00552250` and `005528C0`, each with independent values. `00269F40` writes `+0x102` alone. The other `+0x100` writers in the Phyre range are dword or qword stores in bodies not shown to share the class. **So the words are always equal, and the guard reduces to "member count non-zero"** *for descriptors written only by the class's code; that the four non-stack outside receivers are other types is not shown (the contract states it this way since `7b0941f33`).* The reset re-initialises the six member-list heads (`+0x50`, `+0x60`, `+0x80`, `+0x90`, `+0xA0`, `+0xB0`) only when the descriptor holds no members. What the two parallel counts were meant to differ on is not in the image. | **ANSWERED 2026-09-26 (FABLE, Claude Opus 5.5): status restated; answered in the register on 2026-09-25, and propagation to the contract is a task, not a question.** *Previous status, kept as history:* PARTIAL — answered in the register; the contract carries it when OPUS publishes |
| PCD-5 | `0063E410`, called at the end of a successful rebind, is unread. | **ANSWERED 2026-09-14 (FABLE)** — read whole: it sums `+0xF0` over the descriptor and its ancestors (to the root `02CF8270`) into `+0xF4`, and stores the parent's `+0xF8` plus `max(+0xF0, 0)` into `+0xF8`; what `+0x38` (negated into `+0xF0`) measures is not established |

Each element binds a model resource through `0x740` pool `022C6F28`: `+0x30` weapon (equip slot 0), `+0x60` off-hand (slot 1), `+0x90` body, `+0xC0`/`+0xF0` the def-row `+0x38`/`+0x3C` part-8 pair. Full map and k-enum in the doc §7.1; OPUS's PARTIAL notes retained below. |
 `k = 0` → `rsi+0x30` (slot 1) · `k = 1` → `rsi+0x60` (slot 2) · `k = 2` → `rsi+0x90` (slot 3) · `k = 3` → `rsi + (arg4 + 4) × 0x30` — **the slot comes from a further argument** (`002E31F8`–`002E3207`) · `k = 4` → `rsi+0x90` again, **the same slot as `k = 2`**, reached through its own preamble gated on `byte [01FD49EC]`.
**THREE CORRECTIONS TO THE QUESTION AS ASKED.** (1) There are **five** arms, not four. (2) `k` is not a part index — `k = 2` and `k = 4` select the **same** slot, and `k = 3` does not name a slot at all. (3) The row says *“k = 0, 1, 4, 5”*; across all **11** call sites in the eight callers the only **literal** values are **0** (×2) and **3** (×2), and the other **seven compute `edx`** — so the reachable set is **not** established from the call sites, and 1, 4 and 5 appear as immediates nowhere.
**AND ANY `k` OUTSIDE 0–4 IS A SILENT NO-OP**: the default at `002E34D7` is a bare epilogue — pops and `ret`, touching nothing — so a `k = 5` call, if one is reachable through those seven computed sites, does nothing at all and reports nothing.
**WHAT A SLOT IS, structurally.** Each `0x30` element begins with an id whose `-1` means empty (`cmp dword [rbx], -1`, `002E32E3`), passes its low word to `0042F250` (`002E32EB`), and carries a flags byte at `+0x11` masked `& 0x9F` (`002E32F0`–`002E32F6`). **Element 0 is never selected by any `k`** — the arms index from slot 1 upward, and `rsi+0` is the header those `-1` tests read.
**THE OPEN HALF, which is what the question actually asked:** which body part, binding or model each slot holds. Nothing in this function names them; it is a generic indexed update over a record it does not interpret. `002E3110` already carries the working name `Movement.CharacterPresentation.BindingUpdate` and is called `BindingUpdate` on [add-motion-skeleton-and-high-model-tables.md](../17-Presentation-Rendering/Model-And-Motion-Formats/add-motion-skeleton-and-high-model-tables.md), which is consistent with the reading and does not name the slots either. **Answering the open half needs the producer that FILLS `[actor+0xC0]`, not another read of the consumer.** | PARTIAL |

The allocator itself stamps each block's header with an encoded address (`0036A209`..`0036A20E`, `[block-0x10]`), so the arena is addressed in this 32-bit space by design. *Why it works.* It requires every such pointer below 4 GiB, and nothing in the image checks that: the arena is CRT heap (imports `malloc` ×37, `_aligned_malloc` ×3, `calloc` ×1; no `VirtualAlloc`, `HeapAlloc` or `MapViewOfFile` import), and the image opts out of ASLR (DllCharacteristics `0x8120`: `HIGH_ENTROPY_VA` and `NX_COMPAT` set, `DYNAMIC_BASE` clear; base `0x120000`, image end `0x3096000`), so the process runs without address randomisation and its heap grows bottom-up from the low address space, which is what the PS2-era 32-bit convention relies on (a reading of the documented loader behaviour, tier 6). Static; the encode, resolve, allocator, registration, slot copy and completion calls read in full.
