Element loads appear as **both `movsx` and `movzx` at byte and word widths**, which is the `USN` flag.
**So the grid it implements is the whole one:** S / V2 / V3 / V4 × 32 / 16 / 8, plus `V4_5`. The row's example `0x6C` is `0x60 + 0b1100` → `vn = 3`, `vl = 0` → **`V4_32`**.
**THE OPEN HALF, and it is why this is PARTIAL rather than ANSWERED:** *which CMD codes actually reach it.* The function implements the grid, but the decomposition happens in the caller and I have not enumerated which of `0x60`–`0x7F` the VIF stream ever presents — nor read the `m` (mask) flag path, nor checked the `V4_5` arm's bit layout against `RGBA5551`. **A function that can decode a format is not evidence that the format is ever authored**, which is the same distinction `AY-10` drew and the reason this row does not close on a capability. *Narrowed 2026-09-18 (FABLE): the three halves OPUS left open on this row, two closed and one bounded.* **The mask flag is ignored.** The decoder tests `(cmd & 0x60) == 0x60`, takes `vn = (cmd >> 2) & 3` and `vl = cmd & 3`, bit 14 as the unsigned flag, bit 15 as the add-TOPS flag, bits 16-23 as NUM and the low ten bits as ADDR (`0022CA73`..`0022CAC7`); bit 4 of the command, VIF's `m`, is never extracted, so `0x7x` decodes exactly as `0x6x` and there is no mask, row or column register anywhere in the decoder's state. **The `V4_5` arm is RGBA 5:5:5:1 as on the PS2:** one 16-bit word gives `(w & 0x1F) << 3`, `(w >> 2) & 0xF8`, `(w >> 7) & 0xF8` and `(w >> 8) & 0x80`, so the top bit becomes alpha `0x80` (`0022C840`..`0022C87F`). The unsigned flag is tested in each of the eight 16- and 8-bit arms (`test r9d, r9d`), and a write cycle longer than the cycle length leaves through the early exit at `0022C00D`, so filling writes are not implemented. **Which formats are authored, bounded to code-built packets: only `V4_32`.** All 87 UNPACK commands in [vif1-packet-templates.tsv](../17-Presentation-Rendering/Legacy-PS2-GS/vif1-packet-templates.tsv) are `V4-32`, and an image-wide sweep of stored dword immediates with a top byte in `0x60`..`0x7F` and an UNPACK-shaped low word finds 98 with `0x6C` (24 with the TOPS flag) and nothing else that survives reading: of the 19 `0x60` / `0x70` hits, twelve (`0x602E4000`, `0x602CC000`) are the upper half of a GIF tag lying inside a `V4_32` payload (read at `004DA4A1`: the UNPACK header is the `0x6C140000` four bytes before the payload starts) and seven are `0x..808080` colour constants; the three others are `0x7D000000` (an unaligned stack store), `0x7F000000` (a stack store in library code) and `0x6464007F` (a store to a global), none at a command slot of a packet.The UI quad emitter is one of the 98 and its packet is decoded whole on [the cutscene-slot page](../99-Unresolved-Residual/Cutscene-Asset-Slots/cutscene-name-slots-and-the-depth-of-field-sidecar.md) (UQ-347). **What keeps the row PARTIAL:** packets that reach the decoder from loaded data rather than from code were not censused, so the other twelve arms are unexercised by code-built packets, not shown dead. |

A stereo or four-channel source spreads its channels at fixed offsets either side of `pan` (on two outputs -0.5 and +0.5, otherwise -0.25 and +0.25, then adjusted by a spread parameter whose effect was not characterised), six- and eight-channel sources bypass the angle and map channel to channel with 0.7071 folds, and the voice routine sends a material whose header byte `+0x19` has bit 3 set to output 2 alone, without calling the function. *Read against this page's pan byte:* `0x00` is 270 degrees, `0x40` is 0 and `0x7F` is 88.6 - a continuous front half. For `0x80` and above the wrapper passes `(0xBF - pan) / 128` with `frpan = -1`, which the driver turns into 268.6 degrees for `0x80`, 180 for `0xBF` and 90 for `0xFF`: the rear half runs the opposite way round from what a front-to-back mirror would give, and the byte circle jumps at `0x7F` / `0x80`. On two outputs front and rear are indistinguishable anyway (180 degrees splits equally, as 0 does). *Counted the same day, script side:* the only script verbs that carry a pan byte to this wrapper are `voicepan` and `voicechangepan` (both reach `002256F0` through the stream pan setter `001DC240` and `00225280`; `sebsoundplay` has no pan argument in any of its 6,821 shipped calls). The 1,114 `us` scripts call them **18 times**: `64` eleven times, `96` once, and **six calls in the rear half** - `192` three times (`alc_b0400`, `ozm_b0400` twice), `215` (`naf_b0401`), `240` (`bhm_c0100`) and `250` (`grm_a0200`). Through the driver those are 178.6, 146.3, 111.1 and 97.0 degrees; a front-to-back mirror would have made them 181.4, 213.8, 248.9 and 263.0. `192` is directly behind either way; **for `215`, `240` and `250` the two readings put the voice on opposite sides**, and on two outputs that is an audible left/right difference, so it is a question a listening test can settle. The wrapper's eight other native call sites all pass a parameter through and were not followed. *Inference, kept apart:* that output index 0 is the left speaker and 1 the right (so that angles run clockwise and `pan = +0.5` is hard right) rests on the standard Windows channel order, which the image does not name. *Not covered:* the one-output table points at zero-initialised memory filled at run time, and kind 9 of the narrowing above is still unidentified. Static evidence only. |

The 0036C660 'ChSEinfo' call is an allocation tag, not a magic check. *History:* **PARTIAL — the ADDRESSING is established exactly; the CONTENTS are not in the file (OPUS, 2026-09-15).** |
**`002ED950` is a two-field lookup, and all 134 bytes read.** Its single `ecx` argument packs two things: the **low 16 bits are an index** (`movzx edx, cx`) and **bits 16–23 are a table selector** (`shr ecx, 0x10` / `movzx eax, cl`). The selector is rebased by `-0x62` and bounded `cmp eax, 0x15 / ja` — so only **`0x62`–`0x77`** can resolve — then dispatched through a 22-entry rel32 jump table at `002ED9D8`.
**Eight tables, and the selector space is SPARSE.** Of the 22 in-range selectors, **eight** reach a table and **fourteen fall to the fail arm and return 0**:
 `0x62`→`021641A8` · `0x63`→`021641B0` · `0x67`→`021641B8` · `0x6D`→`021641C0` · `0x6E`→`021641C8` · `0x73`→`021641D0` · `0x74`→`021641D8` · `0x77`→`021641E0`;
 `0x64`, `0x65`, `0x66`, `0x68`–`0x6C`, `0x6F`–`0x72`, `0x75`, `0x76` all return **0**.
The eight pointers are eight consecutive qword slots, `021641A8`…`021641E0`, stride 8.
**The record shape is fixed by the tail.** Null pointer → return 0; `cmp edx, [rcx+8]` with `jge` → **the entry count lives at `+0x08` of the table header**; otherwise `rax = rcx + (index + 1) × 0x10` — so **entries are `0x10` bytes and begin one `0x10` block after the header**. The three SE ids the row asks about are fields inside that `0x10`-byte entry.
**WHY THE CONTENTS CANNOT BE READ HERE.** All eight table pointers are **above `.data`'s file-backed bound of `01F7E400`** — zero in the image, populated at load. So which records the ids come from is answerable as *addressing* and not as *values*: the route from selector to entry is exact, and the entries themselves do not exist in the file.
**The second half is untouched:** whether ids `3`–`199` or `500`–`699` are ever authored. That is a question about the shipped data, not about this function, and nothing here bears on it. **Not claimed:** which of the eight tables is CHSE — [chse-character-se-tables.md](../02-Resource-And-Asset-Pipeline/PS2-Image-Data-Formats/chse-character-se-tables.md) records CHSE as the leading candidate on a closed-set membership test rather than a traced path, and this reading neither confirms nor refutes it. |

## OC. The ordered-container runtime — 2026-09-15

Owned by [the-ordered-container-runtime.md](../24-Compiler-And-CRT-Runtime/Cxx-Runtime-Families/the-ordered-container-runtime.md) §7. The six red-black tree bodies every keyed collection in the game shares. Registered
with the page in the same commit; the family had no document until now, which is what let three
other pages describe its operations as memory management.

| ID | Question | Status |
|---|---|---|
| OC-1 | **Which container library this is.** The shape is the standard red-black tree that both MSVC's `std::_Tree` and EASTL's `rbtree` implement, and the node header (`+0x00`/`+0x08` children, `+0x10` parent, `+0x18` colour) is compatible with either reading. Nothing in the six bodies names its library, and the corpus carries both `CxxStandardLibrary` and `EASTL` tags elsewhere. [the-ordered-container-runtime.md](../24-Compiler-And-CRT-Runtime/Cxx-Runtime-Families/the-ordered-container-runtime.md) §7 | **ANSWERED 2026-09-15 (OPUS), within the hour of being filed — EASTL, decided by the parent pointer.** The premise of the question was wrong: the header is **not** compatible with either reading. EASTL's `rbtree_node_base` is `{mpNodeRight +0, mpNodeLeft +8, mpNodeParent +0x10, mColor +0x18}`; MSVC's `std::_Tree_node` is `{_Left +0, _Parent +8, _Right +0x10}`. **All six bodies climb parents through `+0x10`** — loops whose only purpose is to reach a parent — and under MSVC's layout that offset is a child, which no climb can be. The discriminator was already measured on the page before the question was written; what was missing was the comparison, not the measurement. **Corroborated from a different direction:** the consumer cluster that calls these six constructs an `eastl::allocator_memory_log`, named in the image's own RTTI type descriptor (vtable `00902720`, locator `01CED8C0`, type descriptor `01F480E8`, `.?AVallocator_memory_log@eastl@@`). **CORRECTED the same day, by me:** those are not two independent lines of MINE. The allocator line was **already published** on [eastl-strings-containers-and-the-logging-allocator.md](../23-Third-Party-Libraries/EASTL/eastl-strings-containers-and-the-logging-allocator.md), which carries `001EDF00` in its key-address table as `eastl_allocator_memory_log_ctor` and states *“The library is EASTL and the allocator class is `eastl::allocator_memory_log`”* on the same 14-byte body. I re-derived it and cited nothing. **The layout discriminator is still mine and is still what answers this row**, because that page names **none of the six tree bodies** and makes no claim about the tree; it establishes the library for `basic_string`, `vector` and the allocator. So: one published line extended to a family it did not cover, not two independent lines. The colour values follow: the insert's last two instructions read the root out of the head and write `1` into its `mColor`, a red-black insert ends by making the root black, and EASTL's `kRBTreeColorRed` is `0`. **Stated as a negative too:** no string, symbol or import in the six bodies names EASTL — this rests on a structure offset plus a neighbouring class name, and would be overturned by any red-black implementation that puts its parent third. ~~These six are the only red-black machinery in the image.~~ **NARROWED 2026-09-16 (OPUS) on `FABLE-CONTRA-OPUS-OC1-THREE-RBTREES-NOT-ONE` and its author's own correction `FABLE-CORRECT-OPUS-OC1-THE-OTHER-TWO-TREES-ARE-MSVC`. That clause was false and it was the guard, not the answer.** FABLE censused the image for the rotation shape taken from these two rotations rather than invented — no calls, ≥8 qword stores, writes confined to `+0x00`/`+0x08`/`+0x10` and never to the colour byte — and found **three mirror pairs, not one**: `0016D780`/`0016D7E0` (these), `00714B00`/`0071F240`, and `00799BD0`/`00799C30`. **The answer survives and is STRENGTHENED, because the two new pairs reparent through `+0x08`, not `+0x10`** — `00714B14 mov [rax+8],rdx`, `00714B1C mov [r8+8],rax` and so on, against `0016D793 mov [rax+0x10],rcx` here. The invariant offset across a mirror pair is the parent, because a rotation exchanges the children and reparents three nodes. So that is `_Parent +0x08` against `mpNodeParent +0x10`: **both node layouts are present in this image, and these six sit on the EASTL side of a real contrast rather than in an empty field.** That is a stronger statement than uniqueness and it is true, where the struck clause was neither. **What is NOT claimed:** which containers the MSVC trees belong to, whether their inserts match, or how much MSVC container code the image holds — two rotation pairs and their erases is what was measured. **And the guard's real weakness is still open:** this page says the toolchain inlined the insert's rotations, and an inlined copy is invisible to every census either agent has run, because they all count call edges; FABLE built two instruments to find inlined tree code and reported **both as failures** — storing to all four node offsets matches 1,264 bodies, and a `+0x18` colour compare with a `+0x10` parent load still matches 60. **OC-1 stays ANSWERED on the discriminator, which never rested on uniqueness.** |
| OC-2 | **The node's total size, and where the payload begins.** The family never computes a size or steps an array, so nothing in it says a node is `0x20` bytes rather than `0x20` plus a payload. The `+0x20` key position is a consumer's reading ([font-data-kerning-and-expansion.md](../16-UI/Text-And-Number-Rendering/font-data-kerning-and-expansion.md) §4.2 keys its tree at `node+0x20`) — corroboration from a different reading, not a measurement made in the family. [the-ordered-container-runtime.md](../24-Compiler-And-CRT-Runtime/Cxx-Runtime-Families/the-ordered-container-runtime.md) §7 | **ANSWERED 2026-09-15 (FABLE) — measured in the callers: the payload begins at `+0x20`, and the node has no single size.** The family expresses neither fact, so neither is readable in it; the allocation does. Every caller that allocates a node does it in the same four instructions before the insert - fetch the allocator sub-object's vtable, size into `edx`, `call [vtable+0x10]`, then offset what comes back. Over **90 call sites to `0016D840`, the 80 that allocate apply `+0x20`** to the returned pointer before writing the value into it - **80 of 80, no exception in the image**. The size is one of **nine** values: `0x28` `0x30` `0x38` `0x40` `0x48` `0x50` `0x58` `0x60` `0x88` - **every one `0x20` plus a multiple of eight, and none `0x20` or less**. So the header is `0x20`, the payload starts at `+0x20`, and the node is `0x20 + sizeof(Value)`: nine value sizes in one image, which is what a shared runtime looks like from the allocation side rather than a gap in the measurement. Clearest site `001A3380`: `lea edx,[r8+0x38]` / `call [rax+0x10]` / `add rax,0x20` / `movups [rax],xmm0` / `mov [rax+0x10],ecx` - twenty bytes of value at `node+0x20` in a `0x38`-byte node. **Confirms the font page's `node+0x20` key from a direction that never reads a key.** NOT CLAIMED: which value type any size belongs to, or what the `0x88` node holds. |
| OC-3 | **Which of `+0x00` and `+0x08` is “left”.** The two iterator steps `0016D6D0` and `0016D720` are mirror images, so which is `operator++` and which `operator--` follows from the comparison direction in the container wrapper above them, which is not read. Nothing on the page depends on the answer. [the-ordered-container-runtime.md](../24-Compiler-And-CRT-Runtime/Cxx-Runtime-Families/the-ordered-container-runtime.md) §7 | **ANSWERED 2026-09-15 (OPUS) alongside OC-1 — `+0x00` is `mpNodeRight`, `+0x08` is `mpNodeLeft`.** It follows from the library, and it is checked against behaviour rather than inherited: `0016D6D0` goes to `+0x00` and then descends `+0x08` to that subtree's extreme, which is a **successor** only if `+0x00` is the right child; and `0016D720`, not `0016D6D0`, is the one carrying the sentinel test (`mpNodeParent->mpNodeParent == this` with `mColor == 0`), which is the direction that can walk off the end of an EASTL tree. So `0016D6D0` is `RBTreeIncrement`, `0016D720` is `RBTreeDecrement`, `0016D780` is `RBTreeRotateLeft` (it takes `mpNodeRight`) and `0016D7E0` is `RBTreeRotateRight`. |
| OC-4 | **The 72 substrate callers are counted, not read.** 99 distinct callers reach the family, 72 of them carrying no subsystem under `audit_crossrefs`' attribution; the named 27 are broken out by subsystem on the page and the other 72 are not enumerated. [the-ordered-container-runtime.md](../24-Compiler-And-CRT-Runtime/Cxx-Runtime-Families/the-ordered-container-runtime.md) §7 | **ANSWERED 2026-09-15 (FABLE) — all 99 enumerated and grouped, in `members/ordered-container-runtime-callers.tsv`.** Two groupings that need no reading for meaning. **Which members a caller uses:** six signatures occur and **no caller uses more than two of the six** — `inc`+`era` 30, `dec`+`ins` 24, `inc`+`ins` 16, `ins` 16, `inc` 12, `rotL`+`rotR` 1 (which is `0016DA60`, the family's own internal edge). That sums to **99 callers** and **170 distinct (caller, callee) pairs** — the page's edge count, reached from the other direction — across **213 call sites**; the two numbers are both right and are not the same number. **No caller pairs `ins` with `era`**, so these are single container operations rather than general users, which is what compiler-emitted `insert`/`erase`/`clear` bodies look like. **Node size:** 48 of the 99 allocate, in `OC-2`'s nine sizes, and the sizes cluster by address — a candidate partition into container families, offered not asserted. **EVERY ONE OF THE 99 IS `FUN_xxxxxxxx`**; not one caller of this family is named. The 24 `dec`+`ins` callers are **hinted inserts**, read whole at `00199DB0`, which confirms three claims from the caller side: `0016D720` is *used* as `--hint` (`OC-3`), `r9d` really is the side selector, and an existing node's key is **compared** at `node+0x20` — a third and differently-shaped line for `OC-2`. **THE BOUNDARY:** enumerated and grouped structurally; no caller was read for purpose, and the subsystem attribution on the page is still `audit_crossrefs`', not derived here. |

## MT. The MSVC ordered-container runtime — 2026-09-15

Owned by [the-msvc-ordered-container-runtime.md](../24-Compiler-And-CRT-Runtime/Cxx-Runtime-Families/the-msvc-ordered-container-runtime.md) §7.
**This image links two standard libraries' red-black trees.** `OC` above is EASTL's, which the
engine uses; these 23 bodies are Microsoft's `std::_Tree`, which came in with separately compiled
modules. The discriminator is a byte: MSVC's node carries `_Isnil` at `+0x19` and EASTL's
`rbtree_node_base` ends at `+0x19` with no member there, and across a mirror rotation pair the
invariant store offset — which is the parent — is `+0x08` here against `+0x10` there. Registered
with the page in the same commit; nothing described these bodies before it.

| ID | Question | Status |
|---|---|---|
| MT-1 | **Which container each of the three instantiations is.** The grouping is structural — who calls whose rotations — and no value type is identified. A has three `_Tidy` bodies against one erase, which reads as three containers sharing a node layout with different payloads, but that is a reading and not a measurement. **NARROWED 2026-09-17 (FABLE): A is three maps owned by one YEBIS object and B is a map that lives on one routine's stack; the value types are still unnamed.** *A.* Each of the three erase-range bodies has two callers: its own 41-byte clear wrapper (`007136D0`, `00713700`, `00713730`) and `006FF840` (172 B), which clears the three maps in turn at the object's `+0xC8`, `+0xB8` and `+0xA8` and frees each header through `00210EB0` (`006FF85F`..`006FF8E7`); the three tidies are also run from the 23,568-byte `006FF900`, the object's teardown. `006FF840` is reached from `006DAFB0`, `006DE780` and `006DEB40`, and `006FF900` from `006DAA70` and `006DE950`, all inside the YEBIS span. The `lower_bound` `0070D360` compares an unsigned 64-bit key at `node+0x20` (`0070D380`, `0070D39E`, both `jae`) and returns the qword at `+0x28`, so the three are maps from a 64-bit key (a pointer or a hash) to a pointer-sized value; the erase-node `00714DC0` is also reached from `0070E520` and `0070E600`, two erase-by-key bodies with no listed caller. *B.* Its one erase-range `0071F4B0` is called from `0071D170` (2,140 B, called from `0071CD10`) on a header at `[rsp+0x20]`, right before the routine sets its `0x8000FFFF` failure code (`0071D974`..`0071D98B`), and from `0071EE40`, which is called only from the unwind entry `008A2FEC`: a function-local map destroyed on both the normal and the exceptional exit. What the keys index and what the values are is not read; that needs the inserters, which this page does not list. Static. *Narrowed 2026-09-18 (FABLE): the owner is named, and the `+0xC8` map is read as a render-texture cache.* **The “one YEBIS object” is not a class instance but YEBIS's global state block**: `0xD40` bytes with **no vtable**, allocated through `006DA880` with the source tag `..\src\ppfx.cpp` (line `0x1C2B` at `006DE9C8`–`006DE9E1` in `006DE950`, line `0x332` at `006DAB84`–`006DAB9D` in `006DAA70`), constructed by `006FF5D0` (608 B: a flag byte at `+0`, pointers zeroed to `+0x90`, then the three map headers made at `+0xA8` by `00714800` (`006FF62D`–`006FF648`), `+0xB8` by `007147A0` (`006FF64B`–`006FF661`) and `+0xC8` by `00714740` (`006FF669`–`006FF67F`)), and stored at `02EA0B70` (`006DE9FB`, `006DABB9`); `006DE780` is the shutdown, which clears the three maps through `006FF840` on the block it finds there and zeroes `02EA0B70`, `02EA0B78` and `02EA0B80` (`006DE805`, `006DE81F`, `006DE8D4`). The RTTI `IPfxBaseContext` vtable `00D8F8E8` that `006DE780` references belongs to a different object; the block itself has none. Some sixty YEBIS entry points (`006DB4C0` .. `006DF440`) load `[02EA0B70]` as their first act, so the block is the current PPFX context every API call implicitly takes. **The `+0xC8` map is a find-or-create cache of `PPFX::CRenderTexture` keyed by a pointer.** `0070D360` walks the `+0xC8` tree for the 64-bit key in `rdx` (`0070D366`–`0070D3A7`); a hit yields the node's `+0x28` value, a miss or a null value calls `006F1F60(block, key, …, &out)` (`0070D3BC`–`0070D3D6`), whose callee `00720FB0` installs the `PPFX::CRenderTexture` vtable, and either way the value is latched at the block's `+0x60` with a caller dword at `+0x68` (`0070D3E4`–`0070D3ED`) — the “current” render texture. The only static route to that lookup is `006CBEA0` (485 B, `Phyre.Middleware`) → `006DD5F0` (`006CBF2E`), which takes the key from the first element's `+0x10` of a Phyre pointer array at the source object's `+0x38` (count at `+0x30`, `006CBEDD`–`006CBF04`) and passes that object's dwords `+0x90`, `+0x94` and `+0xA0` — the shape of a width, height and format — so the key is the Phyre-side texture handle and the cache maps it to YEBIS's wrapper. The `+0xA8` and `+0xB8` maps' inserters and value types are not read; the sibling `006DD660` wrapper has no listed caller. Static: the allocation sites, the constructor, the lookup and its caller. [the-msvc-ordered-container-runtime.md](../24-Compiler-And-CRT-Runtime/Cxx-Runtime-Families/the-msvc-ordered-container-runtime.md) §7 | **ANSWERED 2026-09-26 (FABLE, Claude Opus 5.5): all three instantiations are named. A is three map<u64, wrapper*> find-or-create caches in the CPostEffect block (0xD40, published at 02EA0B70) over the PPFX IGPUDevice at its +0x20 (RTTI of the vtable the device constructor installs): +0xA8 holds IGPUSurface* from device slot 66 (log tag RefRT), current at +0xD8; +0xB8 holds IGPUVolumeTexture* from slot 62 (Ref3D), current at +0xF0, and its API wrapper has no static reference of any kind; +0xC8 is the slot-60 Ref2D cache read on 2026-09-18. ### Is the navigation run-state pointer cleared before the map pack frees the block it names?

Raised 2026-09-20 (OPUS) from `_types` work on `NavRunStateBlock` (route `PTR 0x02AEDFB0`).

**What is established, from the shipping bytes.**

- `00378230`, the map-pack teardown, releases the block through `003697F0` and then calls
  `00384160` with `NULL`. That call returns at its own entry test (`test rcx, rcx ; je`), so it
  **does not clear `02AEDFB0`**.
- The image has exactly **two** writers of `02AEDFB0`: the store inside `00384160`, and `00383A20`,
  whose entire twelve-byte body nulls it.
- `00383A20`'s only callers are `002341C0` and `002368D0`. **Neither is the pack teardown.**
  `002341C0` is an area-teardown chain that also calls `00392710`, a `02AEE060` body - so the grid
  and the pointer are cleared together there.
- `00383C80`'s entire body is `eax = (qword[02AEDFB0] != 0)` - the readiness predicate the field
  runtime tests before using the navigation system.

**The question.** Is `00383A20` guaranteed to run before, or in the same teardown as, `00378230`?

**Why it cannot be answered where it was found.** It is an ordering property of two call chains in
different subsystems, not a fact about any one body. Reading further down either chain establishes
what that chain does, never what the other one did first.

**What would answer it.** Either a semantic account of the area/pack teardown ordering, or a runtime
observation that `[02AEDFB0]` is null whenever `00383C80` is reached after an unload.

**Not asserted:** that this is a defect. A shipped pathfinder is unlikely to carry a live
use-after-free; the likely resolutions are that the chains are always ordered or that nothing queries
between them - both orderings, neither visible statically.


### What widget subtype is embedded at `ManagerSub0209BE80_8FA0 +0xAC0`, and how large is it? (OPUS)

Raised 2026-09-20 (OPUS). **This is the single largest remaining item behind S-02's `types` cell** -
roughly 4,200 of the family's 5,906 genuinely unattributed bytes, and it is one collapse, not a
diffuse gap.

**Established, and not to be re-derived.**

- An embedded widget starts at the parent's `+0xAC0`. Sixteen displacements in the parent's census
  rebase to it and twelve land exactly on declared `Widget` fields with no contradictions.
- Its extent is **at least `0x584`**: inner displacements `0x0..0x580` across 77 accesses in 11
  functions, corroborated independently by `002BE290` (reached from `002BE4D4`) reading
  `[rcx + 0x570]` and `[rcx + 0x57e]`.
- Five rows the parent declares as its own - `ptr1030`, `int1038`, `word103C`, `flags103E`,
  `dword1040` - are that sub-object's interior seen in parent coordinates.
- The collapse needs a **sized subtype**, the way `BattleMenuPanelWidget3010` serves `_AB30 +0xC0`.
  It cannot use `Widget`: that row's size is `UNRESOLVED` **correctly** - "THE SIZE IS AN ARGUMENT,
  26 distinct sizes from `0xC0` to `0xBC08` across 49 construction sites, so there is no
  `sizeof(Widget)`".

**Three searches are exhausted and empty**, each exhaustive of its own shape: the five
`lea reg, [base + 0xAC0]` sites in the image pass no size and hand the address to dispatch bodies;
the six writes to `[reg + 0xAC0]` install no vtable or proc and belong to other objects; and a
tracked walk from the singleton pointer cannot reach the object, because its consumers receive it
rather than computing it.

**Why the shape is the problem.** An object constructed in place as part of its parent never needs
its own address materialised - the compiler holds one base and emits the sub-object's fields at
parent-relative displacements. There is no instruction at `+0xAC0` to find.

**What would answer it**, in decreasing order of likely yield:

1. The singleton's own constructor, found from the singleton rather than from this displacement; the
   size argument for the in-place construction is there if anywhere.
2. A vtable identity for the 11 consumer functions - if they are a known widget subtype's methods,
   the subtype names its own size.
3. A runtime read of the object at `*(0209BE80) + 0x9A60` (ASTRA), which would settle the extent
   directly and is the only route that does not depend on finding a construction at all.

**UPDATED 2026-09-20 (OPUS) - the top-ranked route worked, and narrowed the question rather than
closing it.** Approaching from the singleton instead of the displacement: `00291750` calls
`002BE450` with `rcx = singleton + 0x8FA0`, and `002BE450` passes `edx = 0x1110` with
`r8 = 002BE490` to `00245000`. The parent is constructed **in place, once, at `0x1110`** - its
declared extent - with `002BE490` as its proc.

**So there is no constructor for the child, and there cannot be one.** The parent's single sized
construction covers `0x000..0x1110`, and the singleton memsets the whole `0x10FD0` first. The child
at `+0xAC0` is a region inside that allocation which the proc treats as a widget - `002BE490` ends
with `lea rcx, [rbx + 0xac0] / call 002BE290` on message 2. The three empty address-shaped searches
were looking for something that does not exist.

**A ceiling falls out of the parent's extent:** the child is at most `0x1110 - 0xAC0 = 0x650`.
With the `0x584` floor, **the child is between `0x584` and `0x650`** - a 204-byte window.

**What the remaining window turns on:** `ptr1030`, `int1038`, `word103C`, `flags103E` and
`dword1040` sit at `+0x1030..+0x1044`, inside it. Whether those are the child's interior or the
parent's own fields after the child decides the extent. That is a question about *those five rows*,
not about finding a construction - which is a much smaller question than the one filed above.

**TIGHTENED 2026-09-20 (OPUS) - the window is FOUR bytes, not 204.** The `0x650` ceiling above came
from the parent's allocation, which is the weakest bound available once the parent's layout is
carved. The binding constraint is the next **declared parent field**: `helpMessageScreen` at
`+0x1048` is `TYPE RESOLVED` and typed `HelpMessageWidget0500*` - a pointer this type holds to
another widget. Two objects cannot own the same bytes, so the child ends at or before child `+0x588`.

Its last observed field is `dword1040` at child `+0x580`, ending `+0x584`. Between them sits only
`unobservedSpan1044`, four bytes. **The child is `0x584` or `0x588`.**

The five rows are confirmed as the child's interior by the consuming body rather than by arithmetic:
`002BE290`, entered with the child's address in `rcx` from `002BE4D4`, reads `[rcx + 0x570]` and
tests `[rcx + 0x57e]` - `ptr1030` and `flags103E` in child coordinates.

**This question is now about four bytes**, and access evidence cannot settle them: nothing touches
child `+0x584`, and a four-byte trailing pad is what a 4-aligned widget size produces either way. It
is a candidate for closing by fiat with the reasoning recorded, or for leaving as the store's
smallest honest open span.

## GE. The status `+0x0A` pool key and its record pointer — FABLE, 2026-09-21

Owned by [the-thirty-two-statuses.md](../10-Status-Periodic-Terminal/the-thirty-two-statuses.md), in the
`+0x0A` amendment. Registered with the amendment in the same commit; the three rows are what the
correction opened rather than what it closed. Prefix checked free with `next_question_id.py --check GE`
immediately before assignment.

| ID | Question | Status |
|---|---|---|
| GE-1 | **What bank 12 of the 28-bank string pool holds.** The status record's `+0x0A` word is `12000 + id`, which `002F9860` resolves as bank 12, entry = the status id. The bank's slot `02EC3DE0` is written by exactly one body, `002F7800`, which hard-codes `0xC` and forwards `&02F973C0[12]` through `00238640` to a single loader entry; `002F7800` has no direct call site and no aligned qword pointer to it in the image, so the contents are a loader and data question. The earlier *12000..12031 are the clan ranks* reading was of a flat pool, not this one. | ANSWERED |
| GE-2 | **Whether the 32-bit record-pointer arithmetic can ever truncate.** `0031E27E`–`0031E286` builds the status row pointer as `movzx esi` / `imul esi` / `add esi, eax` over `ImageAddress_ResolveRuntimePointer`'s 64-bit return, so `rsi` is the zero-extended low 32 bits of `stride × index + base`; `0031C7B5` does the same on the sibling table. Correct only while the resolved base is below 4 GiB — the shape `EO-3` tracks elsewhere. Nothing observes it going wrong and no defect is claimed. **ANSWERED 2026-09-23 (SWE2-CONTRACT): yes, in exactly one window — the carry out of `add esi, eax` is dropped, so truncation needs `low32(rowbase) + 40 × idx ≥ 2³²`; with the shipped stride 40 and 32 rows that is a resolved base in the top ~1.2 KiB under 4 GiB, or above it.** Whether the arena ever lands there is the `J-C` live read of `01F83530`; the design assumes sub-4 GiB backing (the arena's own links are 32-bit, FABLE's `CD-2`/`J-C` finding), so the window is a configuration the arena cannot address either. Nothing shipped observes it. Static. | ANSWERED |
| GE-3 | **What `[rsi + 0x0A]` reads when the registry slot is missing.** `0031E259` and `0031E266` both branch to the read at `0031E288` itself when `02EBF118` is null or the resolve fails, so the pointer build is skipped and `rsi` carries whatever it already held. Whether either branch is reachable in a shipped run is not established. ~~**ANSWERED 2026-09-23 (SWE2-CONTRACT): `rsi` is `0`, not whatever it held — `0031C5EC` clears it in `0031C5D0`'s prologue and no dispatch path writes it before an arm runs, so `0031E288` reads `word [0x0A]` — the null page, a guaranteed fault, not a graceful fallback.** Reachable only before `003847B0` (a 3-instruction shim to `003845F0`, master field `+0x40`) installs `02EBF118`; afterward `desc+0x0C` is a shipped nonzero offset and `0020E600` cannot return 0, so both branches are dead in normal play. A pre-install class-26 query faults rather than mis-resolves. Static.~~ | **ANSWERED 2026-09-25 (FABLE, Claude Opus 5.5), ruling on OPUS's contradiction: nothing - with the slot missing, `0031E288` is never reached.** (1) The arm is entered only after `BattleEncodedId_IsValidForClass` (`0031E13F`–`0031E146`). OPUS's no-stub replay (`candidates/ge3-opus-replay-missing-slot/`, `59dfb5f1a`) shows it refusing a pre-install class-26 query: `0031E14C` is never reached, and the query returns cleanly. (2) With the validator bypassed, the first fault is earlier. A null slot jumps `0031E156` → `0031E222`, and a failed resolve goes `0031E167` → `0031E18B` → `0031E1A9`. Both set the record pointer `rbp = rsi`, and `0031E22C movzx eax, byte [rbp + 0x10]` faults before `0031E24F`. (3) `rsi` is **0** (`0031C5EC` clears it in `0031C5D0`'s prologue) - SWE2-CONTRACT's finding, credited. After the install by `003847B0` both branches are dead in normal play. *History: an unpublished SWE2-CONTRACT cell of 2026-09-23 said a pre-install query reaches `0031E288` and faults reading `word [0x0A]`; that mechanism clause is ruled wrong above.* |

## GH. The UI request router contract's open questions — FABLE, 2026-09-21

Owned by [CONTRACT-ui-request-router.md](../16-UI/CONTRACT-ui-request-router.md) §8. Registered with
the contract in the same commit. The unnamed request ids are **not** re-registered here: they are
`UQ-162` on the owning page, and they are an identity question, not a mechanism one. Prefix checked
free with `next_question_id.py --check GH` immediately before assignment.

| ID | Question | Status |
|---|---|---|
| GH-1 | **What `003F4E70` does with the request latch `02092734`.** The latch has exactly three readers image-wide: the router `00254B50` at `00254B71`, which refuses everything while it is 1; the input arbiter `00253C70` at `00253FE3`; and `003F4E70`, which was not read. Since invariant `R-4` is the claim that this one dword closes the router and the arbiter together, the third reader is the one body that could widen or qualify it. **ANSWERED 2026-09-23 (SWE2-CONTRACT): it mirrors the latch, it does not gate on it — R-4 stands.** `003F4E70` is a message handler (ids 1, 2, `0x10`, `0x11`); on id 1 (the mount message) it writes `win+0xF4 = [02092730]` (the request id, R-3) and copies the latch into `win+0xF8` bit 0 via `(flags ^ latch) & 1 ^ flags` at `003F4FD7`–`003F4FE2`. The id-`0x11` arm later re-issues `00252B40(+0xF4, +0xF8 & 1)`. It never writes or branches on `02092734` — a snapshot for the window's own bookkeeping, not a qualifier. Static. | ANSWERED |
| GH-2 | **Why `002E15D0` and `002E1AE0` write the mailbox cells.** The image-wide sweep of `0215F1A0`..`0215F1AC` gives the id and parameter cells five writers: the post `002E1B10`, the script path `002E1A60`, the request-12 path `002E1AE0`, the drain `002E09A0` and `002E15D0`. The first four are accounted for; `002E15D0` is not, and whether it is a third producer or a second reset decides whether the producer census on [the router page](../16-UI/Request-Router/ui-request-router.md) §2 is complete. **ANSWERED 2026-09-23 (SWE2-CONTRACT): `002E15D0` is a second reset — the producer census is complete.** A 28-byte leaf zeroing all four cells unconditionally (`0215F1A0` pending, `0215F1A1` blocked, `0215F1A4` id, `0215F1A8` param). Two callers, both teardown: `0026A5F0` (manager-slot unload — the `002E15D0`/`002E1690` pair the field-runtime-pass contract documents per slot) and `0026DB30` `WorldPersistence_ResetBanksForFieldTransition`. `002E1AE0` stays as accounted (request-12 path via `0034DA80`). Static. | ANSWERED |

## GJ. The glyph-run drawing context and the text-element dispatch table — FABLE, 2026-09-21

Registered on `AUDITSPEC-REQ-FABLE-REGISTER-71-OPEN-ITEMS`, which found 71 open §7 items with no
registry presence. These eleven are the two `99-Unresolved-Residual/Glyph-Run-Rendering/` pages'
share: both carry `status: PARTIAL`, both state their open items clearly, and **neither page nor any
of its items appears in this file under any id** — so they were invisible to package selection
rather than unasked. The wording below is the pages' own, tightened; nothing here is new work.
Prefix checked free with `next_question_id.py --check GJ` immediately before assignment.

| ID | Question | Status |
|---|---|---|
| GJ-1 | **What the shared drawing context object is for.** ~~Its lifecycle, size and field map are read; nothing in the image names it.~~ **ANSWERED IN SUBSTANCE 2026-09-21 (FABLE), §3a of the owning page: it is PARALLEL INDEXED QWORD TABLES with the control block at the end, not a control block behind 4 KB of padding.** The head is reached neither by fixed displacement nor by its own address - a whole-image sweep of `0209D490`-`0209E598` finds ONE reference, the initialiser's `lea` - but 25 functions load the pointer and **seven access it as a base with a runtime index, all at scale 8**, with a second array based at **`+0x400`**. That table's rows are **24 bytes** (`lea rdx,[rcx+rcx*2]` then `[ctx+rdx*8+0x400]`) and its selector is **the position of a CONTROL CODE** in the 106-entry table at `01DF1030`, returned by `00197790` through `InputManager_GetSingleton` - **and `-1` unless the developer-console byte `[console+0xC3D]` is set**, which is why the cluster is residual. Still open: the record's remaining fields, and `GJ-2`. | **ANSWERED** |
| GJ-2 | **What the three pointer slots at `+0x1060`, `+0x1078` and `+0x1090` point to.** ~~Each is read by one function and written by none of the functions examined.~~ **ANSWERED 2026-09-21 (FABLE), §3c of the owning page: each holds the base of its own QWORD ARRAY.** All three are read by one body, `002B5C90`, in four identical instructions - load the slot as a pointer, take a runtime index from the caller's frame, `mov rbx,[ptr+idx*8]`, then read the same `+0xA` int16 the `+0x400` control-code path reads - so they are three parallel arrays selected **by code path**, each preceded by the same `001E0BD0`→`001E0DA0` lookup with a `-1` guard. **A near-miss worth keeping:** all three sit at exact 24-byte boundaries from `+0x400` (rows 132/133/134) and at none from `+0x000`, which is a discriminating test and is *wrong* - reading the sites overturned it. **Residue, narrower than the question:** who WRITES the three slots is still unanswered; the whole-extent sweep rules out an address-taken write and `002432B0` writes the other table. | **ANSWERED** |
| GJ-3 | **Whether the drawing context is ever passed to another function at all.** The corrected census finds no argument-passing site but under-reports by construction (§5 of the owning page), so this is open rather than answered in the negative. **ANSWERED 2026-09-21 (FABLE), §5a: IT IS NEVER PASSED — and the liveness census was the wrong instrument, not merely a weak one.** Asked at the other end, no liveness is involved: a function that **dereferences the context without ever loading `0209CC40` must have been handed it**. Sweeping nine offsets already tied to this object gives 33 functions, **26 loaders and 14 candidate receivers** — and all fourteen fall, **six by ACCESS WIDTH** (`001CCB20` writes `+0x10D8` as a *word*, `001CD0E0` and two others read `+0x10D4` or `+0x10D8` as a *byte*, `00792350` as a *qword*, where the context's are dwords — a different structure at the same displacement) and **eight because no caller of theirs loads the pointer**. The two instruments fail in opposite directions, which is what makes the negative worth stating: a pass the liveness walk misses would still show at the callee here. Also tightened: **26 loader functions over 121 sites** — the page's own 121 reference sites, now attributed — **all between `002A9F00` and `002B5C90`**, so the object is never reached from outside its own cluster. *Bounded by: a receiver touching only offsets below `+0x10C8`.* | **ANSWERED** |
| GJ-4 | **Whether `+0x10FC` is one dword or overlapping fields.** **ANSWERED 2026-09-21 (FABLE), §3e of the owning page: it is a BYTE**, and a three-state one (`cmp byte [.],2` then set 1 or 2, 0 on release paths). Every access image-wide is byte-sized except one dword and one word store in `002B24B0`, and those are **a bulk clear of the contiguous region `+0x10EC`..`+0x1101`** - the qword/dword/word split a compiler emits to zero a struct span. **The same function proves it**: it saves `+0x10FC` and `+0x10FF` as BYTES at `002B257D`/`002B258B`, overwrites them inside the wider store, and restores them as BYTES at `002B279F`/`002B27B7`. Also settled on the way: `002B24B0` is a save/reset/restore wrapper preserving five fields plus the render-buffer record across a nested draw, so the control block is **scoped, not global**. | **ANSWERED** |
| GJ-5 | **What `[0209CC48]` is**, cleared beside every column-1 dispatch. **ANSWERED 2026-09-21 (FABLE), §3d of the owning page: a pointer to the CURRENT 24-BYTE RENDER-BUFFER RECORD** in the table at `02EBEFC0`, selected by the index at `02EBEFF0`, with `0209CC50` the 16-byte write cursor into that record's buffer (`[rec+8]`, mirrored at `0209E5A0`). `002B4730` sets all three immediately after `RenderCommand_SubmitCurrentBufferAndSwap`, so the "clear" is a **cursor reset on a buffer swap**, not a flag clear. The stride, the `bts` of bit 28 and constants like `0x6C008150` are GS qwords with GIF-shaped tags. **Also joins two neighbourhoods:** that record table runs up to `02EBF000`, the float the authored-data table registry uses to fix its array's lower bound. | **ANSWERED** |
| GJ-6 | **What the initialiser's conditional float at `01E0CE0C` scales.** **ANSWERED 2026-09-21 (FABLE), §3f of the owning page: NOTHING, and on shipped data it is not even computed.** The cell has ONE writer - the initialiser - and **zero readers image-wide**. And the branch that writes it is `if (00254A10() == 0)`, where `00254A10` reads `[01E02814]` (**ships as 0x0A**) and tests it against the mask `0xD81`, whose bits are 0, 7, 8, 10, 11 - bit 10 is set, so the predicate returns **1** and the arm is not taken. For completeness the value would have been **4.0**: `0024ABC0` is `(float)[01E0C1D8] * 0.001953125` with `[01E0C1D8]` shipping as 512, giving exactly 1.0, times `[01CEBC70] = 4.0`. A double negative, both halves measured. | **ANSWERED** |
| GJ-7 | **Which text each of the four font drawers is responsible for.** `PROPOSED-repos9e-6` stands; §6 of [the text-element dispatch table](../99-Unresolved-Residual/Glyph-Run-Rendering/the-text-element-dispatch-table.md) narrows `002AC5F0`'s entry points but does not name its output. **NARROWED 2026-09-21 (FABLE), §6c — and one of the four is not a drawer.** The table as bytes: kinds 0 and 1 share columns 0 and 1, **kind 2's row is entirely null**, kind 3 has only column 2 — five filled slots, four bodies, and the dispatchers `test rax, rax` for exactly that. `002AC5F0` is **the control-code engine above the emitters, not a peer**: 1,658 instructions against 329–511, 44 callees, the whole `003FFAxx` family (19 calls to `003FFAB0` alone), and it **calls `002A9F00` four times**. `002AA800` and `002AAE40` have **zero direct call sites in the image** — table-only — while `002A9F00` has **eight in three functions**, so it is the shared emitter and the other two are the kind-specific ones; the one structural difference is that `002AA800` alone does not call `002AC5F0`. Also found: `002B0280` writes `0x7D00` to the context's `+0x10DC` immediately before each of its three calls to `002A9F00` — the `GJ-10` reveal's deliberate opt-out. **Still open**, and now dependent on `GJ-8` rather than on reading more of these bodies: which text each kind carries. **Narrowed again 2026-09-25 (FABLE, Claude Opus 5.5):** with `GJ-8`'s kinds (SWE2-CONTRACT), the drawers map as follows. `002AAE40` draws the message-window runs (kind 3). `002A9F00` draws the full-pipeline elements (kind 0). `002AA800` is the uninstantiated kind 1. `002AC5F0` is the control-code engine above them. **Kind 2 is stamped on the game's byte-charset text**: `002B3400`, which stamps it, is on the not-`ex` arm at the three `ex`-test sites where it appears, and `ex` strings are UTF-16 (UQ-361). At one site `002B0280`, the byte-charset renderer, draws it outside the table. At the other two, `002DD680` follows, and that body is not read. Still open: which on-screen strings become kind 0 and which kind 1. **ANSWERED the same day (FABLE, Claude Opus 5.5), by builder:** - kind 0 (`002A9F00`) is the message window's page text. It is built by `002B3C30` / `002B3D50` from the text-slice copy `002A1B00`, the window-open reconfigure `002A3250`, and the constructor wrapper `002B32C0`, whose only callers are message-window functions; a second wrapper adds five sites elsewhere. - kind 3 (`002AAE40`) is the message window's run elements. - kind 2 (the null row) is screen label text, 21 `002B3400` sites in 19 functions, on the byte-charset path. - kind 1 (`002AA800`) has no builder. | ANSWERED 2026-09-25 — each drawer's text named by its builders ~~PARTIAL — drawers mapped to kinds~~ |
| GJ-8 | **What `obj[0xA3]`'s four kinds are.** The selector's domain is four rows wide; nothing read there names any of them. **NARROWED 2026-09-22 (FABLE): the domain is bounded by what is authored, not by the table's width.** `GJ-11`'s sweep shows that code owned by this cluster writes only **0, 2 and 3** — **no cluster-side site writes `1`**, the same shape `GJ-9` found at `+0xAC`. The one writer of `1` (`007E7401`) is `Audio`-owned and is a different structure at the same offset. **The kinds still need naming**, but only three of the four rows are reachable from the owning structure's own code. **ANSWERED 2026-09-23 (SWE2-CONTRACT), page §8b — the kinds are emit-pipeline identities:** kind 3 = the message-window run (`002A4830`, sole caller inside `002A6190`; emitter `002AAE40` calls `002AC5F0`); kind 2 = the handler-less element (`002B3400`, 19 callers; null row — dispatches nothing, and `002AFCB1` on it would call a null); kind 0 = the full-pipeline element (`002B3C30`/`002B3D50`; emitter `002A9F00` cooperates with `002AC5F0`); kind 1 = the control-code-free sibling (`002AA800` never calls `002AC5F0`) no cluster-side code instantiates. Residuals: no designer-facing names exist in the image; kind 1's instantiation path unfound. [the text-element dispatch table](../99-Unresolved-Residual/Glyph-Run-Rendering/the-text-element-dispatch-table.md) | ANSWERED |
| GJ-9 | **What `obj[0xAC]` and the global `01E0CDC8` gate** in the guarded dispatcher — the condition under which column 1 runs at all. **ANSWERED 2026-09-21 (FABLE), §4a of [the text-element dispatch table](../99-Unresolved-Residual/Glyph-Run-Rendering/the-text-element-dispatch-table.md): the two terms are not two enables, and only one of them is live.** `01E0CDC8` is **`1` at rest** (it ships as `1`) and has **two writes image-wide, both in `002A6190`**, inside the arm the 21-entry table at `002A698C` gives **message id 2** alone: it is set from `001EDEC0(window[+0xB4])` at `002A6464` and **put back to `1`** at `002A65D8` before the arm returns — a scoped latch, not an enable. `001EDEC0` resolves no record; it returns `1` unless the **60 fps `FrameLimit` TIME BASE** is in effect — `01F82E38`, written only by `001EDDC0` from `setting[18]`, which lies in `.data`'s **virtual tail with no raw bytes** and so initialises to **0** (*name corrected the same day: this row first said "2x render-scale mode"; `01DFE0B4` is the frame base, **1 at 30 fps and 2 at 60**, and the database had already named it in three places — the measurements stand, the label did not*) and the suppressor `01DFE0C0` is clear (it **ships as `1`**), in which case it returns `(~arg) & 1`. And `obj[0xAC]` is on the **embedded text-draw block, not the widget**: a byte-write sweep at `+0xAC` and at `+0x16C`/`+0x17C`/`+0x18C` — every base the nine callers use — plus the three stack frames finds **no site in the image writing `1` to it**, and the block's initialiser `002B3400` does not write it. So column 1 runs **unconditionally for all five callers** outside one window's id-2 message. The same latch also gates three sites in `002A7720` and one in `002A8C50`. | **ANSWERED** |
| GJ-10 | **What `[0209CC40]` is** beyond being the cluster's shared context with 121 reference sites, and what `+0x10D8` means to the handlers that consume it. **ANSWERED 2026-09-21 (FABLE), §3g of the owning page: `+0x10D8`, `+0x10DC` and `+0x10E4` are the PROGRESSIVE TEXT REVEAL - the typewriter.** `002AF960` seeds all three from the text-draw block in five instructions (`+0x10D8` and `+0x10DC` from its words `+0x8C` and `+0x90`, `+0x10E4` from `(s8)+0x9D * float +0x50`), and `002A9F00` **decrements both counters once per glyph** at `002AA0B1`. `+0x10DC` is the **test**: while it is positive the glyph draws at its own alpha, and once it is not, the alpha is multiplied by `+0x10E4` - which **steps down by a fixed amount per glyph** (`002AA07D`) - and clamped to `[0, 128]` (`002AE0F8`..`002AE100`, and identically at `002AE27E`). `+0x10D8` is never tested: it is converted to float and **divided by a per-call total** at `002AD68C`, a progress fraction that scales a geometric quantity. `002AE610` **refunds one unit to both** immediately before the emit call unless flag `0x400` is set, so an inserted number's digits are not charged to the reveal. The three are saved and restored together by `002B24B0`, `002B2970` and the argument-insertion control code **because they are one state**. `+0x8C` defaults to `0x7D00` (32,000), which is why the effect is invisible at rest. *Not settled: `+0x90`'s default, and who authors `+0x9D` and `+0x50`.* | **ANSWERED** |
| GJ-11 | **Which code sets each kind.** Ten byte-writes to `+0xA3` exist image-wide; the four in this cluster are identified and the rest are not. **ANSWERED 2026-09-22 (FABLE): `+0xA3` is not one field, so “which code sets each kind” has no single answer.** An image-wide byte-displacement sweep (two arms, planted control `002B3470` PRESENT) finds **14 writes and 20 reads**; that reconciles with the page's ten exactly — four are read-modify-write **bit** operations (`or …,1`; `and …,0xFE`), so 10 plain + 4 bitwise = 14. The **13 writer bodies span five owner domains** by the ledger's own ownership data: `UI.Text.ControlCodeHandler` (writes **3**), the cluster neighbourhood (**2**, **0**, **0**), `Presentation` (the four bitwise ones), `Audio` (the writer of **1**), third-party `Rendering.PPFX`, and two `BitfieldStateAlgorithm` bodies. **The PPFX case needs no locality argument — third-party middleware cannot own this game's text element** — and the `Presentation` group treats the byte as **bit 0**, which is not how a `0..3` selector is written (`and 0xFE` would turn kind 3 into kind 2). So §7's refusal to assume the Audio writer was the same structure is confirmed, now with an owner label rather than an address range. *A discriminator that FAILED is recorded on the page:* “does the writer reach the cluster context `0209CC40`?” failed its control, because the block's own initialiser `002B3400` never references that global. [the text-element dispatch table](../99-Unresolved-Residual/Glyph-Run-Rendering/the-text-element-dispatch-table.md) | **ANSWERED 2026-09-22 (FABLE)** |

## GI. The 13 DD-family pages' prose residue, registered for owner verdict — SWE2-FRONTIER, 2026-09-29

The status-currency ruling (FABLE `b27e23f80`, ACCEPT from SWE2-AUDIT-SPEC and SWE2-AUDIT-SEM) lets a page read
DOCUMENTED only when the owner confirms filled sections, tier-cited claims and **no unregistered prose residue**.
`documented_rule.py` marked these 13 SWE2-FRONTIER pages READY (no open box, no live id), but the owner read found
each page still owns residue stated only in prose / on the status line. Per the register's pass-29 rule every open
question must carry an id, so the residue is registered here — each page keeps `PARTIAL` and its status line now
names its GI id, which makes the residue routable to producer lanes.

| GI-1 | Which value of the gambit row's `+0x14` bit 0 selects condition art and which selects action art, and which art type `00566C10`'s icon set is ([the-gambit-screens.md](../16-UI/Gambit-Screens/the-gambit-screens.md) "Not yet established"). | **ANSWERED 2026-09-29 (FABLE, Claude Opus 5.5)** — the premise does not hold: `+0x14` bit 0 is not a condition/action selector and `00566C10` draws no condition or action icon. `00566C10` is the marker of a tab strip (two pulsing page arrows plus, when bit 0 is set, one fixed pointer sprite that slides to the selected tab); `+0x14` is its own create record, set to 1 by the gambit pick list's strip installer `0056C170` (`0056C304`) and 0 by the shop strip's `00567200` (`00567438`), so bit 0 means "has a sliding pointer" for condition and action pickers alike. Condition versus action is the pick list's `+0x588` (1 target conditions, 2 actions): `0056ADA0` builds the tabs with `0056B100` (target grid `0208D310`, menu kind `0x23`, tab frame 0) or `0056AE80` (action grid `0208D300`, kind `0x22`, tab frame 1), so condition art is tab frame 0 and action art frame 1 (2/3 when a page is empty). The page's member rows for `0056AE80`/`0056B100` were swapped and its list/editor tree inverted; both corrected. The byte kernel `00432300` (23 sites in 8 bodies, incl. both emit paths) is the PS2 colour modulate `min(255, e*c >> 7)` against the draw-param `+0x40` colour's first dword; `0x80808080` is the exact identity (47 % of shipped entries). The two-mesh path `00434CD0` blends with `00433830` — `round(cur*(1-w) + next*w)` — when `+0x1F1` bit 4 is clear. Per pass the three draw paths re-colour (flat broadcast when `param+0x1A8+p` set, else per-corner modulate by `param+0x138+4p`; `00432CC0` sets `alpha = trunc(alpha*L[n].w) mod 256` over the lit per-normal table) and the builders emit the colour as `float(byte)` lanes 0..255 and the UV as GS STQ divided back by Q. (a) **Another body is in the way:** the gather (`00391D10`, or `003920F0` when ~~x is~~ any coordinate is NaN, C1) lists the actors within the leader's radius (`ActorRuntime_GetClass3FloatPair` `00265090`), and any one of them other than the leader whose movement body would pair with the leader's in the separation pass (`00314EB0`: equal layer `+6`, owner `+0x119` zero or different; [the movement body](../06-Movement-And-Navigation/the-movement-body-pool-and-the-separation-pass.md)) refuses. The relation query `00313F80` that follows does not change the answer: both of its counters refuse (`0033798D`-`0033799C`). A unit whose `+0xE68` class is 1 is skipped when the leader's is 4, and the actor check is skipped when `002EA7F0` refuses the leader (the actor tested is `rbp`, resolved from unit `+0xEA9` through GTAB / MABE *(Corrected 2026-10-02, FABLE, on SWE2-AUDIT-SEM's review [`auditsem-review-gr19-gr11-0930`](candidates/auditsem-review-gr19-gr11-0930/REVIEW.md) C3)*). (b) **The ground refuses the point** (`00337700`): the corridor family's `LQUERY` (`00391410`) must hit nothing at the point, `00384130` must map its X/Z to a grid cell (not `0xFF`, off-map), and `00336390` must pass the point and the four corners of a square of half-width max(radius A, radius B) through the point query `0032A6A0` under the leader's `+0x1F4` mask ([the corridor query family](../06-Movement-And-Navigation/CONTRACT-corridor-query-family.md)). ~~So a kill leaves no loot when the enemy dies where the leader could not stand: in another colliding body's reach, inside static geometry, off the map grid or off walkable ground.~~ *(Narrowed 2026-10-01, OPUS for SWE2-DATA, on SWE2-AUDIT-SEM's C2, [review](candidates/auditsem-review-gr19-gr11-0930/REVIEW.md):)* So a kill leaves no loot when the enemy dies where the leader could not stand: another actor in the leader's movement-body layer within the leader's radius (the separation pass's pairing rule, not a contact test), a hit in `LQUERY` (`00391410`) at the point, a point off the navigation grid, or a refusal from the point query `0032A6A0` at the point or a corner; what the two queries test is not named, and how the defeated unit's own body is kept out of the gather is not read. The gather's filter word `0x1C` and the `+0x1F4` mask are not named. *Was:* **OPEN 2026-09-30 (FABLE), static:** read the shared placement test `003377C0` (DE-4's validator) with its callees `00314EB0`, `00313F80` and `00337700` (and the two gather queries) and state the condition in game terms |
